title: Fates of Exact Finite-N First-Order Transitions: Coherent Suppression versus Spectral-Collapse Termination
authors: Jiong Li, Li-Wei Duan et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Symmetry-protected ground-state crossings can produce exact first-order transitions (FOTs) even at finite N, in contrast to continuous transitions governed by soft-mode criticality.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We establish exact Juddian ground-state crossings for arbitrary finite N in the one- and two-photon anisotropic Dicke models and identify a common two-channel structure: the eigenvalues of the coupling matrix set the local normal-state instability thresholds, whereas its determinant fixes the exact crossing. Despite this common structure, the resulting FOTs have distinct fates determined by the bosonic response.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the one-photon model, the overlap between coherent Juddian branches vanishes in the thermodynamic or infinite frequency-ratio limits, asymptotically suppressing the FOT cusp. In the two-photon model, squeezed Juddian states lose normalizability at spectral collapse, thereby terminating the physical FOT line at finite N.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Thus spectral collapse can terminate an exact finite-N FOT while preserving its collective imprint in the parity-resolved spectrum.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In such systems, computational organisation cannot be directly characterised from algorithms or internal representations. slides.hook: Aluminum nitride-based ferroelectrics combine high remanent polarization, thermal stability, weak size effects, a wide bandgap and back-end process compatibility, making them promising for high density non-volatile memory.

title: Methane and ethane adsorption on calcite surfaces: effects of surface morphology from molecular dynamics and 3D-RISM
authors: Felipe Silva Carvalho, Tyler Luchko et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Understanding the adsorption of alkanes on mineral surfaces is important for industrial processes such as oil and gas recovery from shale reservoirs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Previous studies have examined the adsorption of functionalized and non-functionalized alkanes on calcite, as well as adsorption under confinement. However, real surfaces commonly exhibit defects that can influence adsorption behavior.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the three-dimensional reference interaction site model (3D-RISM) are used to investigate the adsorption of methane and ethane on calcite surfaces with step defects. MD simulations were carried out with and without positional restraints to investigate the effects of carbonate reorientation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results highlight the importance of surface heterogeneity in fluid-mineral interactions and demonstrate that 3D-RISM is an efficient tool for semi-quantitative screening of adsorption across complex surface geometries.

title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
authors: Andrea Giuseppe Di Francesco, Rishabh Jain et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: G-Retriever combines graph soft prompts with a verbalized description of the same graph to strengthen the textual prompt signal. We conduct an in-depth analysis of G-Retriever and uncover a pathological behavior we term token collapse.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted models, G-Retriever's graph tokens become almost indistinguishable across inputs. We provide evidence that the same failure is inherited by subsequent methods, even with multi-token pooling.

title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
authors: Bastien Le Guellec, Su Hwan Kim et al. (4 researchers)

comments.author: Dr. David Sterling (Caltech)
comments.text: What are the thermodynamic boundaries of this configuration?

replies.author: Prof. Liam Henderson (CERN)
replies.text: The phase transition holds up to ~14.2 K before quantum coherence degrades.

slides.hook: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

title: Parallel Teleportation via AME(5,2) States on IBM Quantum Hardware
authors: Zheng Liang Lim & Hoi-Kwong Lo

slides.hook: The five-qubit Absolutely Maximally Entangled AME(5,2) state, whose every pair of qubits is maximally mixed so that all its information lives in non-local correlations, could in principle serve as a single shared quantum networking resource for teleporting two unknown qubits in parallel (each via its own Bell measurement and Pauli correction).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Nonetheless, its hardware implementations remain scarce despite its theoretical importance. Here, we demonstrate parallel teleportation based on a five-qubit absolutely maximally entangled state, AME(5,2), on the superconducting processor ibm_pittsburgh.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We construct three-qubit Clifford decoders that extract two Bell pairs using three logical two-qubit gates for each of 60 inequivalent sender-receiver assignments. Using parallelization and classical Pauli frame post-processing, we retain reference-receiver entanglement on both channels after three teleportation rounds.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish a hardware demonstration of two-channel entanglement transmission through repeated AME-assisted teleportation and provide compact decoding circuits for reconfigurable multipartite communication.

slides.hook: Diffusion trajectory planners with domain-specific experts face a practical question in unseen regions: can they rely on selecting among existing experts, or must the planner itself adapt? We study this question using a planner with a shared adapter and per-domain expert adapters.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Across three real-world held-out maps, none of eight test-time routing schemes improves the fleet-mean lateral offset over the static default, which uses the same expert for every scene. slides.content: In contrast, reward-based fine-tuning on just 20 target-region scenes yields substantially larger gains. On matched evaluation slices, joint replay achieves a fleet-mean offset of 6.9 m, compared with 12.4 m for the static default.

slides.content: These results show the limited headroom for selecting among existing experts and the greater open-loop gains available from adapting the planner.

authors: S. Wilhelmina, B. N. Jayawiguna et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: According to General Relativity (GR), gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although GR has been highly successful in describing gravitational phenomena, exotic compact objects with high mass and strong gravitational fields, as well as low-mass objects, have motivated the study of modified theories of gravity. slides.content: Overall, the f(R,T^2) gravity model can accommodate quark star configurations and reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects, particularly those associated with GW190814 and the lightest compact object observed, HESS J1731-347, respectively.

slides.hook: Networks of repeated neural modules with delayed neighbour coupling need stability guarantees for every number of modules, but delay-dependent criteria certify one network at a time and grow with its size.

title: Enhanced orbital-angular-momentum dimensionality and spatial-spectral decoupling in thin-film SPDC
authors: Dmitrii Akatev, Jakub Lewandowski et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Thin-film spontaneous parametric down-conversion, due to the relaxed phase-matching condition, generates photon pairs that are extremely broadband in frequency and angle and highly entangled in time/frequency and position/momentum.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we show that it also provides a very broad orbital angular momentum (OAM) spectrum, which, in contrast to the case of bulk crystals, is decoupled from the frequency spectrum. To demonstrate it experimentally, we generate photon pairs in a 7~μmathrm{m}-thick lithium niobate film and compare them with those from a 500~μmathrm{m}-thick periodically poled lithium niobate crystal under identical pump conditions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The thin-film source exhibits a substantially broader OAM spectrum, with the azimuthal Schmidt number almost 9 times larger than that of the bulk source. On this highly entangled state, we perform quantum-state tomography in selected two- and four-dimensional OAM subspaces, demonstrating high-purity maximally entangled states.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results highlight thin nonlinear films as a promising platform for high-dimensional quantum-state generation with weak spatial--spectral coupling.

title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
authors: Huiting Liu & Jinsong Wu

slides.hook: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We investigate this failure in an adaptive residual-routing decoder whose sequence-level routing summary exposes prefix positions to future tokens despite a correct causal attention mask. An anomalous 24-layer checkpoint reduces validation loss from the baseline's 3.5958 to 1.4259, yet it fails a prefix-invariance audit and has substantially higher reference-model perplexity during generation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Layer-wise diagnostics and implementation inspection trace the violation to a full-sequence summary broadcast through the dynamic routing-query path. Two independently trained 12-layer causal repairs eliminate detectable leakage and return validation loss and reference perplexity to the control scale, removing the large apparent advantage.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results illustrate how hidden future-token access can produce misleading claims of architectural progress and why lower teacher-forced loss should be interpreted together with whole-model causal checks and free-running evaluation.

title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
authors: Andrew J. Ochoa, Martin J. A. Schuetz et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.

title: Efficiently classifying shocks in complex systems requires dormant reporters
authors: David A. Brewster & Philippe Cluzel

slides.hook: Many natural and engineered systems are large complex networks of interacting components, and external perturbations drive them along different dynamical paths.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Identifying which perturbation occurred matters for diagnosis, control, and prediction. Yet often times only a few components can be jointly monitored.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

slides.hook: The scarcity of optically visible O stars near the theoretical zero-age main sequence (ZAMS) has puzzled astronomers for over four decades.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We argue that it reflects prolonged accretion. If massive stars assemble over Myr timescales, as the inertial-inflow model predicts, core-hydrogen burning begins before accretion ends, and the stars become optically visible at the end of accretion on a birthline displaced from the standard ZAMS.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We test this interpretation by comparing the hot-side envelope of Galactic O stars in the Kiel diagram with accreting stellar-evolution models, adopting a growth law t_{mathrm{form}}=τ_0(m_{mathrm{f}}/60 M_odot)^α with formation time t_{mathrm{form}} and final mass m_{mathrm{f}}. The resulting birthlines reproduce both the displacement and the high-mass turnover of the observed envelope, with best-fitting parameters (α,τ_0)=(0.52,4.3,mathrm{Myr}), consistent with independent constraints from the luminosity functions of compact H II regions and OB stars.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The inferred growth law agrees with cloud-scale simulations and the inertial-inflow model, and implies that mass assembly and main-sequence evolution overlap substantially in massive stars, with broader implications for stellar evolution and feedback.

slides.hook: Protein Language Models (PLMs) have made remarkable progress following scaling laws established in natural language processing across sequence- and structure-based tasks, yet the potential of tokenization remains underexploited.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Unlike human language, proteins preserve structure despite extensive sequence variation a property standard tokenization strategies fundamentally fail to capture. title: Orbital-coherence memory in electrical transport and its self-consistent Maxwell response
authors: Pengfei Zhu

slides.hook: An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force.

title: FidLIF: Parallel Training of High-Fidelity Spiking Neurons with Exact BPTT
authors: Kaixiang He & Yujie Wu

slides.hook: Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) show promise in energy-efficient computing through event-driven computation and stateful temporal processing, their recurrent membrane dynamics render their training inherently sequential and inefficient for long sequences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing methods achieve full-sequence parallelism in SNNs through two main strategies: redesigning or approximating spiking dynamics to avoid reset-coupled temporal dependencies, or relying on iterative relaxed fixed-point solvers that suffer from excessive memory costs and iteration-dependent backward overhead. To address these limitations, we present FidLIF, a novel framework that reconciles the incremental update and hard-reset behavior of standard spiking LIF neurons with parallel forward propagation and BPTT-equivalent backward propagation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: FidLIF iteratively recovers the full-sequence membrane-potential trajectory in parallel. By exploiting the lower bidiagonal structure induced by the local recurrence of LIF neurons, FidLIF formulates each forward trajectory correction and backward adjoint propagation as associative scans with an O(log T) temporal depth.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By reconciling parallel training with step-by-step execution, FidLIF enables high-fidelity spiking dynamics to benefit from parallel hardware without compromising incremental inference at deployment.

title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
authors: Fu Zheng, Wei Liu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.

title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
authors: Long Huang

slides.hook: We present an organizing framework for concatenated quantum error correction based on the observation that the syndrome projection of a stabilizer code reshapes the noise channel in a code-determined manner.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: For any stabilizer code, one level of QEC maps the physical noise to a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights are fixed by the code geometry. Coherences between different syndrome classes vanish, and no physical Pauli twirl is required to reach this block-diagonal form.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Concatenation can then be viewed as the iteration of the same redistribution step: the dominant logical error after one level selects the code used at the next. We instantiate the framework with the two smallest stabilizer codes, the bit-flip and phase-flip codes, and apply it to amplitude damping.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The scope of the framework, in particular for coherent and correlated noise, is stated explicitly.

title: Migrate Computation, Not Data: Fault Recovery in Neuromorphic Many-Core Systems
authors: Muyang Cao, Di Yu et al. (7 researchers)

comments.author: Dr. David Sterling (Caltech)

slides.hook: As neuromorphic systems scale to thousands of near-memory cores, aging-induced permanent faults in neuron-update datapaths become an important obstacle to long-term deployment.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing online recovery methods typically retire a faulty core and migrate its neurons, along with their weights and membrane states, to healthy cores. This whole-core treatment incurs high recovery traffic and makes recovery depend on scarce destinations; at high utilization, there may be enough surviving compute capacity but insufficient free storage to copy the affected neuron context.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This paper presents SpikeRelay, an online recovery framework for diagnosed compute-unit faults. SpikeRelay exploits the fact that, in many neuromorphic cores, the compute datapath, local SRAM, and router are distinct modules: a compute fault need not destroy stored weights and states or disconnect the core from the NoC.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Consequently, SpikeRelay sustains 100% recovery at 92.2% SRAM utilization and a 50% fault rate, whereas the best baseline achieves only 22.1%.

title: GenomeOcean Anywhere: Private WebGPU Inference for Genome MoEs
authors: Guang Yang & Fengchen Liu

comments.author: Dr. Julian Thorne (Cambridge)
comments.text: Could this interface handle real-time streaming latency under 20ms?

slides.hook: Genome foundation models are most useful where sequences are generated, yet the largest models need datacenter accelerators and a place to send private DNA.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We ask whether a 15-billion-parameter genome mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can instead run on volunteers' web browsers, with the experts spread across many untrusted devices, without changing its predictions and without revealing the sequence to any single device. We build a system in which a trusted coordinator runs attention and routing while browser workers run every expert feed-forward network through hand-written WebGPU kernels, and we protect the expert inputs with real-valued Lagrange coded computing: each worker receives only a Gaussian-padded share, computes the expert's linear maps, and the coordinator decodes from any two of three workers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On GenomeOcean-MoE (8 experts, top-2 routing, 24 layers), the browser path matches native llama.cpp at every quantization level, the distributed path stays at the BF16 numerical noise floor (KL 0.0036 nats per token), and an unfitted latency model predicts decode time within 0.74% (median) under emulated wide-area links. We first show that plaintext expert inputs are not private: a probe recovers the token from a single vector at every depth, and one worker can identify the source genome from 300 unordered tokens with 92% accuracy.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: With coded experts, an adaptive attacker trained on shares falls to the most-frequent-token baseline, one worker's information about each token is bounded below one bit per forward pass, and the fidelity cost stays below the BF16 noise floor; in Chrome, coded decoding runs at 220 to 376 ms per token, depending on how much of the routing is hidden, and continues without replicas when a worker fails.

title: Do Generative Priors Align with Human Naturalness Perception?
authors: Taiki Fukiage

slides.hook: Visual generative models are trained to capture the probability distributions of natural images, yet whether their native priors reflect the regularities governing human perception of image naturalness remains an open question.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we probe these priors through native prediction errors across 25 open image and video generators. Because raw single-image losses are dominated by scene content and visual complexity, we evaluate directional loss differences using content-preserving, paired relational interventions that selectively disrupt facial configurations or physical illumination consistency while limiting changes in low-level image statistics.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across both domains, these loss differences reproduce human-like selective sensitivities and tolerances, capturing the classic Thatcher effect on faces and shape-dependent responses to illumination inconsistencies. Notably, these loss differences reliably track continuous gradations of human naturalness judgments across individual stimulus pairs (peaking at r = .84 on faces and .64 on physical scenes) and retain unique human-aligned signals even after controlling for feature distances from frozen vision encoders and standard image quality metrics.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these findings demonstrate that learning visual distributions yields generative loss landscapes that capture distinct aspects of human naturalness perception.

title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
authors: Chaoyue Li, Zeyu Gao et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.

slides.hook: Reward models score responses for preference optimization, filtering and ranking, and pooling scores across prompts needs them to be comparable.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Yet pairwise evaluation compares two responses to the same prompt, so any score component shared by a prompt's responses cancels and goes untested. We study this component by comparing between-prompt variation in model scores with the same variation in human ratings of the same responses.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We propose a human-referenced audit, built from a between-prompt variance share, a sibling-rating regression and prompt substitutions, and apply it to eighteen released scorers and six matched training conditions. We find that scores cluster by prompt more than the ratings do: on HelpSteer2, six reward models have between-prompt shares of 0.34 to 0.64 against a human share near zero.

slides.hook: High-throughput drug screening relies on low-cost primary assays to prioritize compounds for more expensive dose-response profiling, where potency is ultimately quantified.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Current screening strategies largely focus on identifying compounds that will confirm biological activity on follow-up, implicitly assuming that confirmed activity will also yield a usable potency estimate. However, confirmed biological activity in screening does not necessarily translate into a quantifiable potency, because active compounds can still fail to produce a reportable dose-response estimate.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We therefore present a framework for modeling quantifiability, whether follow-up testing will yield a usable potency estimate, as a distinct triage objective from biological activity. Quantifiability was strongly predictable from the preceding low-cost screen, with most predictive information arising from the observed screening features rather than molecular structure.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings establish experimental measurability, distinct from biological activity, as a predictable property of screening outcomes and show that quantifiability-aware triage can improve the allocation of costly dose-response profiling capacity.

title: Prompt Jet Launching and Delayed Thermal Disk in Tidal Disruption Event for Prolonged Activity GRB 220706A
authors: Yuri Sato & Rin Oikawa

slides.hook: GRB 220706A exhibits X-ray flaring activity extending to ~51 days after the trigger, along with a luminous optical thermal component emerging on a timescale of ~10^6 s.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such prolonged central-engine activity could be powered by a collapsar fed by an extended stellar envelope. However, a relativistic jet may struggle to break out of the extended envelope.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: These challenges motivate a tidal disruption event (TDE), although explaining both the early relativistic jet and the luminous late optical thermal emission within one TDE framework remains difficult. We investigate a TDE scenario in which shocks between stellar debris streams drive the early inflow of some debris, potentially carrying preexisting fossil magnetic flux toward the black hole (BH) and powering an initial relativistic jet via the Blandford-Znajek mechanism.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Continued fallback may sustain central-engine activity beyond the observed X-ray flaring episode, making future X-ray monitoring a test of this scenario.

title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions
authors: Clemencia Siro & Laura Hollink

slides.hook: Metadata-conditioned generation is often framed as a data-to-text task in which additional input fields should improve grounding.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Museum description generation challenges this assumption because catalogue records are heterogeneous, partially visual, and unevenly documented across geographic regions. We study how metadata composition shapes the generation of artefact descriptions through a two-phase framework.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Phase 1 analyses natural metadata variation in a large museum collection, where field count, field type, image availability, and Place co-vary. Phase 2 introduces controlled field probes that hold object identity fixed while varying metadata quantity, field type, and image access.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: More broadly, our findings show that metadata-conditioned data-to-text evaluation should assess field- and claim-level support, rather than relying only on aggregate input coverage or reference similarity.

title: A Network-Structured Bayesian Hierarchical Model for Sparse Mutation-Drug Response Associations: Application to Cancer Pharmacogenomics
authors: Hammed A. Olayinka & Saheed O. Olayemi

slides.hook: We develop a network-structured Bayesian hierarchical model for sparse association mapping between genomic alterations and quantitative treatment-response phenotypes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The framework combines a Gaussian Markov random field prior that borrows strength across pathway-connected genes, a global-local horseshoe prior inducing sparsity, and a conjugate Gibbs sampler requiring no Metropolis-Hastings steps. Though broadly applicable to high-dimensional settings with known predictor networks, we validate it using cancer cell-line drug-sensitivity data.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Applied to GDSC2 (N=951 cell lines, G=219 driver genes, D=295 drugs), the model identifies 126 gene-drug associations (0.195% of 64{,}605 pairs), concentrated in EZH2 (45 drugs, all sensitivity-direction, mean effect -0.911 lnIC50) and KMT2D (36 drugs, all sensitivity-direction, mean effect -0.496 lnIC50). These markers show external support in an independent PRISM screen (1{,}518 compounds), with KMT2D achieving complete directional replication (36/36) and EZH2 partial replication (8/12).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show the framework identifies sparse, interpretable, externally supported drug-sensitivity markers while enabling principled investigation of tissue-specific departures from shared effects.

slides.hook: Solving high-dimensional structural model updating problems requires an algorithm capable of navigating complex, non-convex landscapes with correlated parameters.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing hybrid evolutionary algorithms typically rely on static architectures or fixed switching rules, resulting in disjointed search phases. To address this, this study proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning-governed dynamic DE-CMAES Orchestration (DRL-DCO) algorithm, in which a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)-based actor-critic agent continuously governs the evolutionary process as a single, unified system rather than a mechanical concatenation of algorithms.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Guided by a progression-aware state representation and a diversity-informed reward, the agent fluidly reallocates computational resources between the differencevector-based exploration of Differential Evolution (DE) and the covariance-guided exploitation of CMA-ES, while jointly regulating population size, elite preservation, and a restart mechanism to escape local optima. This allows DRL-DCO to autonomously transition between exploration-dominant, exploitation-dominant, and mixed-strategy regimes across generations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Validated on high-dimensional single-objective optimization benchmarks and the IASC-ASCE structural health monitoring benchmark, DRL-DCO achieves superior convergence accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art adaptive and hybrid evolutionary algorithms, as well as single-operator DRL-governed baselines.

title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. II. System-parameter uncertainties and overall errors
authors: Chia-Hsien Huang & Hsi-Sheng Goan

slides.hook: In the companion paper (Part I), we developed an optimal-control framework to suppress intrinsic and decoherence-induced errors in controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we extend this framework to incorporate uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and zero-flux qubit frequencies, enabling the design of high-fidelity gates robust against noise and parameter uncertainties. We classify these uncertainties by whether they perturb the off-diagonal coupling strengths or the diagonal detunings of the Hamiltonian, and we identify distinct suppression mechanisms for each class.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Coupling errors are mitigated through dynamical decoupling induced by strong detuning modulation. For a 30-ns gate, this strategy reduces the coupling error to 6.21times10^{-7} and tolerates coupling-strength uncertainties up to 2πtimes4 MHz while keeping total gate infidelity below 10^{-3}.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together with the companion study (Part I), this framework offers a practical approach to balance speed, fidelity, and robustness while reducing the need for exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Assay-Aware BindingDB: Curating Experimental Context for Binding Affinity Prediction
authors: Ming-Hsiu Wu, Xuejiao Shirley Guo et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Protein--ligand binding affinity prediction is fundamental to computational drug discovery, yet modern AI-driven models are limited by pervasive heterogeneity in their training data: bioactivity values are aggregated across diverse assay types and experimental conditions without accounting for protocol-level differences, introducing systematic noise.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing harmonization approaches either discard assay-level metadata or collapse it into coarse categorical distinctions, leaving rich contextual signal unused. We address this gap with two contributions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: First, we introduce Assay-Aware BindingDB, augmenting 74,425 BindingDB protein--ligand pairs across four assay types (ITC, SPR, RBA, and FPA) with structured metadata extracted from primary literature using a two-stage agentic framework that separates evidence extraction from ontology-conditioned JSON synthesis. Against domain-expert references, the framework achieves presence F1 geq 0.947 and semantic content accuracy geq 0.913 across all assay types.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results support the hypothesis that systematically curated assay metadata provides informative signal for affinity prediction.

slides.hook: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

slides.content: To isolate L1-specific transfer, we compare bilingual models trained on an L1 that matches the readers' L1 background to both a monolingual English baseline and bilingual models trained on other L1s. We demonstrate that matching the readers' L1 improves the prediction of L2 reading times.

slides.hook: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution.

slides.content: Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. slides.hook: emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure.

title: A Spiking Ring-Attractor Architecture for Representation and Control of Revolute Robot Joints
authors: Aung Htet, Alejandro Rodriguez Jimenez et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Robotic systems with revolute joints evolve on circular state spaces, yet most control architectures represent these states using Euclidean variables that ignore this underlying geometry.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We propose a fully spiking neural control architecture in which ring attractors encode joint states, enforcing representations consistent with the topology of revolute systems. Homeostatic regulation computes goal-state mismatch directly over these distributed representations, and opponent gain-modulated populations convert this mismatch into controlled phase shifts of the activity bump, implementing set-point regulation as motion on the ring.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that the bump dynamics follow an SO(2) geometry, and that gain asymmetries induce a signed phase velocity on the ring. To interface distributed activity with scalar regulation signals, we derive an analytic Fourier phase decoder and implement its signed components using push-pull spiking populations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results establish a neuromorphic control framework in which representation, regulation, and action are unified within a ring-attractor substrate aligned with the geometry of revolute systems.

title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
authors: Andrea Blasi Núñez, Gianluca Barmina et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond the setting they were trained for.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we study this question for NLAs along four closely related questions: (i) Do NLA verbalizations exhibit compositional structure with respect to their input? (ii) Do NLAs generalize to finetuned versions of the model they were trained for? (iii) Can NLAs recover finetuning objectives in model diffing? (iv) Can NLAs be specialized for model diffing? Across four models from three families, our experiments provide evidence supporting a largely positive answer to all four questions. Specifically, verbalizations of composed analogy activations mostly name the target while rarely mentioning the subtracted word, and an NLA can be reused on lightweight finetunes of its original model without retraining, with reconstruction quality degrading noticeably only for the largest model.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our findings suggest that NLAs can meaningfully verbalize differences in activation space, rendering NLAs a promising direction for future work.

title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
authors: Juan C. Zapata, Emilio De Biasi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

title: Simulation-based inference of profile evolution for high-precision pulsar timing
authors: Sai C. Susarla, Gregory Ashton et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Pulsars are exceptional cosmic laboratories, the most stable of which rival atomic clocks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Nearly all of that precision rests on one observable, the average pulse profile unique to each pulsar and stable over decades. These profiles change shape systematically with observing frequency, reflecting the physics of the emitting pulsar beam, but if left unmodelled, it can bias the arrival-time measurements, undermining precision timing.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Profile-domain timing has been proposed to address this effect, but current implementations use stochastic sampling, which is computationally prohibitive and has limited the application in large-scale analyses. Here, we present a simulation-based inference approach to profile-domain timing, using a normalising flow conditioned on a convolutional embedding of the frequency-phase portrait.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Fundamental properties like non-Gaussian noise, pulsar self-noise, jitter, scattering, and profile change can be inferred by simulating them rather than by deriving a new likelihood for each, opening a promising pathway to include machine learning methods into pulsar timing workflows.

slides.hook: Leveraging the high-precision photometric redshifts of the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS), we aim to investigate the connection between active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and galaxy pairs up to redshifts of sim1.0.

slides.content: We identified 16,824 galaxy pairs with projected separations of r_p < 100 kpc and radial-velocity differences of ΔV < 3500 km s^{-1}. slides.content: The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. title: Uncertainty-aware integration of deuterium metabolic imaging with genome-scale metabolic modeling reveals diet-associated feasible-space remodeling in mouse skeletal muscle
authors: Tin Yau Pang, Samia Maouhoub et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Deuterium metabolic imaging (DMI) measures glucose-derived labeling in vivo, but noisy time courses complicate network-level interpretation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We developed an uncertainty-aware workflow that integrates dynamic DMI data with genome-scale metabolic modeling (GEM) through soft flux constraints. After injection of [6,6'-2H2]glucose, dynamic spectra were acquired from gastrocnemius, soleus, and tibialis anterior muscles of control and high-fat diet (HFD) mice.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A hierarchical four-state kinetic model estimated labeling parameters while accounting for shared plasma input, tissue-specific kinetics, voxel-level fluxes, isotope effects, and measurement uncertainty. Because glucose labeling was more reliable than lactate and glutamate/glutamine signals, only two DMI-derived quantities were used as GEM anchors: glucose processing mapped to hexokinase flux, and glucose-derived oxidative entry mapped to mitochondrial pyruvate dehydrogenase flux.

title: A Time-Variant Spiking Neuron from a Unified State-Dynamics Perspective
authors: Jing Yang, Qianhui Liu et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) have increasingly incorporated rich neuronal dynamics to enhance temporal processing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, richer dynamics do not necessarily enable neurons to adapt how information is processed over time. To examine this issue systematically, we introduce a unified state-dynamics framework that characterizes diverse spiking neurons through a common formulation and enables direct comparison of their dynamical designs.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The framework reveals a common limitation of existing neurons: although they enhance temporal processing through richer internal states and state evolution, the dynamical rules determining how inputs are integrated, how states evolve, and how they are read out generally remain unchanged throughout temporal processing. Such time-invariant rules limit the ability of neurons to adjust information processing as information relevance changes over time.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Extensive experiments show that TV-MCN achieves strong overall performance, with particularly large gains on tasks requiring selective retention and retrieval of information, while ablation studies further support the effectiveness of its time-varying mechanisms.

title: Simulated Control Evals
authors: Jeffrey Olmo, David Zhang et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Control evaluations measure whether safeguards can prevent an AI model from causing undesired outcomes even when it is intentionally trying to do so.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These evaluations typically use purpose-built control settings and extrapolate their results to a model's deployment. However, the effectiveness of safeguards in deployment can depend on features of environments and tasks that control settings do not represent.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To broaden where control evaluations can be run, we introduce simulated control evaluations (SCEs), which use a language model to simulate tool responses in place of an environment. We evaluate SCEs on LinuxArena, where execution provides ground-truth outcomes.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results suggest that deployment-specific SCEs can be more predictive than control evaluations executed in separate control settings.

title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
authors: Chenghong Huang, Yuta Fujihashi et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.

title: Revisiting Distribution Matching for State-to-Vision Policy Distillation in Laparoscopic Robotic Manipulation
authors: Mingyu Sheng, Jianan Fan et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: End-to-end control policies trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) have emerged as an alternative to conventional surgical robotic control approaches, with recent studies exploring state-based policies trained on privileged state observations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, such approaches rely on precise physical states that are difficult to obtain reliably in surgical environments. Vision-based RL provides an alternative by learning manipulation policies directly from RGB observations, avoiding explicit state estimation and manually engineered perception pipelines while enabling policies to acquire task-relevant visual representations.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Nevertheless, obtaining vision-based policies via pure RL methods for surgical manipulation remains challenging. Thus, imitation learning (IL) becomes another solution, yet it requires a large number of expert demonstrations, which are difficult to obtain in minimally invasive surgery.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Experimental results show that, in the context of laparoscopic robotic manipulation, training vision-based policies with general-purpose RL methods is challenging, whereas our proposed state-to-vision policy distillation leads to more consistent and stable performance across tasks.

title: Predicting directional flexibility in proteins
authors: Vsevolod Viliuga, Leif Seute et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Predicting protein dynamics is a long-standing problem in computational structural biology.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Often, protein function critically depends on local directed motions, such as hinge movements, catalytic loop rearrangements and domain reorientations, which can be characterized by directional flexibility and correlated structural motions of the protein backbone. While Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations provide an established but often prohibitively expensive approach, recent deep generative models aim to reduce this cost by directly predicting conformational ensembles, emulating MD.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: However, due to their large size and the need to generate several states until the derived dynamical properties converge, these models remain expensive. In this work, we propose BackFlip-2: a fast SE(3)-equivariant graph neural network trained to directly predict dynamical descriptors, such as directional backbone flexibility and pairwise dynamic correlations, from an equilibrium structure.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: BackFlip-2 model weights, training and inference code are available at https://github.com/graeter-group/backflip.

title: Cross-subject decoding of imagined speech from scalp EEG: a leakage-controlled evaluation on three public corpora
authors: Blessing Isoyiza Adeika & Onyema Osuagwu

slides.hook: A decoder of imagined speech that works for a new user without calibration would make a non-invasive speech interface practical.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We tested whether imagined-speech content recorded with scalp electroencephalography (EEG) transfers across people, and examined why accuracy within a single person remains low. We analyzed three public corpora, ds003626, KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion and reports exact binomial thresholds, group tests and bootstrap confidence intervals.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We trained decoders on each participant and tested them on every other, compared representational geometry across participants without a classifier, applied subject-level alignment, and tested five explanations for the within-subject ceiling. Across 482 ordered pairs of participants, no pair survived correction for multiple comparisons; mean pair-transfer accuracy lay within 0.006 of chance on every corpus, while every within-subject reference lay above it.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Trial count per class was the only variable that ordered the corpora, which favors larger single-condition datasets over further model development.

title: Large Language Model Agents for Evidence Based Genetic Disease Severity Classification
authors: Tohid Ghasemnejad, Ahmadreza Argha et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Disease severity classification for genetic conditions is subjective and labor-intensive, creating bottlenecks in genomic screening, where commercial panels vary widely in size and overlap.

title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
authors: Anthony M. Polloreno, Timothy Proctor et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB mathscr{L} matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Pauli-correlation and active generators are absent from the linear term and enter only at higher order. For the single-qubit native gate set {X_{π/2},Y_{π/2}} we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results turn RB decay rates into interpretable functions of experimentally meaningful elementary error rates.

title: Double-Take: Improving Capacity, Binding, and Selectivity In Long-Context Within Bidirectional Memory
authors: Vakul Raghavan, Utkarsh Grover et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Processing a long sequence does not guarantee that distant information remains usable.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: As context grows, a fixed-size memory must retain many associations, connect information across positions, and preserve relevant structure without being overwhelmed by everything it observes. These are distinct requirements: a memory may store more information without representing the relationships needed for retrieval, and it may transport those relationships without preserving the ones that matter.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Thus, the challenge is not simply extending context length, but constructing a memory that remains usable as context grows. We study this problem in large-chunk test-time training (TTT) and identify two basic failures: single-step writes accumulate interference, limiting capacity, while self-associative writes cannot form cross-position bindings.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results identify capacity, binding, and selectivity as three requirements for usable long-range memory.

title: Density-split analyses of the pairwise kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
authors: Finn A. Roper, Aritra K. Gon et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: We consider the dependence of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect on the environments of foreground cosmological structures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Standard pairwise kSZ estimators exploit the fact that galaxies below separations of sim 200,h^{-1}{rm M}_odot fall towards each other on average, yielding a negative mean pairwise kSZ signal. However, this signal is the residual from a near-cancellation between outflows from underdense regions and infall towards overdensities giving a large variance in the pairwise velocity distribution and hence a low signal-to-noise ratio for the mean kSZ signal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This effect is especially marked at the largest scales, where the pairwise velocity distribution becomes more symmetric about zero. We show that splitting galaxies according to their local overdensity allows the convergence and divergence flows to be separated, yielding pairwise kSZ signals of opposing sign, with a reduction in variance for each subset.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We predict that the density-split pairwise kSZ will increase the significance of detection by only a modest factor; nevertheless, we expect improvements by factors of respectively 11 and 4 in constraining σ_8 and Ω_{rm m} when using the combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope surveys.

slides.hook: The continued demand for smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient technologies has driven condensed-matter research towards materials combining multiple responses within a single phase.

title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
authors: Yasir Mahmood, Daniel Wines et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Silicon nanowires (Si NWs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation nanoelectronic devices due to their tunable electronic properties, and compatibility with aggressive scaling requirements.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The integration of strain further enhances their performance by modulating carrier mobility, band structure, and transport behavior without altering material chemistry. Within the NW, the silicon-silicon dioxide (Si-SiO_{2}) interface serves as a critical region where strain redistribution and suboxide bonding collectively influence the mechanical and electronic response.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we combine reactive force field molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations to investigate how oxidation-induced interfacial structure and crystallographic facet orientation govern strain-dependent bond evolution and facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties in oxidized Si NWs. Simulated dry thermal oxidation generates chemically realistic Si-SiO_{2} interfaces, enabling direct characterization of bond order redistribution and stress gradient development across the interface under tensile strain.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results establish a direct coupling between interfacial suboxide chemistry, mechanical deformation, and electronic structure, providing atomistic insight into strain-modulated behavior at oxidized silicon interfaces in faceted NWs.

slides.hook: AlphaFold confidence scores are widely used to rank protein complex predictions and to select subsets of models for downstream applications.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although these scores provide strong discriminatory power for distinguishing prediction quality, their numerical values were never intended to represent the probability that a prediction satisfies a given structural quality criterion. In this work, we calibrate commonly used confidence scores to estimate the probability that a predicted complex exceeds a chosen threshold of DockQ, an established measure of interface quality.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On antibody-antigen and general multimer datasets, post-hoc isotonic calibration consistently improves agreement between predicted probabilities and observed DockQ success rates while preserving the underlying score ordering. The calibrated probabilities also provide more accurate estimates of the fraction of selected models expected to pass a given structural quality threshold.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Because the calibration is entirely post hoc and requires no underlying AlphaFold model fine-tuning, it provides a straightforward and customizable way to convert existing model quality rankings into calibrated probabilities of passing a chosen structural quality threshold.

slides.hook: Detecting online social engineering (SE) scams often requires examining website workflows, verifying claims against external sources, and connecting evidence across multiple pages.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing detectors provide limited support for these investigations, leaving analysts to manually gather and validate evidence, which inevitably delays detection and subsequent takedown of these attacks. To address this gap, we present ReDence, an open-source hybrid framework for adaptive, evidence-grounded detection across diverse SE scam categories.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: ReDence combines two locally hosted models with complementary responsibilities: a fine-tuned multimodal agentic Investigator (Qwen3.5-4B) that performs investigative planning, evidence interpretation, and reporting, and a specialized Decider (Tev1) that handles binary and multiple-choice tasks, including browser-action selection, evidence assessment, and decisions about whether to continue an investigation. By delegating discrete decisions to a specialized model, ReDence reduces reliance on lengthy language-model responses, while preserving the reasoning capabilities required for complex investigations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: ReDence also produces structured, evidence-grounded reports that document investigative actions, supporting and contradictory evidence, and collected artifacts, which allow analysts to independently audit detection decisions and utilize the collected evidence to support subsequent mitigation and takedown efforts.

title: The ALMA-QUARKS survey: A Keplerian Circumbinary Disk Candidate in the High-mass Star-forming Region IRAS 08303-4303
authors: Gyuho Lee, Kee-Tae Kim et al. (36 researchers)

slides.hook: We present the ALMA Band 6 continuum and molecular line observations of IRAS 08303-4303, a high-mass star-forming region, with an angular resolution of sim 0.3'' (sim 700 au at the distance of 2.35 kpc).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Six dense condensations are identified in the 1.3 mm continuum, and at least four of them are associated with molecular outflows. The estimated outflow parameters, particularly mass outflow rates geq 10^{-4} M_{odot} yr^{-1}, suggest that the driving sources are high-mass young stellar objects.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Two of the condensations are forming a wide protobinary system with a separation of sim 900 au. They reside within a single rotating structure, identified as a circumbinary disk which has a mass of about 2 M_{odot}.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This source, therefore, serves as a key laboratory for understanding the formation of high-mass binary systems.

title: IMPPAT 3.0: An updated FAIR database of phytochemicals and formulations of Indian Medicinal plants
authors: Shanmuga Priya Baskaran, Ajaya Kumar Sahoo et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Ayurvedic formulations represent a rich source of traditional knowledge, encompassing distinct therapeutic approaches, medicinal ingredients, and underlying principles of drug action.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, systematic integration of this knowledge with standardized modern biomedical terminology and resources remains limited. Here, we present IMPPAT 3.0, an updated version of the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry And Therapeutics (IMPPAT: https://cb.imsc.res.in/imppat/) database that extends its scope by incorporating curated and harmonized information on Ayurvedic formulations from authoritative sources, while expanding its coverage of medicinal plants, phytochemicals, and therapeutic use terms.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: IMPPAT 3.0 further enriches plant and phytochemical information with annotations on clinical trials, patents, bioactivity, protein targets, spectral data, plant image links, and AyuCaRe reports. The compiled data is also organized as IMPPAT-KG, a knowledge graph that enables exploration of relationships among IMPPAT entities.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: In conclusion, by integrating traditional medicinal knowledge, IMPPAT provides a FAIR-compliant ethnopharmacological platform for systematic investigation of Indian medicinal plants and Ayurvedic formulations for drug discovery applications.

slides.hook: Generative AI imposes new metacognitive demands on knowledge workers as their work shifts from production to planning, evaluation, and orchestration.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In a randomized, between-subjects experiment on AI-assisted writing (297 workers, 594 essays), we test dynamically-generated metacognitive scaffolds supporting goal specification and task decomposition. title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models
authors: Hossein Resani & Javen Qinfeng Shi

slides.hook: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Inside-JEPA, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state. On Something-Something V2, latent prediction alone performs no better than a random relation head, while inverse-dynamics supervision that recovers actions from channel changes improves relational AUROC by .065-.103 across ten settings with annotated boxes, by .081 on RH20T robot episodes with held-out tasks, and by .050-.061 across five relations using off-the-shelf detection and tracking.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: An inverse head on entity latents decodes actions more accurately but barely improves relational grounding; shuffled labels, two label-free objectives, and action labels on only 5% of the pairs also fail to ground the channels. Given an action, predicted relational changes approach the quality of observed future relations (AUROC .599 vs .621).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: For one-step relational goals, a supervised readout of the 16 channels ranks the correct action among the top five of 65 in 43% of cases, compared with 24% for prediction-only latents and 17% for a frequency prior.

slides.hook: Collision cross section (CCS), derived from ion mobility mass spectrometry, is a common descriptor for molecular annotation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Prediction is challenging for machine learning models because it reflects the size, shape, and ionization state of a gas-phase molecular ion. slides.hook: The brain maintains stable cognition despite continuously changing neural activity.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: How to extract stable cognitive states from variable neural observations remains a central problem in neural decoding. Existing neural decoding methods map neural observations to predefined external labels based on the stimulus-response principle, often capturing recording-specific spurious correlations.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Inspired by how the brain infers the world, and specifically by Bayesian brain theory, we recast neural decoding as cognitive inference constrained by brain-intrinsic priors, yielding high-level meta-neural semantic representations. In decoding experiments spanning five neural recording modalities and three cognitive domains (motor, perception and internal mentation), our cognitive inference method reorganized the geometry of neural observation representations, yielding meta-neural semantic representations that exhibited consistent geometric relationships across cognitive tasks and enabled the recovery of stable cognitive states from variable neural observations.

authors: Younghwan Joo, Sanghyun Oh et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: With a single parameter set, the simulation reproduces three types of published measurements: the change of the surface-to-interface binder ratio with drying rate over a factor of 5.6 and the surface and interface binder levels of films six times thicker; concentration profiles through the film interior; and the response of the interface binder to the time at which the drying rate is switched mid-process. Applied without further adjustment to a published three-stage schedule, the model reproduces the shortened drying and the full interface recovery when the rate is lowered early, and shows that its final high-rate stage begins after the binder has stopped.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Combined with a coater-scale process model, the model can be used to identify operating points for electrode production that improve energy efficiency and product quality together.

title: Alignment of visual brain encoding models with individual perceptual similarity judgments
authors: Daniel Chong, Haomiao Chen et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Encoding models that predict brain activation responses to images have traditionally been trained to maximize accuracy when predicting observed brain data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, their internal representations may not reflect individual human perception. In this work, we investigate whether we can fine-tune brain encoding models to better align their representations with individuals' similarity judgments.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using similarity judgments of 100 images from 8 participants in the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we adapt a generic human similarity judgment model (DreamSim) separately for each participant to obtain personalized perceptual similarity models. These models are then used to obtain subject-specific similarity structure across images in their encoding model training sets.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our framework provides an approach for bootstrapping human similarity judgment data into more individualized, human-aligned brain encoding models of vision.

title: The Structural Anatomy of Galaxies: Environmental Dependence of Morphological and Quenching Evolution at 0.1 < z < 0.5
authors: Can Xu, John D. Silverman et al. (15 researchers)

slides.hook: We investigate how cluster environments affect galaxy star formation, structure, and stellar populations using spectroscopically-confirmed galaxies in X-ray-selected eROSITA clusters, that have deep HSC-SSP imaging and DESI DR1 spectroscopy.
