slides.content: At 0.1<z<0.5, we compare dust-corrected Ha star formation rates (SFRs), effective radii (Re), bulge-to-total light ratios (B/T), and Dn4000 between cluster satellites and a stellar-mass- and redshift-matched field control sample. We identify UVJ-quiescent galaxies and divide the UVJ star-forming population at log(sSFR_Ha)= -10.5 yr-1 into actively star-forming and Ha-low systems, the latter referred to as green-valley (GV) galaxies.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Cluster--field differences depend strongly on stellar mass, projected cluster-centric radius, and galaxy population. Cluster star-forming galaxies show modest SFR suppression but weak structural offsets.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show that environmental quenching and structural transformation are most strongly coupled in the Ha-low transition population.

title: JWST observations of the planetary nebula NGC 6302 IV: PAH spectral characteristics, formation and evolution
authors: Nicholas Clark, Els Peeters et al. (32 researchers)

slides.hook: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and carbonaceous dust have been observed in Oxygen-rich planetary nebulae (PNe), yet their formation and evolution in these environments is an open question.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We aim to study the formation and evolution of the PAHs in the O-rich PN NGC 6302, by characterizing the PAH emission throughout this object. We obtained JWST MIRI IFU spectroscopic observations of NGC 6302 pointed at its central source.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: From these, we extract four template spectra that are representative of the variation in PAH emission throughout NGC 6302. We detect the major PAH features at 6.2, 7.7, 8.6, 11.2, and 12.7 μm, and several minor PAH features.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We find that NGC 6302 formed PAHs in-situ in the current PN phase, likely from small hydrocarbons formed by the photodissociation of CO.

title: Neutron Star-Main-Sequence Star Collision: Formation and Long-Term Evolution of Thorne-Żytkow Objects
authors: Yuhao Guo, Xiao-Tian Xu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Thorne-dot{mathrm{Z}}ytkow objects (Tdot{mathrm{Z}}Os) are stars containing a neutron-star (NS) or black-hole (BH) core embedded in a stellar envelope and powered primarily by mass accretion onto the core.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Classical evolution models of Tdot{mathrm{Z}}Os begin with an assumed equilibrium configuration and predict chemical anomalies in the stellar envelope resulting from nuclear burning in the vicinity of the NS core. Here we connect dynamical formation to long-term evolution by combining a three-dimensional simulation of a post-supernova collision between a 1.4M_odot NS and a 10M_odot main-sequence star with a subsequent stellar evolution calculation using MESA.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The collision successfully produces a bound, quasi-spherical Tdot{mathrm{Z}}O with the NS settled at the center of the stellar envelope. In contrast to the classical picture, the collision heats a substantial fraction of the star and leads to widespread nuclear burning during the subsequent thermal-relaxation phase.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: At the end of our simulation, the stellar luminosity greatly exceeds Eddington in the outer envelope, suggesting that significant mass ejection will occur, leaving behind an isolated NS or BH.

slides.hook: Recent high-resolution (500 bp) Hi-C experiments reported contact maps with unusual patterns around highly expressed bacterial DNA loci.

title: Structure alone supports efficient visual computation in the Drosophila visual system
authors: Eudald Correig-Fraga, Roger Guimerà et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Understanding the extent to which measured synaptic wiring determines computation remains a central challenge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we couple the proofread adult Drosophila melanogaster connectome to an anatomically faithful model of its eye. Visual information is inputted in the eye model, then passed to the connectome, and finally read from a Kenyon-cell-centered linear decoder.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This creates a connectome-only model in which the anatomical graph and eye geometry are fixed and only scalar synaptic gains and neuronal thresholds may be learned. The model supports multitask vision, including color discrimination, shape classification, and numerical discrimination that follows a ratio-dependent scaling characteristic of approximate number perception.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings indicate that the measured connectivity and eye geometry jointly set efficient operating points for visual computation.

title: SpecLess: A Multi Survey Python Package for Machine Learning Classification of Galaxy Morphology and Activity from Photometry
authors: Uzay Aydin & Mehmet Tanriver

slides.hook: Broad band photometry enables scalable galaxy classification without spectroscopy at inference time, yet strong within survey performance may not transfer when the same galaxies are measured by another survey.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present SpecLess, an open source Python package implementing two photometric classification tasks: high confidence Galaxy Zoo 1 elliptical and spiral morphologies, and four SDSS spectroscopic activity reference classes (starforming, starburst, Seyfert, and LINER). Using SDSS+AllWISE, KiDS+VIKING, and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys photometry, survey specific XGBoost classifiers achieve held out macro F1 scores of 0.9332 (SDSS; 35,554 galaxies) and 0.9237 (KiDS; 3,269) for morphology, and 0.7637 (SDSS; 16,931) and 0.7398 (DESI; 11,975) for activity.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Starforming and starburst references are recovered more effectively than Seyfert and LINER, while feature ablations reveal complementary contributions from optical and mid infrared photometry. We quantify catalogue dependence using separately trained common feature models evaluated on matched galaxies with identical labels and data partitions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The package provides a reproducible baseline for photometric galaxy classification across multiple surveys while establishing an extensible, open source foundation for future developments in classification methods and photometric catalogue support.

authors: Fabian Isensee, Constantin Ulrich Harsy et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it.

title: RNA Design via Conditioned Flow Matching and Finite-Policy Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zefeng Lin, Xianyong Fang et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: RNA design aims to identify sequences that fold into specified secondary structures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing methods formulate the task as target-specific search or conditional generation. However, natural RNA evolution proceeds through sequence variation and selection, with compensatory substitutions, whereas these methods do not explicitly model this process.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address this limitation, we propose a two-stage framework comprising RNA Inverse-Folding Flow (RNA-IFlow) and RNA-IFlow-RL. RNA-IFlow uses structure-conditioned Dirichlet Flow Matching to model coordinated variation across the sequence, while RNA-IFlow-RL maps the learned flow to a pairing-preserving finite policy and refines it with thermodynamic feedback.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our work couples coordinated variation with thermodynamic selection, offering a novel paradigm for RNA design.

title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
authors: Anna Bobrikova, Alexandra Veledina et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. slides.content: Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with IXPE and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

title: Thermal expansion mechanisms, heat transport, and band-gap renormalization in strongly anharmonic Rb_2SO_4, Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3, and Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3 from machine-learned interatomic potentials
authors: Ekaterina Spirande, Rustam Arabov et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Rb_2SO_4, Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3, and Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3 are structurally complex materials whose thermal expansion has been interpreted, on the basis of high-temperature x-ray diffraction, in terms of specific polyhedral rearrangements.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study their lattice dynamics and its consequences for thermal and electronic properties using molecular dynamics with actively learned moment tensor potentials trained on density-functional theory data. The anharmonicity measure σ^A (compares the anharmonic contribution to the interatomic forces with the total forces acting on atoms) reaches approx0.3-0.5 for β-Rb_2SO_4, Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3, and Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3 and approx0.75 for orientationally disordered α-Rb_2SO_4, and the imaginary harmonic modes of Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3 and α-Rb_2SO_4 are stabilized at finite temperature.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The simulations reproduce the measured thermal expansion and support the mechanisms proposed from diffraction: expansion along c in β-Rb_2SO_4 arises from both elongation and straightening of corrugated Rb chains, BO_3 reorientation accompanies the anisotropic expansion of Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3, and bending of polyhedral linkages limits expansion along the weakly expanding directions and in cubic Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3. Green-Kubo lattice thermal conductivities differ by more than an order of magnitude between compounds with comparable σ^A, showing that the anharmonicity measure alone does not determine heat transport.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Phonon-induced band-gap renormalization, including lattice thermal expansion, reaches 2.7 and 1.7 eV at 1250 K in Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3 and Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3 and 1.4 eV at 650 K in β-Rb_2SO_4, with zero-point renormalizations of 0.64, 0.70, and 0.31 eV for β-Rb_2SO_4, Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3, and Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3, respectively.

slides.hook: Motivated by a recent experimental work arXiv:2608.20327, we theoretically investigate the nature of phase transitions in a trapped dipolar quantum gas upon tuning the contact interaction strength and dipole orientation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using extended Gross-Pitaevskii simulations including thermal and quantum effects, we map the phase diagram comprising unmodulated superfluids, triangular droplet arrays, and stripe states. We further characterize the order of the transitions separating them through imaginary-time hysteresis analysis.

title: Improving scoring functions for protein-protein docking with LambdaLoss
authors: Richard Zhu, Darren Xu et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Modeling protein-protein interactions requires accurate scoring functions that can rank potential poses (conformations) of a protein-protein complex to differentiate near-native poses from incorrect ones.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we propose a general framework for improving protein-protein pose ranking and other biomolecular interaction models using the LambdaLoss loss function from the Learning-to-Rank field. We test this framework by fine-tuning the energy prediction head of DFMDock with the LambdaLoss on an augmented dataset of 2.9M decoy poses derived from the DIPS dataset.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On targets from the CAPRI score set benchmark, our fine-tuned ranking model LambdaDockScore is better at identifying correct poses in its top-1 and top-5 predictions compared to EuDockScore, a state-of-the-art method. LambdaDockScore also improves upon baseline DFMDock ranking performance for scoring antibody-antigen complexes and protein-protein complexes with very large or small binding interfaces.

title: Orchestra: Corroboration-Based Regulatory Candidate Discovery via Composed Bioinformatics MCP Agents
authors: Jose A. Bird

slides.hook: Orchestra composes two independently built bioinformatics MCP servers -- RegNetAgents, which infers regulatory network topology, and CASCADE, which provides independent functional evidence (LINCS knockdown, DepMap essentiality, super-enhancer status, DoRothEA transcription-factor confidence) -- into one multi-agent LangGraph workflow.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Its central claim is that requiring the two systems to agree on a candidate regulator yields a more trustworthy candidate than either alone. We test this on the TCGA tumor-acquired regulator tier, selecting each query's ten regulators by ARACNe mutual-information edge weight.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across BRCA/COAD focal genes and matched negative controls, requiring at least 2 of 4 evidence sources predicts known-driver status (IntOGen) among focal genes (odds ratio 3.15, Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p=0.016; 2.92 after deduplication) but shows no association among negative controls (p=0.70); a single source does not in BRCA/COAD. In a second panel (STAD) the pattern reproduces and is stronger (OR 6.71, adjusted p=0.0047), again with no association in controls.

slides.content: All experiments invoke Orchestra's real agentic entry point.

title: Adapting Boltz-2 with limited experimental activity data improves early enrichment in virtual screening
authors: Kairi Furui & Masahito Ohue

comments.author: Prof. Liam Henderson (CERN)

slides.hook: Virtual screening aims to prioritize active compounds from large chemical libraries within a limited experimental budget.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: When applying Boltz-2 to virtual screening, a key challenge is how to use limited experimental data from the target assay to improve the prioritization of active compounds. We investigated whether fine-tuning the Boltz-2 affinity heads with a small number of binary activity labels could improve early enrichment of active compounds in hit discovery.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We compared fine-tuning with 40-300 labels in a retrospective evaluation on eight MF-PCBA targets. With 300 activity measurements, fine-tuning increased the number of actives in the top 1% by a geometric mean of 1.77-fold across the eight targets and improved average precision (AP) by 2.14-fold relative to the control without fine-tuning.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings show that affinity-head fine-tuning with limited activity labels improves early enrichment with Boltz-2 and that this benefit can be retained when rescoring a restricted set of candidates.

slides.hook: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing predictors primarily rely on transcriptomic measurements, although chromatin accessibility provides complementary information about the cellular context in which perturbations act. title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
authors: Alberto Carlini, Andrea Lanza et al. (8 researchers)

comments.author: Marcus Vance (Oxford)
comments.text: Has this benchmark been cross-validated across independent hardware setups?

replies.author: Dr. Julian Thorne (Cambridge)

slides.hook: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.

title: Ensemble basis-free coherence for quantum communication
authors: Aleksei Kodukhov

slides.hook: The resource theory of coherence quantifies the quantum properties of states and their role in quantum information processing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Extending coherence theory to ensembles, the natural objects in quantum communication, remains an active research direction, with their operational potential still being explored. In this work, we establish a maximally coherent ensemble in every finite dimension: the continuous ensemble of pure states distributed according to the normalized Haar measure attains the tight upper bound on basis-free relative entropy ensemble coherence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We then prove that ensemble coherence bounds the effective informational advantage of postselective measurements over the Holevo quantity for two equiprobable pure states. Finally, for the qubit B92 QKD protocol, we show that the coherence of Alice's ensemble upper-bounds the secret key rate in the asymptotic regime.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results give ensemble coherence a quantitative operational meaning in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Capturing Open Quantum System Dynamics with Compact Dressed Hamiltonians
authors: Zachary Giles & Dvira Segal

slides.hook: We advance the compact dressed Hamiltonian (CDH) framework to simulate the dynamics of open quantum systems strongly coupled to structured bosonic environments.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The CDH approach combines reaction-coordinate mapping with a polaron transformation, incorporating strong system-environment hybridization into a dressed representation before truncating the collective bosonic mode. slides.content: As a whole, the CDH framework provides an efficient and physical description of strongly coupled open quantum-system dynamics.

slides.hook: Neuronal excitability is commonly modeled using different principles at the cellular and population scales, making it difficult to study how microscopic mechanisms shape macroscopic activity.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce a spatiotemporal excitatory-inhibitory (EI) model that unifies these scales through a common mixed-feedback architecture. We show that combining these mechanisms gives rise to population excitability in strongly heterogeneous populations.

slides.hook: Wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU) systems for construction worker human activity recognition (HAR) routinely report aggregate accuracies above 95 %, rarely under genuine subject-independent (leave-one-subject-out (LOSO)) evaluation, masking the per-individual variance that determines real-world deployment performance.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using the VTT-ConIoT benchmark, we conduct, to our knowledge, the first systematic configuration sensitivity analysis of this dataset: six classifiers across five sensor placements and three window sizes under a single LOSO protocol, a personalised-calibration pilot, and a validated comparison of tabular GAN-based and standard time-series augmentation. title: Grain-Boundary Scattering between Chiral Domains in Chiral Topological Semimetal CoSi
authors: Nicholas A. Lanzillo, Ion Garate et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In contrast, these surface electrons get scattered along the twin grain boundaries between heterochiral domains to the opposite surface, resulting in partial forward transmission and partial backscattering that yields higher grain-boundary resistivity. This work helps elucidate the complexities of electron transport in chiral topological semimetals for potential application in next-generation nano-interconnects.

title: An interactive simulator for integrating biochemical models with experimental data
authors: Herbert M. Sauro, Dan Nguyen et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Biological models based on mathematical simulations (e.g., ordinary differential equations) are hugely beneficial for understanding biological processes and predicting the outcomes of experiments.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such models are built using a variety of sophisticated modeling tools. Unfortunately, the complexity of these tools is often a barrier to use by experimental biologists.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To improve the usability and impact of biological models, we have created a desktop platform (DeskIridium) and a web-based simulator (WebIridium, hosted as a GitHub page) that, in combination, provide features that promote ease of use by experimental biologists, including: human-readable editing of models via the Antimony syntax; sliders for adjusting parameter values while simultaneously displaying simulation results in real time; zero-install distribution; AI chat integration; and generation of standalone Python implementations of SBML models to support reproducibility. The desktop version uses the well-established libroadrunner simulation package; the web-based application uses an Emscripten translated version of COPASI.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Binaries, source code, and the web interface are available at: https://github.com/sys-bio/IridiumSimulator and https://github.com/sys-bio/WebIridium.

title: A neural-network model to find correlations in astrochemical space
authors: Daniel Giovanni Vargas, Darío Barreiro-Lage et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: The detection of new interstellar molecules is central to astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field in past decade has been the increase in both number and diversity of detected species.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using natural language processing models, we develop a machine-learning pipeline, similar to other approaches reported in the literature, to connect molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: These representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17/0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29/0.59, and coefficients of determination of 0.88/0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Beyond accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.

title: PlainMap: a lightweight, restartable mapping pipeline for ancient and modern DNA
authors: Michael V. Westbury

slides.hook: Mapping sequencing reads to a reference genome requires preprocessing and alignment choices that can vary with library type, fragment length, sequencing platform, and reference genome.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These considerations are particularly important for ancient and historical DNA, where short and damaged fragments can make the most appropriate mapping strategy difficult to determine a priori. We present PlainMap, a lightweight and restartable mapping pipeline for modern and degraded DNA sequencing data.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: PlainMap accepts a simple manifest of FASTQ files, automatically identifies single-end and paired-end data from read headers, supports mixed sequencing platforms, and provides alternative mapping strategies for modern and degraded DNA. Deterministic chunking and checkpoint-based execution allow large analyses to resume after interruption, while optional pilot subsampling enables empirical comparison of mapping strategies using identical subsets of raw fragments.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: PlainMap is implemented as a single Bash script and is freely available at https://github.com/BiodiversityExtinction/PlainMap.

title: Convex Equilibrium Potentials for Monge--Ampère: Curvature Bounds and A Posteriori Evaluation
authors: Edison Vázquez, Yingdong Lu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Equilibrium neural networks define their hidden state as the fixed point of a contraction, so their effective depth is set at evaluation time rather than by the architecture.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using them for fully nonlinear PDEs raises two issues that explicit networks avoid: second derivatives may grow with the effective depth, and the potential is only ever evaluated approximately. We study nonnegative softplus equilibrium networks with contraction factor q<1, a convex class suited to the Monge--Ampère equation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A positivity cancellation in the resolvent shows that the Hessian grows at most like (1-q)^{-2}, rather than the (1-q)^{-3} of a direct estimate, and an explicit one-neuron family shows that this exponent is sharp; third derivatives satisfy a sharp (1-q)^{-3} bound. Residual-based a posteriori estimates then control the state, its input derivatives and, in two dimensions, the Hessian determinant at an approximate equilibrium.

slides.hook: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions.

title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
authors: Aditya Kumar & Sayan Choudhury

slides.hook: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude S_{rm cen} mediates interactions between N bath spins through a star-graph topology.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of N^2/e with the collective langle J_yrangle readout, corresponding to a 4.34,mathrm{dB} offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Crucially, with a small N-independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of N^2/4 (6,mathrm{dB} below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude S_{rm cen} provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.

title: IndoNutriQA: An Indonesian Clinical Nutrition Question Answering Benchmark
authors: Tirana Noor Fatyanosa, Ummu Ditya Erliana et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Clinical Question Answering (QA) underpins Clinical Intelligent Decision Support Systems, but progress is severely limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian by the absence of public domain-specific data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce IndoNutriQA, an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs built from real clinical-nutrition reports. Rather than a large-scale training corpus, it is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource: every pair is grounded in a clinically relevant context, enriched with structured metadata (anthropometric assessment, medical diagnosis, document provenance, chunk segmentation).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Eight standardised question types following the Nutrition Care Process (NCP), including the Problem, Etiology, Sign and Symptom (PES) diagnosis statement, are answered for every report, which was written by a graduate-level dietetic intern, by one of three nutritionists. Answers are free-form clinical prose rather than extractive spans, and an expert validation study finds 6-10% of reference answers contestable.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: IndoNutriQA is released to foster research in Indonesian clinical NLP and nutritional decision support.

slides.hook: Computer-use agents increasingly handle private information and act on users' behalf across desktop and web applications, including email.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Phishing therefore poses privacy and security risks that depend not only on whether agents recognize malicious messages, but also on how they respond. slides.content: To expose vulnerabilities that pre-existing datasets may miss, we introduce AgentPhishing, a benchmark for evaluating whether persuasive phishing attacks can evade detection and induce LLM email agents to comply with malicious requests. title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
authors: Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.

title: Multiphysics Simulation Framework for Continuous Ion Transport and Energetics in Atmospheric Pressure Interfaces
authors: Yihui Yan, Jozef Lengyel et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Optimizing atmospheric pressure interfaces requires balancing efficient ion transport with unwanted collision activation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The complex environment at the inlet region, including rapid pressure drops, RF/DC electric fields, ion-gas collisions, and space charge effects, makes simulation of this system challenging. In this work, we introduce MuCITE (Multiphysics simulation for Continuous Ion Transport and Energetics), which combines continuous ion injection, precomputed electric and gas flow fields, and particle-in-cell space charge updates.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Furthermore, by employing improved impulsive collision theory, it can not only predict transport but also analyze the loss position of ions and the evolution of their kinetic energy, internal energy, and dissociation probability during transport. title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents
authors: Yiqi Wang, Zizhi Zeng et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Web agents increasingly serve the same user across repeated online tasks such as booking travel, shopping, and scheduling, so their long-term usefulness depends on how well they know the user's preferences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Passive memory and personalization methods cannot obtain preferences the user never reveals, and clarification methods that value a question by its benefit to the current task overlook the benefit of reusing the answer in later tasks. We study Active Preference Acquisition (APA): which missing preferences are worth the cost of asking? We define the Prospective Personalization Value (PPV) of a missing preference as its expected cumulative utility gain over future tasks minus the effort and disclosure-risk cost of asking, and select questions under a per-interaction budget.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We characterize when cumulative reuse justifies acquisition despite insufficient single-task benefit, and evaluate this regime with an initial-profile diagnostic. APA computes the counterfactual gain of each candidate preference on public task prototypes with the agent's own task solver and aggregates it by the expected reuse of each task family.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The value of acquiring a user preference should account for its reuse across future tasks, not only its benefit to the task at hand.

title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
authors: Robin Quériaux, Solveig Bachellery et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Institutions that deploy large language models in regulated settings often need technical evidence of responsible AI practices before approving a deployment.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: COMPL-AI provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act that organises this evidence under six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, twelve of which current benchmarks can measure. The benchmark suites that produce this evidence are typically operated from a command line, while the staff who approve deployments are non-engineers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present VERA, an open-source self-hosted dashboard deployed to facilitate responsible AI processes within a large European bank. A reviewer selects a model and runs public benchmarks against it.

title: Stochastic gradient descent on the epigenetic landscape: a unified framework for cellular plasticity, tumor heterogeneity, and the asymptotic irrelevance of fitness
authors: Artur C. Fassoni

slides.hook: Phenotypic plasticity, the ability of cells to switch between states, is central to development, differentiation, and therapy resistance.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although it is modeled at several scales, from compartmental ODEs to phenotype-structured PDEs and single-cell stochastic equations, a framework connecting these descriptions is missing. We present such a framework.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Starting from a general n-compartment ODE model encompassing nonlinear growth and linear transitions between phenotypes, we show, with a new, elementary and generalizable proof of a recent theorem, that under uniform competition, the long-term population distribution is solely governed by transition rates. All phenotypes become selectively neutral at saturation, and the imprint of fitness differences during growth fades at an explicit rate.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This framework provides a physical interpretation of Waddington's landscape, where cells perform SGD, and cancer corresponds to a corrupted landscape.

slides.hook: Neural simulation is an essential methodology for studying biological nervous systems, but it remains limited by the computational costs of repeatedly updating neural and synaptic states over many timesteps.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Neuromorphic hardware is a promising substrate for this class of workloads because such devices combine event-driven execution, localized memory, and spike-based communication. However, neuromorphic textit{software} remains comparatively fragmented and difficult to integrate with the model-description standards used by the computational neuroscience community.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This disconnect limits reproducible experimentation and makes direct comparison between conventional and neuromorphic simulation workflows difficult. This paper introduces ``NeuroML2Loihi'', an open-source framework for translating NeuroML model descriptions into Loihi~2-deployable Lava primitives, enabling standardized biological models to be executed on Intel's Loihi~2 neuromorphic chip.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that standards-based neuromorphic neural simulation is feasible on Loihi~2 and can support meaningful comparison against established computational neuroscience workflows.

title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
authors: Tariq Mahassen, Marcin Jastrzebski et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We develop and analyze generative models based on quantum solvers of stochastic differential equations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Unlike the common approach based on layered variational quantum circuits with parameterized rotations, we parameterize the potential of a Langevin process. The associated Fokker-Planck (FP) equations are Hermitianized and solved using a linear combination of cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By encoding the square root of the stationary density, the model enables sampling through computational-basis measurements and is efficiently controlled by coefficients of the block-encoded diagonal potential. We train the proposed model to match empirical distributions within the family described by FP equations, demonstrating parameter recovery for multivariate probability distributions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our approach frames quantum generative learning as quantum model discovery and provides a foundation for extending this framework to high-dimensional, strongly correlated scientific data.

title: Mitigating Saliency Collapse: Robust Saliency-Aware Long-Text Image-Text Alignment
authors: Qiuyu Kong, Zanxi Ruan et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Long-text image-text alignment is essential for fine-grained scene understanding, yet existing methods mainly focus on extending context length or improving local alignment.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We identify an overlooked failure mode, saliency collapse, where models over-rely on text that features visual prominence while underutilizing non-salient context. Consequently, retrieval performance degrades sharply when salient content is reduced, despite that the non-salient context remains informative.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address this, we propose RoSA, a saliency-aware finetuning framework that decomposes image-text pairs into complementary salient and contextual views, enabling joint learning of prominent and contextual semantics. We propose a modality-independent decomposition strategy to combine object-level visual saliency estimation with LLM-based text decomposition to bridge vision and language.

title: Investigating Multi-Cultural Value Selection Biases in LLMs
authors: Siddhesh Pawar, Arnav Arora et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) serve users whose cultural identities are multi-layered, yet cultural evaluations commonly reduce identity to one label.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this work, we study LLMs under simultaneous identity cues, with a country persona in the system prompt and a second identity signaled in the user turn, either by naming a country (explicit cue) or through the query language (implicit cue). We test World Values Survey (WVS) multiple-choice probing and open-ended sociopolitical generation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In multiple-choice probing, language cues shift answers about three times more than explicit cues but away from the associated country's distribution, and explicit cues do not consistently move answers toward the named country. Across 1.6 million open-ended responses, naming a country closes 30-44% of the gap to the model's own responses for that country, and explicit cues produce more differentiated value changes than language cues.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results suggest that country and language cues should be evaluated as distinct signals rather than interchangeable proxies for culture.

title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
authors: Ying-Xue Zhang, Hui-Min Zhao et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level Λ system. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our scheme with these specific features is geared towards enabling compact vapor-cell-based nonreciprocal devices for quantum network applications.

slides.hook: The prospect of imaging single biomolecules, viruses and cells with intense, ultrashort X-ray pulses has driven the development of X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the weak scattering from small particles is easily swamped by background from residual gas, which has so far limited applications to strongly scattering targets such as viruses, cell organelles and cells. Here we report a three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of an isolated 1-MDa membrane-protein complex, photosystem I (PS I), from single-particle diffraction data.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: PS I trimers were aerosolised by charge-reduction electrospray ionisation and injected into the European XFEL beam, with partial helium gas exchange reducing background scattering by 80%. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show that membrane-protein complexes can be imaged in vacuo with X-ray lasers, an important step towards ultrafast diffractive imaging of single macromolecules.

title: Fully Automated Wannier Disentanglement via Projectability Selection in Gaussian and Augmented Plane-Wave Frameworks
authors: William P. Comaskey & Jose L. Mendoza-Cortes

slides.hook: Constructing the frozen manifold for entangled bands requires balancing exact reproduction of the target bands with sufficient variational freedom to build a well-localized subspace from the broader Bloch pool.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present a workflow that systematically determines the energy ceiling for a target number of selected Wannier projections, freezing every Bloch state below this threshold across the sampled k-mesh. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In comparisons where we controlled the extent of the energy ceiling, freezing all sub-ceiling states is generally favored over projectability-based frozen states. Of the seven materials we tested, freezing all sub-ceiling states lowers the band error on four from between 11 meV and 1.2 eV to 18 meV or less, and matches the projectability-based choice to within about 2 meV on the remaining three.

title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
authors: Abrar Alotaibi & Moataz Ahmed

slides.hook: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing automated red-teaming methods either require privileged access unavailable in production, rely on manually engineered per-model templates, or optimize a single objective without population-level diversity. We present REPRO (Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimization), a pure black-box framework that discovers adversarial prompts through evolutionary optimization driven entirely by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: REPRO introduces two mechanisms absent from prior work, both isolated in a component ablation: semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, and Bayesian strategy selection via Thompson Sampling informed by structured failure analysis. We catalog REPRO's behavior on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, including GPT-5-nano, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Grok-4.1.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We therefore present this as a catalog of model coverage under one protocol rather than a head-to-head ranking, and develop both qualifications in the paper.

slides.content: The properties of dust grains are expected to change significantly in dense molecular clouds due to shielding from interstellar radiation and increased frequency of grain-grain and grain-gas collisions. title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
authors: Yanzhe Zhao & Yongzhang Ji

slides.hook: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns, but repeated candidate evaluation makes large analyses expensive.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: HP-GSBS is an open-source Python package that reorganizes the search around reusable interval contributions and correlation statistics. Streaming candidate reduction and local refinement further reduce repeated work; CPU, PyTorch CUDA and Triton backends share sequential segmentation decisions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across seven controlled workloads with two realizations each, median same-input speedups range from 154 to 1730 times. All 168 optimized executions reproduce original boundaries and selected state counts, with maximum absolute t-distance difference 1.88times10^{-11}.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By removing redundant computation, HP-GSBS makes established neural-state segmentation faster while preserving its scientific outputs.

slides.hook: EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. slides.hook: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs.

slides.hook: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We ask the reverse question: when an LLM is confident, consistent, and wrong, do users bend towards it? In a within-subjects experiment, 32 participants learned up to five science topics by chatting with five assistants built on the same model (GPT-5-mini). Unknown to participants, each assistant's briefing had 0, 25, 50, 75, or 100% of its facts replaced by plausible falsehoods, and every assistant spoke with full confidence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A surprise quiz after each topic offered the correct fact, the planted falsehood, and two distractors, with a confidence rating for every answer. Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10, and the planted option was chosen on 60% of falsified items against 11% of correctly taught ones (odds ratio 12.5).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We introduce a baseline-corrected Human Deference Index to quantify this human-side sycophancy and argue that trustworthiness is a property of the human-AI pair, that sycophancy evaluations should measure both directions, and that learning interfaces must make reliability legible claim by claim.

slides.hook: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na_xTMO_2, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na_xTM_{0.5}TM'_{0.5}O_2 oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti^{3+/4+} < Mn^{3+/4+} < Co^{3+/4+} < Ni^{2+/3+} < Fe^{3+/4+}, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO_6 octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn^{3+} and Ni^{3+} through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
authors: Brian Coyle, Jonathan H. Fetherolf et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Randomised quantum simulation algorithms such as qDRIFT reduce circuit depth by replacing deterministic product formulas with stochastic compilations, but achieving high accuracy can require many steps.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In vanilla qDRIFT, Hamiltonian terms are sampled with probabilities proportional to their coefficient magnitudes. We propose StateDRIFT, a variant of qDRIFT which optimises its sampling distribution to estimate time-evolved quantities using knowledge of the initial state and target observable, with a provable truncation bound that keeps qDRIFT's guarantees.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The distribution at each depth is chosen by solving an optimisation problem targeting bias and/or variance. StateDRIFT can significantly reduce the bias and variance of estimators, and hence circuit depth, which we test on short-time dynamics of lattice models and molecules under Jordan-Wigner up to 18 qubits.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: StateDRIFT involves measuring observables and commutators on the initial state, so we propose two practical ways to estimate these: classical surrogates such as tensor networks, and classical shadows, which recover most or all of the saving from exact oracles in the systems tested.

title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control
authors: Fanxing Li, Yuxiang Huang et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Tasks such as quadrotor dynamic-gate racing require agents to anticipate external motion while maintaining precise high-frequency control.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: World-model-based reinforcement learning provides a natural solution by learning latent dynamics for future imagination, yet it often entangles environmental evolution and the robot's own dynamics in a single learned rollout, where model bias can affect policy optimization efficiency. title: Quantum Broker: QoS-Aware Distribution of Quantum Computations
authors: Giuseppe Bisicchia, Alessandro Bocci et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. This paper presents the Quantum Broker, an open-source and provider-agnostic framework for Quality-of-Service-aware quantum execution management.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The framework operationalizes shot-wise distribution by exploiting the statistical independence of quantum measurement shots to dispatch a single circuit across multiple heterogeneous QPUs according to user-defined constraints and optimization objectives. It combines a modular execution architecture, interchangeable backend-profiling strategies, and the Quantum QoS Specification Language (QQSpec), a declarative language for expressing QoS requirements.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Overall, the Quantum Broker provides an extensible execution-management layer for engineering portable, reproducible, and QoS-aware quantum software over fragmented quantum cloud infrastructures.

title: Algorithm Modelization: Transforming Optimization Algorithms into Evolvable Intelligence
authors: Jian Yao, Zhiyao Zhang et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Can algorithms be learned and evolved as models, rather than repeatedly redesigned as programs? We explore this question by introducing Algorithm Modelization, a new paradigm that turns iterative algorithms into trainable models.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Its central idea is to regard algorithm execution trajectories as computational experience: by learning how algorithmic states evolve over iterations, a model can internalize the knowledge embodied in existing algorithms, reproduce their computational behaviors, and further evolve beyond them through training. As a first realization of this paradigm, we modelize iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, where preceding generations constitute the computational context for generating the next population.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We develop a dimension-independent population-temporal architecture to capture both population interactions and iterative dynamics, together with an imitation-to-surpassing learning framework that first acquires algorithmic knowledge from heterogeneous teachers and then improves the resulting optimizer directly through optimization feedback. The modelized optimizer consequently goes beyond reproducing individual algorithms: it consolidates heterogeneous search knowledge into a single trainable model, achieves stronger optimization capability through subsequent improvement, and generalizes its acquired knowledge across problems and substantially larger unseen dimensions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results establish a promising path from manually designed algorithms toward general algorithm models that learn, generalize, and evolve from computational experience.

title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
authors: Ivan Moloshnikov, Dmitry Kunitsyn et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
authors: Hanqing Zhang, Jie Bao et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) increasingly rely on large-scale transcriptomic pretraining, yet expanding pretraining data can yield diminishing gains while substantially increasing computational cost.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our data scaling analyses showed that incorporating biological knowledge, including cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information, provided additional scaling dimension than simply increasing data size. Motivated by this observation, we present scKITE, a simple yet effective scFM that integrates cell-annotation and gene-regulatory supervision into a shared transcriptomic Transformer encoder through lightweight auxiliary decoders.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: La-Ribo: RNA Co-Design via Geometry-Latent Flow Matching

slides.hook: RNA function arises from the coupling of nucleotide sequence and three-dimensional structure, motivating their joint design.

slides.hook: Biomolecular therapeutics often start from known sequences and require targeted editing to improve multiple properties while satisfying hard biochemical and manufacturability constraints.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, existing generative methods do not jointly support multi-objective optimization, hard feasibility, and sequence editing in discrete, variable-length biological spaces. In this work, we introduce Pareto-Constrained Molecule Editing (pCoMole), a framework built on discrete flow matching that steers a pre-trained Edit Flow toward user-specified preferences while enforcing terminal feasibility.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: pCoMole defines a feasibility-gated terminal distribution using an augmented Tchebycheff utility and realizes the resulting preference tilt through a Doob-h transform of the underlying edit process. To make this construction practical, we approximate the required harmonic function using short Monte Carlo rollouts over candidate edits, yielding an efficient guided editor with provable preference consistency.

slides.content: Together, pCoMole enables constraint-aware, Pareto-aligned editing of biomolecular sequences in discrete, variable-length spaces.

slides.hook: In quantum mechanics, conservation laws are usually understood only statistically and only in the context of unitary evolution: during such evolution, if an observable commutes with the Hamiltonian, its expectation value and Born-rule probability distribution remain unchanged.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Individual measurement outcomes, however, disrupt even this weak form of statistical conservation. Recently, though, it has been argued that a stronger, non-statistical form of conservation, valid at the level of individual measurement outcomes, can be recovered.

slides.content: The proposal relies on the claim that any superposition of eigenstates of a conserved quantity must ultimately be prepared relative to another physical system, which serves as the relevant reference frame and remains correlated with the system being prepared. On this enlarged description, the change observed in the measured system is claimed to be exactly compensated by an opposite change in the preparer, thereby restoring conservation at the level of individual measurement outcomes.

slides.content: We show that the proposed mechanism is not adequately justified and, moreover, does not establish conservation in individual measurement outcomes as claimed.

title: Universal Construction and Exact Self-Reproduction in Ternary McCulloch-Pitts Networks
authors: Charles C. Norton

slides.hook: A fixed network of McCulloch-Pitts threshold units with weights in {-1,0,1} can hold other threshold networks in its state and run them: the state is a ring of banks of records, each record a unit of a stored network, and each step evaluates one record.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We use such a network to carry out von Neumann's universal construction and self-reproduction exactly. As a cellular automaton keeps its rule, the fixed network keeps its weights, and what reproduces is a stored network.

slides.content: A constructor of 143 records reads the description of a network from its tape, builds that network in the next bank, copies the description onto the next tape and hands control to what it built; started on its own description, it rebuilds itself, weights included, in every generation. The scheme scales to a universal computer.

title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
authors: Deng Pan, Xue-Jian Gao et al. (11 researchers)

slides.hook: Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve 100% case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and 98.28% on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of 1.334times over the baseline. Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by 46.6% over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.

title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
authors: Hayden Prairie, Jacob M. Ryan et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.

slides.hook: Ophthalmic clinical decision support requires fast, accurate, and privacy-preserving inference, yet autoregressive large language models (LLMs) incur substantial latency and computational overhead for decisions among predefined actions.

title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech
authors: Shahryar G. Namdari, Francesco Iacomi et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. We evaluate the approach on the Chisco imagined speech dataset across five subjects, reporting Top-k accuracy, macro-F1, and balanced pairwise matching accuracy (2v2).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these findings suggest that EEG-language alignment can retain comparable fixed-intent decoding while supporting similarity-based retrieval, intrinsic reliability ranking, and evaluation of broader semantic structure.

slides.hook: The M-sigma correlation of inactive galaxies plays a crucial role in estimating the black hole mass (MBH) in active galactic nuclei (AGN): 1) it is used to calibrate the reverberation mapping (RM) method; 2) the RM is the basis of the single epoch method, the most-used technique to determine MBH of broad-line AGN; and 3) in narrow-line AGN, MBH is often directly inferred from the M-sigma correlation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The main goal of this work is to test whether the M-sigma relation calibrated from inactive galaxies can be reliably applied to a local AGN population spanning Seyfert 1, Seyfert 2, and hidden broad-line region galaxies (HBLRs), and whether the resulting AGN relation has sufficient predictive power to be used as an indirect MBH estimator. To investigate this hypothesis, we used the 12 micron AGN sample, a local representative and largely unbiased sample.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Since a substantial fraction of this sample has good-quality NuSTAR data, we estimated their MBH with the X-ray scaling method, which works for any AGN accreting at moderate or high level. We find that the M-sigma correlation of the 12 micron AGN sample is different from the one obtained with inactive galaxies and has a substantial scatter.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Finally, we find suggestive evidence that Seyfert 1 and HBLRs have similar and systematically higher Eddington ratios than Seyfert 2 galaxies.

title: Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet
authors: Xiaoqing Lian, Pei Liu et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Comprehensively characterizing cellular diversity is critical for understanding tissue development, identifying disease-associated populations and investigating gene programmes linked to specialized functions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Advances in single-cell profiling reveal additional cell-specific transcripts and molecular associations, yet many foundation models represent only a restricted portion of this increasingly rich molecular information. Here we present CellNet, which enables panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes by integrating DNA-derived gene identities and measured RNA expression in a shared image representation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Pretrained on 231 million cell profiles spanning 40 species, CellNet improves rare-population and condition-associated state recognition in evaluated cohorts while retaining competitive general cell representations. It predicts withheld coding-gene expression and selected non-coding targets in total-RNA data, and recovers lineage-specific expression patterns in spatial measurements.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results establish CellNet as a scalable framework for interpreting cellular diversity through increasingly comprehensive transcriptomic measurements.

title: Agentic AI uncovers conserved cross-tissue protein co-abundance programs inaccessible to single-dataset analysis
authors: Runyu Guan, Dehao Wu et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Protein co-abundance clusters preserved across tissues can reveal shared disease mechanisms and candidate therapeutic targets, particularly when proteins implicated in organ-confined diseases converge in peripheral or accessible tissues.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, previous cross-tissue studies have focused on biologically pre-selected tissue pairs, leaving most possible combinations and non-obvious relationships unexplored. We present an LLM-agent framework for large-scale, evidence-grounded comparison of tissue-specific protein co-abundance networks.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The framework constructs tissue networks, derives pairwise consensus clusters, and integrates evidence from expression atlases, protein interaction and complex databases, pathway annotations, disease catalogues, and literature. Applied to all 820 pairwise combinations of 41 human tissues and fluids, it identified 1,833 conserved co-abundance clusters across 406 tissue pairs.

slides.hook: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system.

slides.content: Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state.
