slides.hook: Cosmological cross-correlation analyses are commonly based on two-point statistics, which are optimal for Gaussian random fields but do not capture all relevant information in the presence of non-Gaussianity, which is ubiquitous in late-time cosmic fields.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This motivates investigations of higher order statistics, and one method is to use machine learning to construct a correlation-optimized tracer field that can utilize cross-correlation information beyond two-point statistics. slides.content: We train a 1D U-Net on paired simulated fields and study controlled cases based on Gaussian and log-normal random fields. slides.hook: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's ε hyperparameter.

title: Reciprocity coordinates a three-way trade-off in recurrent neural circuits
authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Mingyi Huang et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Biological neural circuits contain both unidirectional and reciprocal connections, but how reciprocity affects circuit computation remains unclear.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We varied reciprocity r{ho} across 21 levels in recurrent-network simulations while holding network size, connection density, and directed-edge count fixed. Low-reciprocity networks produced more diverse stimulus-driven activity and performed better on four continuous-input tasks, whereas higher reciprocity generally improved performance on three delayed-memory tasks.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Increasing reciprocity reduced online memory capacity and accelerated recovery from perturbations. A post-cue noise experiment showed that higher reciprocity suppressed internal noise propagation but made cue-evoked states less distinguishable, and component matching separated the contributions of cue separation and within-cue dispersion to readout robustness.

title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
authors: Sihan Yang, Jie Huang et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.

title: FlyHack: Stress-Testing Mechanistic Claims in a Connectome-Constrained Visual Model
authors: Aashish Dhawan

slides.hook: Connectome-constrained neural networks make biological components directly accessible to intervention, but their mechanistic conclusions can still depend on the comparison model, intervention, circuit representation and trained solution.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We stress-test these dependencies in flyvis, a emph{Drosophila} motion-vision model, using its 50-model ensemble, task-matched causal CNN controls and replicated interventions. At the level of model behaviour, three-level reverse-phi reversal in flyvis is strongly period- and velocity-dependent and also appears in task-matched CNNs; neither family reproduces the fly's stationary-sawtooth response.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Adversarial direction reversal requires a perturbation bound of 0.21--0.27 times stimulus contrast in flyvis versus 0.13--0.25 in CNNs, but the gap over a parameter-matched CNN largely closes for larger CNNs. At the level of mechanism, matching attribution to the intervention matters: for held-out-mean replacement, first-order edge attribution patching reaches pooled AUROC 0.970 and Spearman 0.872, versus 0.933 and 0.126 when its zero-aligned score is evaluated against the same ground truth.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results support a narrower use of connectome-constrained models: they make mechanistic hypotheses directly testable, but the resulting claims must be scoped to the model family, intervention, representation and trained solution.

title: HyCoSeq: Contextual Hyperbolic Representation Learning for Genomic Sequences
authors: Chenhao Zeng, Zhibin Pu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Hyperbolic geometry provides a natural inductive bias for genomic representation learning, but existing hyperbolic genomic models primarily use Lorentz convolutions to learn local sequence representations, while their residual pathways do not directly aggregate full Lorentz representations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We propose HyCoSeq, a contextual hyperbolic representation learning framework for genomic sequences. HyCoSeq incorporates weighted Lorentzian residual aggregation into multi-curvature Lorentz encoding, allowing full Lorentz representations to participate directly in geometry-consistent local aggregation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: It further introduces a bidirectional long short-term memory network that integrates information from both sequence directions to learn contextual relationships among local representations at different positions within a genomic sequence, thereby extending local hyperbolic convolutional encoding to sequence-level contextualized representations. Extensive experiments across diverse genomic tasks show that HyCoSeq outperforms existing hyperbolic baselines and, without large-scale genomic pretraining, achieves competitive performance against substantially larger pretrained DNA language models.

title: Chemical and geometric representation fidelity improves drug--target affinity prediction
authors: Yixiao Li, Yining Qian et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Predicting drug--target binding affinity (DTA) requires models to distinguish subtle chemical and structural determinants underlying molecular recognition.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although recent approaches increasingly incorporate richer drug and protein information, such information may be compressed, homogenized or discretized during representation construction, causing affinity-relevant distinctions to be lost before interaction modelling. We hypothesized that this representation-stage information loss constitutes an upstream bottleneck that cannot be reliably overcome by increasingly complex interaction predictors.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To test this hypothesis, we developed ReGeoDTA, a representation-preserving framework that maintains affinity-relevant chemical heterogeneity in molecular representations and continuous geometric relationships in protein structures. Across three benchmark datasets, ReGeoDTA consistently improved affinity prediction, and the proposed representation-preserving strategies retained their benefits across diverse DTA architectures.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings identify representation fidelity as an upstream design principle for accurate and generalizable drug--target affinity prediction, with potential implications for computational compound prioritization.

slides.hook: Ovarian follicle development has been modeled either by compartmental models, where developmental stages are represented by discrete compartments, or by physiologically structured population models (PSPMs), formulated as transport PDEs describing follicles along a continuous maturation variable.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

slides.content: Here, we introduce a class of ODE systems derived as finite-dimensional reductions of PSPMs via a perturbative moment closure. These systems provide backbone approximations of the structured dynamics, retaining key nonlinear mechanisms governing recruitment, selection for dominance, and atresia while projecting maturation onto macroscopic variables.

title: HPOQuest: A Rare-Disease Diagnostic Agent Using Active Phenotype Acquisition
authors: Kamilia Zaripova, Nassir Navab et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: More than 300 million people worldwide are affected by one of over 7,000 known rare diseases, yet diagnosis remains difficult because patients initially present with incomplete and heterogeneous phenotypes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present HPOQuest, a training-free framework for sequential phenotype acquisition in rare-disease diagnosis. Starting from a small set of observed patient phenotypes, HPOQuest maintains a probabilistic disease ranking and iteratively selects informative follow-up questions to support clinicians during patient assessment.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Confirmed phenotypes update the disease ranking, while all responses update the candidate question set. Across four benchmark cohorts, HPOQuest substantially improves diagnosis from sparse initial phenotypes, with gains of up to 30% points at Recall@1 and 45% points at Recall@5.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that sequential phenotype acquisition can substantially improve rare-disease diagnosis from limited initial clinical evidence.

title: Predictable performance is suboptimal, and what it means for model routing
authors: Guanhua Zhang & Moritz Hardt

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) differ in capabilities and costs, motivating routing methods that adaptively choose a model for each query.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These methods rely on performance prediction: given a query, estimate whether a model will answer it correctly. Most routing methods train separate predictors of candidate models' performance to guide model selection.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our work shows that performance prediction only beats a simple baseline when the candidate model is suboptimal on the task or the performance predictor adds significant capacity relative to the candidate model. Specifically, we take a model's self-confidence, the probability it assigns to its chosen answer, as a baseline and study how much a performance predictor can improve on it.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Cascading exhibits the same two patterns: predictor-based routing offers larger gains over confidence-based routing for more suboptimal models, and these gains diminish after finetuning.

title: Design and Analysis of Temporal Representations in Neural Networks
authors: Alban Colas-Gattepaille & Alexandre Muzy

slides.hook: The ability to represent temporal information is often hypothesized to underlie the efficiency and learning capabilities of biological neural networks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This motivates the development of spiking neural networks. However, it remains unclear how temporal information is actually represented in neural networks and how different forms of temporal representation affect performance and computational efficiency.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce the notion of the degree of temporal representation of a neural network, defined by whether its constituent functions (activation, learning, encoding, and decoding) explicitly manipulate time as a computational variable. This perspective yields a continuum ranging from non-temporal representations, where time does not explicitly appear as a computational variable in the network functions, to fully temporal representations, where computations explicitly operate on temporal variables.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We further analyze how temporal representations induce distinct forward and backward computational trajectories, leading to gradients that depend explicitly on the history of event times.

title: EEG Entrainment to Non-Speech Rhythmic Patterns Associated with Dimensions of Language Performance
authors: Francisco J. Martínez-Murcia, Nicolás J. Gallego-Molina et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Developmental dyslexia (DLX) affects 5-12% of the global population and impairs learning to read.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Its biological basis, particularly the difficulties observed in oral phonological tasks, remains debated. Entrainment, the coupling of brain oscillations to speech rhythms, is essential for encoding phonological representations.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We investigated whether brain entrainment to non-speech rhythms could predict DLX in 48 participants listening to white noise amplitude-modulated at rates matching Spanish speech units. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) signals yielded accurate DLX prediction for the 40 Hz stimulus using the Heights Ratio PAC measure (balanced accuracy 0.929, p = 0.0069, in the best case), indicating a stronger phonemic entrainment deficit in dyslexic individuals.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: In conclusion, our methodology identifies dyslexia-specific entrainment patterns near language-associated brain regions, together with compensatory entrainment in right-hemisphere areas.

title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks
authors: Francesco Panetta, Federico Di Valerio et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing, but they still suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This work investigates the integration of Experience Packing and Replay (EPR) as a memory-efficient continual learning strategy for deep SNNs under low-latency constraints. The proposed framework combines Batch Normalization Through Time stabilized VGG9 SNNs with Spike Activation Maps (SAM), which provide forward-only explanations based on spike activity.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: These explanations are temporally aggregated into spatial attention maps and used to select the most informative image patches for replay, instead of storing full images. Experiments on Split CIFAR10 and Split CIFAR100 show that SAM-guided EPR improves the accuracy-memory trade-off under tight memory budgets, and remains competitive while requiring substantially less storage.

title: Shift-aware score transport for privacy auditing without retraining
authors: Yaohong Yang, Gauri Pradhan et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Privacy auditing empirically assesses privacy leakage by using membership inference attacks to establish lower bounds on privacy loss.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We consider an observational auditing setting in which the auditor cannot insert canaries, control data inclusion, or retrain the target model, and must instead rely on fixed sets of known members and non-members. This setting is relevant for large deployed models or when retraining is restricted by computational or access constraints.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this case, non-members available for auditing may differ in distribution from the training data, causing membership-inference scores to be skewed due to the distribution shift. We address this problem by estimating the counterfactual in-distribution non-member score distribution using the available out-of-distribution (OOD) non-members.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Across multiple datasets with distribution shifts, our method yields substantially more stable privacy estimates while retaining tighter lower bounds than baselines.

title: HETDEX [OII] galaxies at z le 0.48: Growth of structures from power spectrum multipoles
authors: Jeongin Moon, Eiichiro Komatsu et al. (12 researchers)

slides.hook: We use the monopole and quadrupole power spectra of [ion{O}{2}]-emitting galaxies in the HETDEX Public Data Release 1 to constrain the growth of cosmic structures at zle0.48.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We interpret the power spectra using a simulation-based model built from the Mucho-Uchuu-1G N-body simulation. The best-fit model reproduces the observed power spectra remarkably well up to k_mathrm{max}=0.7~h~mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}, and goodness-of-fit tests confirm that the HETDEX [ion{O}{2}] clustering is consistent with the textit{Planck} flat ΛCDM cosmology.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We test the general relativity (GR) prediction for the linear growth index, γsimeq 0.55. When the Alcock-Paczyński parameters are held fixed at their fiducial values, we find consistency with the GR prediction, γ=0.55pm 0.05.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish HETDEX [ion{O}{2}] galaxies as a competitive, independent low-redshift probe of the growth of structures and motivate future full cosmological inference.

title: Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization for Selective Combinatorial Optimization Problems
authors: Haohui Zhang, Xinyu Hu et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Reinforcement learning has emerged as an effective approach for combinatorial optimization, but most existing methods focus on problems such as the Travelling Salesperson Problem (TSP) in which all elements must be served.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Selective combinatorial optimization problems (SCOPs), including the Orienteering Problem (OP), Prize-Collecting TSP (PCTSP), Stochastic PCTSP and Knapsack Problem (KP), additionally require selecting which elements to include. This selection creates sampled solutions with substantially different objective values, yet standard preference optimization reduces such comparisons to binary rankings and discards the magnitude of these differences.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization (RWPO), a pairwise training objective that incorporates reward-gap information into preference learning. For candidate trajectories sampled from the same instance, RWPO weights each preference loss according to the normalized difference in their rewards, assigning greater training emphasis to comparisons that represent larger improvements in solution quality.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The results demonstrate that preserving reward-gap information can substantially improve preference-based learning for selective combinatorial optimization and support generalization to large-scale instances.

title: Reconstruction-Aware Cryo-EM Particle Picking
authors: Riku Itsuji, Yuanhao Wang et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) determines the structures of proteins and macromolecular assemblies at near-atomic resolution, and the final 3D reconstruction depends on extracting a clean particle stack from noisy micrographs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This extraction decomposes into three sub-tasks, namely particle picking, contamination removal, and 2D class selection. Each of them, however, is trained and evaluated in isolation, and none is optimized for the reconstruction.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We instead integrate the three sub-tasks into a single pipeline posed against downstream reconstruction quality. We instantiate the pipeline with a state-of-the-art component for each sub-task, CryoTransformer picking permissively, MicrographCleaner masking contamination, and CryoSift selecting 2D classes by a continuous quality score, and close the loop with a fine-tuning step that returns the surviving particles to the picker.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We also show that the best 2D F1 is not the best resolution, so particle selection is better treated as one reconstruction-aware pipeline judged by the map it delivers.

title: A Little Red Dot emerging from a nitrogen-rich UV-luminous galaxy with Very Massive Stars
authors: Alberto Torralba, Jorryt Matthee et al. (16 researchers)

slides.hook: JWST is revealing abundant populations of high-z galaxies with unforeseen properties: UV-luminous galaxies with high nitrogen enrichment, populations of very massive stars (VMSs; >100 M_odot), and early forms of massive black hole growth such as the Little Red Dots (LRDs).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present all these phenomena appearing simultaneously in COLA1, a luminous (M_{rm UV}=-21.3) galaxy at z=6.6. New NIRSpec medium-resolution data reveal a blue UV continuum (β_{rm UV}=-2.5) with strong emission lines including NIV] lambda1486, stellar P Cygni profiles, and broad HeII lambda1640.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We fit the UV with stellar population models, and find that the models including VMSs (limited to 300 M_odot) are statistically preferred. The best-fit stellar population has M_*approx10^8 M_odot, and a young age of 2.4pm0.8 Myr.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We speculate that runaway collisions of massive stars in a dense stellar cluster may have lead to the seeding of an intermediate-mass black hole resulting in the formation of an LRD.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Disentangling Decomposition from Typed-State Quality Assurance in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
authors: Maria Gabriela Alves Zuppardo & Vinicius Cardoso Garcia

comments.author: Dr. Kenji Sato (RIKEN)
comments.text: Has this benchmark been cross-validated across independent hardware setups?

replies.author: Marcus Vance (Oxford)
replies.text: Yes, replicated across both A100 clusters and TPU v5e pods with <1.5% variance.

slides.hook: Multi-agent LLM pipelines are often credited with gains in software engineering tasks, but it is rarely clear whether a gain stems from the typed contract between agents or from the specialized prompts that decomposition enables.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study this attribution problem in Requirements Engineering, comparing three architectures for classifying requirements as functional or non-functional and then prioritizing them with MoSCoW: a single-call baseline; a two-call variant that reuses the pipeline's specialized prompts but passes an unvalidated intermediate; and a pipeline with a Pydantic-validated typed state. The 18 conditions cover PROMISE NFR+ (625 requirements), three locally hosted small language models, and two languages.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The F1 gain over the baseline is associated with the two-call, specialized-prompt variant (up to +0.075), whereas the typed state adds a small difference (-0.003 to +0.013) that is significant in one of six comparisons. Beyond accuracy, the typed pipeline contains out-of-range model outputs at the agent boundary, while the unvalidated variant fails later and drops the requirement, and it shows a small, reproducible increase in inter-model MoSCoW consistency whose cause our design cannot isolate.

slides.content: The implementation and replication package are archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23380444).

slides.hook: Molecular profiling from routine histopathology could expand access to precision oncology when sequencing is unavailable, tissue is limited, or training cohorts are small.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We developed a hybrid quantum-classical strategy that replaces softmax attention in a transformer for histopathology-based gene expression prediction with a quantum-derived doubly stochastic matrix (QDSM). Across 29 cancer cohorts from The Cancer Genome Atlas and an independent pancreatic cancer cohort from the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium, QDSM attention produced selective gains, with the largest relative improvements in smaller, data-limited cohorts, including adrenocortical carcinoma and uveal melanoma.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Rather than improving transcriptome-wide performance uniformly, QDSM redistributed predictive accuracy across genes and pathways, improving biologically relevant targets in some tumor contexts while worsening others. In adrenocortical carcinoma, preferentially improved genes were enriched for adverse overall-survival associations, linking enhanced molecular inference to prognostically relevant biology.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings position QDSM attention as a context- and target-dependent strategy for image-based molecular profiling and molecular triage when direct testing is unavailable, incomplete, or impractical.

slides.hook: Recent advances in biomolecular structure prediction have enabled accurate modelling of increasingly complex molecular systems.

slides.content: However, nucleic acid structure prediction remains challenging because of conformational flexibility and the limited availability of high-quality 3D structural data. title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
authors: Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

title: Tunable flat bands from a parent chiral Hamiltonian
authors: Jun-Hyung Bae, Alexei Andreanov et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Systems with flat bands are interesting as they potentially host many exotic quantum phenomena that would be hard to observe in usual systems with dispersive bands.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Multiple approaches were developed to construct flat band systems, with most of them requiring fine-tuning and/or solving a challenging inverse-eigenvalue problem. title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
authors: A. Jian Yang, An Huang et al. (177 researchers)

slides.hook: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training, combining SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD across various scaffolds to integrate complementary training signals and strengthen agentic coding capabilities. Furthermore, model merging combines different experts and checkpoints from different stages while mitigating conflicts among their parameter updates.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The resulting IQuest-Q1 demonstrates capabilities in both coding and general tasks. We release IQuest-Q1 as an open-source model to support community research and development.

authors: Mullosharaf K. Arabov & Svetlana S. Khaybullina

slides.hook: Bashkir is a low-resource agglutinative language written in Cyrillic and remains poorly represented in modern LLMs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present an open resource suite and a systematic benchmark of adaptation methods: the Bashkir Web Corpus (71,567 documents, 46.9M tokens, 16 sources) and three labelled datasets for binary, multiclass and multilabel text classification; the benchmark covers the first two. Experiments use eight architectures (82M-8B: DistilGPT2, GPT-2 base/medium, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B, mBERT, XLM-R) and three adaptation groups (full fine-tuning, QLoRA, in-context learning), plus continual pretraining (CPT).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: (1) QLoRA on 3.8-8B models outperforms encoder-only fine-tuning on binary classification: YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B with CPT reaches macro-F1 0.748 vs 0.653 (XLM-R) and 0.650 (mBERT); pairwise differences are significant after Holm correction (p<0.001). (2) YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B significantly outperforms Mistral-7B and Phi-3-mini on multiclass classification, BPB and native-speaker ratings (mean 3.28 vs 2.52 and 2.22; n=100; alpha=0.69-0.77; p<0.05); on binary classification its QLoRA advantage is not significant (p>=0.084).

slides.hook: Magnetic interaction between astrophysical objects can play an important role and produce electromagnetic radiation in various systems, ranging from planet-moon and star-planet systems to binary compact objects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We extend our previous numerical study of an ideal magnetized plasma flowing past a conducting sphere to the case where the sphere is magnetized. Such a flow generates magnetic disturbances and produces a drag force on the sphere.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We examine the drag coefficient as a function of the strength and orientation of the conductor's internal magnetic field relative to the background magnetic field. We find that a strong internal magnetic field that is aligned with the background field significantly enhances the drag coefficient compared to the unmagnetized case; this enhancement is related to the increased magnetic flux that connects the conductor and the open, external field region.

slides.content: Our results suggest that magnetic interaction may play a larger role in orbital evolution of some binary systems than previously expected.

slides.hook: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To evaluate and improve AI assistants in such settings, we need user simulators that faithfully follow complex user intents while exhibiting realistic conversational behavior. Existing approaches manifest a trade-off: prompted assistants can follow complex user intents but lack behavioral fidelity, while specialized user simulators better approximate conversational behavior but struggle to remain faithful to complex intents.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) recipe that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. A crucial contribution of the method is operationalizing naturalness with a lightweight discriminator trained in an alternating, adversarial loop with the user simulator.

title: Exploring Optimal Parameters for Ligand-Based Virtual Screening in Early Drug Discovery
authors: Temitope Sobodu, Victor Chibuzor Johnson et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Ligand-based virtual screening depends on choices that are often treated as implementation details, including the similarity threshold, fingerprint setting and atom-invariant scheme.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We examined how these choices altered the composition of ranked searches against the Enamine library for four aminergic reference ligands: atomoxetine, bupropion, mirtazapine and venlafaxine. Candidate sets were evaluated by compound-weighted scaffold novelty, normalized Shannon scaffold diversity and three computational estimates of synthetic accessibility.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We first identified ligand-specific operating points along cumulative Tanimoto-ranked searches. We then compared five extended-connectivity fingerprint settings at matched retrieval depths and compared ECFP4 with the feature-class analogue FCSFP4.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results support a staged screening design in which a pooled default is followed by ligand-specific calibration and expert review.

title: RecallGS: Geometry-Grounded Recall for Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting
authors: Thanh-Khoi Nguyen, Thien-Phuc Tran et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables open-vocabulary scene understanding from streaming observations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, existing methods recover geometric context missing from image-derived semantic features using an additionally learned 3D network, incurring extra training and runtime overhead. We observe that such geometric-semantic evidence may already exist in the agent's observation history and can be retrieved rather than learned.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Based on this insight, we introduce RecallGS (Geometry-Grounded Recall for Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting), a lightweight, training-free mechanism that treats past observations as a non-parametric geometric-semantic prior. RecallGS follows a recall-ground-fuse pipeline: CLIP retrieves relevant observations, alpha-compositing weights identify geometrically supported views, and aggregate their semantic features over each Gaussian's rendered footprint.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On ScanNet and ScanNet++, RecallGS achieves strong semantic segmentation performance at 2.48 FPS, demonstrating that geometric-semantic context can be effectively recovered from observation history without an additional learned 3D branch.

title: PyGPLA: A Python Package for Generalized Phase Locking Analysis
authors: Amir Khani, Christian Beste et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Spike-field couplings measure the links between neuronal spiking and local field potential (LFP) and provide a tool to study how neural populations coordinate activity across spatial and temporal scales.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While modern high-density electrophysiology enables the simultaneous recording of numerous LFP channels and neuronal units, this massive scale poses significant statistical and computational challenges for conventional pairwise coupling analyses. The number of channel-unit comparisons grows rapidly, and a coherent population-level structure can be obscured by high-dimensional coupling matrices.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Generalized Phase Locking Analysis (GPLA) addresses this challenge by organizing spike-triggered LFP phase information into a complex coupling matrix and extracting dominant low-rank modes. These modes summarize whether a population is coupled to the field, which channels and units contribute to the coupling, and how their relative phases are organized.

slides.content: Designed for straightforward integration into existing neural data analysis pipelines, PyGPLA supports multivariate spike-LFP coupling analysis, from coupling estimation and interpretation to significance assessment using analytical and surrogate-based tests.

title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
authors: Haotian Dong, Marek Biesiada et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat ΛCDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered H_0 from 74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20} to 71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18} mathrm{km,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}} in the forward analysis and from 60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97} to 63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93} mathrm{km,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}} in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.

title: PQ-Vault: Provably Quantum-Safe Asset Custody for Unmodified Ethereum
authors: Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: A quantum computer could recover the key of any Ethereum account whose public key appears on chain.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We prove that no sidechain or bridge that leaves Ethereum's rules unchanged can protect such accounts: their funds must move into a contract whose release condition relies only on quantum-safe primitives. We design emph{PQ-Vault}, a custody system for unmodified Ethereum combining this vault, a quantum-safe proof-of-stake sidechain whose checkpoints carry compact certificates, and an optimistic dispute protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We give the first security proof of compact certificates against quantum attackers and a matching attack: with classically chosen parameters, the guarantee falls from 128 to about 60 bits, and a simple rule restores it. We show that a common seed-update rule in hash-chain proof of stake lets an attacker steer chosen slots and profit from splitting its stake, and give an election whose steering gain and inclusion delay are provably bounded against quantum attackers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: For 65,536 validators, a certificate is 0.8 MB, 260 times smaller than all signatures, and verifies in about 20 ms; the vault accepts a checkpoint for about 420,000 gas.

title: manylp: reproducible, exact, and batched linear programming for genome-scale dynamic flux balance analysis
authors: Fabio Cumbo

slides.hook: Dynamic flux balance analysis (dFBA) and its community, spatial and ensemble variants predict microbial metabolism by solving one linear program (LP) per species and time step, often 10^6 to 10^8 LPs per study.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These LPs share their constraint matrix and objective and differ only in their bounds, yet general-purpose solvers treat each one independently, and GPU first-order solvers struggle with the degenerate, badly scaled matrices of genome-scale models. Moreover, metabolic optima are usually faces rather than vertices, so solvers return arbitrary flux vectors and dFBA predictions depend on the solver used.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present manylp, a batched solver for such bounds-parametric LP families that returns certified vertex solutions. Building on the bunching technique of stochastic programming, manylp caches optimal bases and certifies whole batches with one dense matrix product per basis on CPUs or GPUs; LPs outside the cached critical regions are re-solved by a warm-started lexicographic dual simplex, and new bases are propagated across the batch.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

slides.hook: Relativistic ray-tracing algorithms serve as indispensable numerical tools for investigating gravitational theories and high-energy astrophysics.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this paper, we develop and release SpinOctopus, a versatile relativistic ray-tracing code tailored for arbitrary axisymmetric spacetimes, powered by a Fortran/Python hybrid architecture and OpenMP multi-threading acceleration. This numerical toolkit is capable of simulating timelike orbits and their corresponding light curves, null geodesics, as well as black hole images illuminated by a wide array of phenomenological sources, including geometrically thin and thick accretion disks, geometrically thin tilted disks, relativistic jets, spherically symmetric accretion flows, and point sources.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To execute these tasks, users are solely required to specify the covariant metric tensor of the target spacetime and the simulation parameters within a dedicated configuration file. Benefiting from our customized adaptive step-size strategy for geodesic integration, SpinOctopus achieves an impressive processing efficiency of sim 800 rays per second per thread on an Intel Core i7-14700 platform when simulating geometrically thick accretion disk images.

slides.content: Additional capabilities, such as simulating Fe Kα fluorescent line profiles and geometrically thick tilted accretion disk images, will be introduced in future releases of the framework.

title: Agri-SCHOLAR: Simulation-Grounded In-Season Rolling Advisories for Agricultural Crops Using LLM-Bounded Optimization
authors: Geetha Charan, Vedant Balasubramaniam et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Existing agricultural advisories to farmers suffer from several limitations: (a) remain largely expert-driven, (b) do not adequately account for in-season weather, and (c) do not scale to individual farms.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this paper, our objective is to close these gaps by developing Agri-SCHOLAR (Simulation-Grounded Crop Harvest Optimization with LLM-Guided In-Season Advisory Rollouts). Agri-SCHOLAR is a rolling, in-season advisory framework that issues, at intervals of every few days or every week, a personalized advisory using the following information: soil and crop properties, observed weather to date, short-range forecast of weather, and a season extrapolation of weather based on historical analogs.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The novelty and depth of Agri-SCHOLAR lies in each advisory being produced by a closed-loop system which couples multiple LLM agents with a powerful crop simulator (such as APSIM in our case). The simulator crucially serves as an evaluation oracle.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We conduct a detailed 11-year analysis of the maize crop in two selected locations of South Asia and show that Agri-SCHOLAR consistently outperforms the region's standard packages of practice and satisfactorily addresses the limitations of existing agricultural advisories.

title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO_3)_n/(LaNiO_3)_m superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts

slides.hook: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO_3)_n/(LaNiO_3)_m superlattices, with (n,m) = (1,1), (2,2) and (2,4), from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Charge transfer drives the system towards the V^{4+} and Ni^{2+} configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting C-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with a^-b^+c^- or a^-b^-c^- octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a d-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling.

Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen 2p states through p-d covalency.

title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
authors: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Amine Ahriche et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity v_wto 1.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We generalize this treatment to arbitrary v_w< 1, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. We first extend the analytical trapping-equation approach to finite-thickness boosted kink profiles for both elastic and inelastic collisions, then go beyond this by numerically solving the full Klein-Gordon equation without assuming SO(1,1) symmetry or thin walls, across a broad grid of v_w and potential shapes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We find the analytical generalization underestimates the true efficiency factor by orders of magnitude away from v_wto 1, and provide new semi-analytic fit functions consisting of a power-law continuum plus a resonance peak, which reproduce the main spectral features of the numerical results across the parameter range studied. Applying these to a toy dark sector model, we show particle production is strongly suppressed as v_w decreases from unity, enhanced for lighter produced particles, and that the relative contribution from the oscillatory peak differs from prior runaway-regime estimates.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We also discuss limitations of the trapping equation and the off-shell effective-action truncation underlying this formalism.

title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
authors: Yen-Ku Liu, Hongjie Chen et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and transfer-learning settings. We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show that time-series dataset similarity is task-dependent, and that learned metric integration provides a stronger proxy for downstream transfer behavior than manually selecting one similarity metric.

title: CRANE: Post-Hoc Counterfactual Retrieval for Multimodal Classifiers
authors: Franco Rugolon, Ioanna Miliou et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Counterfactual explanation methods have been introduced for unimodal settings, with dedicated frameworks for tabular, timeseries, text, and image data, yet no post-hoc method has been designed for classifiers that learn from multimodal inputs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing explainability methods for multimodal classifiers apply modality-specific attribution independently to each input, which fails to yield coherent explanations and does not transfer to arbitrary pre-trained multimodal architectures. To address these shortcomings, we present CRANE (Counterfactual Retrieval via Agnostic Nearest-neighbour Explanations), the first post-hoc, model-agnostic framework for nearest-neighbour multimodal counterfactual generation that retrieves real training examples from the target class as candidate explanations, ensuring plausibility by construction.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across four heterogeneous datasets and three fusion strategies, we show that Multimodal Consensus Retrieval (MC-R), which intersects per-modality neighbour sets to identify instances jointly close to the query in every modality, emerges as the strongest multimodal strategy, achieving the best or joint-best outcome on three of four datasets while grounding every explanation in the joint training distribution. Unimodal strategies remain competitive when a single modality dominates the decision boundary.

slides.content: Unimodal strategies remain competitive when a single modality dominates the decision boundary.

title: Optical and near-infrared s-process abundance scales in the Galactic disc
authors: Andrés E. Piatti

slides.hook: A discrepancy has recently emerged between optical and near-infrared (NIR) s-process abundance scales, particularly for Neodymium (Nd).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We investigated this issue using a direct cross-match between the optical Gaia-ESO Survey (DR5) and NIR SDSS-V/MWM (DR19). While atmospheric parameters and Cerium (Ce) abundances exhibit robust 1:1 correlations, Nd displays a systematic X-shaped vertical stretching.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our analysis reveals that the SDSS-V pipeline expands intrinsic Nd variations by a scaling factor of 5.54 relative to the stable optical baseline. This phenomenon is driven by baseline compression in the APOGEE H-band, where the growth of the molecular forest (CN and CO) at high metallicities depresses the local continuum.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that the observed scale expansion is a spectroscopic artefact of line-blanketing rather than a physical Galactic trend.

title: Contrasting Crystal-Field and Dipolar Anisotropies in the Triangular Antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO_3)_2
authors: Cheng Su, Yonglin Wang et al. (13 researchers)

slides.hook: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO_3)_2 by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO_6 octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry Rbar{3} structure over the previously proposed Rbar{3}m model.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below T_{rm N}=0.1 K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the ab plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO_3)_2.

title: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents
authors: Ping-Lin Kuo, Suman Navaratnarajah et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: Modeling Tissue Detachment and Rupture Using an Extended Vertex Model with T2-inverse Transitions
authors: Shota Nishimoto & Yuichi Togashi

slides.hook: The vertex model is widely used to describe the mechanics of epithelial tissues, but its conventional formulation assumes that all cells remain tightly packed and always share edges with their neighbors, making it difficult to represent local detachment or gap formation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we propose a minimal extension of the vertex model that enables cell detachment by introducing a new topological transformation, T2-inverse, which acts as the inverse of the classical T2 transition. When the imbalance of forces acting on a vertex, quantified by a tension metric T, exceeds a threshold, the T2-inverse splits the vertex into multiple vertices and creates a closed polygon that is incorporated as a pseudo-cell.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This operation allows the model to represent the emergence and propagation of local detachment events. Using this framework, we simulate the stretching of a cell sheet and show that force-induced local detachments can accumulate to produce macroscopic tissue rupture.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that the proposed model extends the capability of the vertex model to describe tissue-level breakdown processes, including detachment and tearing, and provides a foundation for studying a broader class of epithelial mechanical phenomena.

slides.hook: The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

authors: Hongcan Guo, Yian Zhao et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. slides.hook: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

title: Stellar Loci X: Selection of Nitrogen-Rich Giants Using GALEX NUV and Synthetic SDSS Photometry
authors: Liangyu Yu, Haibo Yuan et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Nitrogen-rich (N-rich) field stars (likely second-generation escapees from globular clusters) provide a powerful, but currently sample-limited, probe of globular-cluster disruption in the Galactic halo.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We exploit the fact that enhanced NH, CN absorption depresses optical u band flux, while the near-ultraviolet (NUV) band is largely insensitive to nitrogen enhancement while remaining sensitive to overall metallicity. Combining GALEX NUV photometry with (synthetic) SDSS optical photometry, we construct a [Fe/H]-dependent stellar-locus model for giants and select significant redder u-g outliers as N-rich candidates.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: For a relaxed cut ([Fe/H] <= -0.8, 2 sigma) we identify 970 candidates, with an estimated completeness of 64-65% and purity of 41-62% from multiple validations. A stricter selection ([Fe/H] <= -1.0, 3 sigma) yields 220 candidates, with lower completeness (30-38%) but substantially higher purity (60-91%).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This scalable photometric approach enables systematic searches for N-rich halo stars and is well suited to forthcoming wide-field surveys such as CSST.

title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training
authors: Sebastian Loeschcke, Ivan Koryakovskiy et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Vector quantization (VQ), in particular lattice-based methods, offer strong rate-distortion trade-offs for low-bit large language models (LLMs), yet their behavior under quantization-aware training (VQ-QAT) remains poorly understood.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We scale lattice VQ-QAT to billion-parameter LLMs and multi-billion-token training regimes, and introduce SQuAT, a shape-gain VQ-QAT approach trained with a separate straight-through estimator (STE) for the shape and gain. SQuAT decomposes weights into direction and magnitude: normalized directions are quantized using an E_8-derived spherical codebook, while gains are quantized independently with low-bit scalar quantizers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that, unlike a standard STE applied to the full quantizer, which ignores the shape-gain structure, these separate STEs induce tangent-space updates for directions, yielding an implicit form of spherical (Riemannian) optimization. To enable scalability, we develop a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme, in which workers quantize disjoint weight blocks and communicate only discrete indices, reducing VQ-QAT training time by 12.8times and allowing us to scale it to 10B tokens.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Across instruction-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen3-4B, and base Qwen3-1.7B, SQuAT consistently outperforms standard VQ-QAT STE under identical quantizers and initialization, and achieves SOTA VQ-QAT accuracy.

title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
authors: Kang Wang, Siyu Chen et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both mathbf{k} and mathbf{q} space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.

slides.hook: Stellar-mass black holes (BHs) and neutron stars (NSs) observed by space-based gravitational-wave detectors offer constraints on binary stellar evolution that are complementary to those from ground- based detectors.

title: CellMSA: Context Modeling for Single-Cell Representation Learning
authors: Suyuan Zhao, Minghao Liu et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Single-cell transcriptomics enables profiling of cellular states at unprecedented resolution, but its high dimensionality, sparsity, and technical batch effects pose significant challenges for representation learning.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing single-cell foundation models typically encode each cell independently or only model cells from the same batch for denoising, thereby underutilizing the rich relational information across batches and cell types to model gene expression patterns. We argue that single-cell models can benefit from more informative cell-context modeling.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By comparing consistency and variation across cells, models can capture fine-grained gene-gene dependencies associated with cell states, which are essential for learning high-quality representations. Inspired by the use of multiple sequence alignment (MSA) context in protein modeling, we propose CellMSA, a single-cell representation learning framework that introduces an MSA-inspired inductive bias into transcriptomic modeling.

slides.hook: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a widely adopted technique for biomolecular structure determination.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The conventional cryo-EM computational pipeline first combines many particle images to reconstruct an electrostatic potential (ESP) map and then fits an atomic model to the recovered map. title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
authors: Jacques L. Pienaar, Eran Tal et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

slides.hook: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) offers substantial advantages to the fabrication of complex structural components, but its widespread adoption is slowed due to complexities in the process-structure-property relations which is the cause for uncertainty and drives risk.

slides.hook: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

slides.hook: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. title: 2Flow2SN: Dusty Supernova Cosmology with Photometric Redshifts and Contamination using Neural Simulation-Based Inference

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) demands statistical frameworks that simultaneously account for selection effects, photometric redshift uncertainties and non-Ia contamination at scale. We present FlowSN2, a modular statistical framework combining hierarchical Bayesian modelling and simulation-based inference (SBI), that reframes photometric SN cosmology from a regression task to a joint inference problem over light curve summaries and photometric redshifts.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By employing neural likelihood estimation via normalising flows, FlowSN2 approximates the data distributions of selected objects in a form that can be reused across different cosmological models, achieving amortisation over the Hubble diagram. slides.hook: The enumeration of chemical structures traditionally relies on graph- and group-theoretic techniques, including Pólya theory, in order to account for stereochemical symmetries.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These methods require bespoke derivations and methods for each molecular family of interest, and quickly become very intricate for nontrivial classes. In this work, we demonstrate that analytic combinatorics provides a unifying, highly extensible, and relatively simple framework for enumeration problems.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using the symbolic method, we show that classical counting problems, such as the enumeration of acyclic alkanes and other hydrocarbon families, can be naturally solved via concise combinatorial specifications of the class of interest. We first demonstrate the simplicity of this approach by replicating existing results in this framework, requiring significantly less work than previously necessary, and then extend these ideas to more complex problems, counting broader classes of molecules accounting for both tetrahedral and E/Z stereoisomerism, counting the distribution of stereogenic units, and enumerating achiral and meso compounds.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: All results are made reproducible through CombOL, our open-source software package which automates the translation of combinatorial specifications into generating functions using the symbolic method, and performs both univariate and multivariate enumeration.

slides.hook: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present.

title: Cross-species representation learning aligns mouse and human neural dynamics and tracks clinical drug efficacy
authors: Marko Tvrdic, Justin Richmond Domingo et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Preclinical models poorly predict human drug efficacy, particularly in neurological disorders.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Neural activity offers a uniquely rich source of translational information because it captures high-dimensional variation in nervous-system function that can be measured in both animals and humans. However, its high dimensionality makes it difficult to distinguish conserved disease-related features from variation arising from species, recording modality and experimental context.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we test whether shared neural dynamics can be identified directly from electrophysiology data by learning representations organized by biological state rather than species. We develop a dual-rule contrastive learning framework that aligns corresponding mouse and human states while preserving separation between distinct phenotypes.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these findings show the potential of cross-species neural representation learning to map heterogeneous human disease onto experimentally tractable preclinical states and assess whether interventions restore human-relevant circuit function.

authors: V. M. Kovalev & I. G. Savenko

comments.author: Dr. David Sterling (Caltech)

slides.hook: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.

title: Motif-Vocab: StatisticallyCalibrated Transcription-Factor-Identity Tokenization forGenomic Language Models
authors: Liangyu Li & Michael White

slides.hook: Tokenization is a central design choice in genomic language models, yet most deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) tokenizers use characters, fixed-length k-mers, or frequency-derived subwords without explicitly using prior information about the specificity of DNA-binding regulatory factors.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Motif-Vocab, a biologically informed tokenizer that scans both DNA strands for statistically calibrated motif matches, emits transcription-factor (TF) identity tokens, and applies nucleotide, k-mer, or byte-pair encoding (BPE) to unmatched sequence. Motif-specific null distributions put position-weight matrices (PWMs) of different lengths and degeneracy on a common significance scale; deterministic overlap rules make the representation reproducible.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In controlled Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) pretraining on two billion base pairs, real motif libraries outperform randomized-motif controls on 54 of 55 in-scope downstream tasks. On a motif-disjoint recognition task derived from DART-Eval Task 2, TF-specific tokens improve macro-F1 by 0.040 over a position-matched generic motif token and by 0.033 over a matched no-motif tokenizer (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.027--0.038).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Thus, Motif-Vocab is not a universal accuracy replacement; it is a targeted, interpretable inductive bias for motif-sensitive genomic modeling.

slides.content: We compare the DEM L36 superbubble with other Galactic and Magellanic Cloud superbubbles. slides.content: We perform a multi-wavelength morphological analysis to understand the shape and structure of the superbubble and X-ray spectral analysis to derive physical parameters of the hot gas. We find significant X-ray emission in DEM L36, dominated by a central bubble region mostly confined by a thin Hα filamentary shell.

slides.content: It is likely the DEM L36 superbubble was initially shaped by a central massive stellar population that has since dispersed and largely lost to supernovae, with smaller clusters at the edges of the swept-up shell being currently supplying the energy input.
