title: Multilingual Brain Decoding Reveals Shared Cortical Semantic Geometry
authors: Yi Guo, Yong Hu et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Human languages differ markedly in lexical and syntactic form yet can convey similar semantic content.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The neural basis of this cross-language semantic commonality remains unclear. Here we developed a multilingual brain decoding framework and analysed brain recordings from 227 participants spanning Chinese, English and French.

slides.content: We found that cortical semantic representations exhibited consistent semantic geometry relationships across languages and individuals, revealing a shared cortical semantic geometry. title: Orbital-angular-momentum control of localized Floquet states and photocurrents in Weyl semimetals
authors: Kyle S. Netherwood, Juan I. Aranzadi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Structured light provides a route to controlling quantum materials not only through its polarization, but also through its spatial profile and orbital angular momentum (OAM).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We develop real space theories of a Weyl semimetal driven by a vortex beam and show that optical OAM generates highly localized Floquet vortex states with pronounced circulating photocurrents. Exploiting cylindrical symmetry, we derive a Bogoliubov-de Gennes-like radial equation that resolves the states by angular momentum and reveals their evolution between the light-dressed Weyl cones.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: For Laguerre-Gaussian beams, the spatially varying drive produces strong hybridization between localized vortex states and bulk states. We complement this continuum description with a Wilson-lattice formulation that retains the full two-dimensional spatial structure and enables direct calculation of local photocurrents.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results establish optical OAM as a tunable control parameter for creating and manipulating localized current-carrying states in Weyl systems and provide a real-space framework for studying photocurrents generated by spatially structured light.

title: LLM Evolutionary Search Strategies Should be Compared by Tokens
authors: Tal Oved, Roi Pony et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: LLM evolutionary search is currently evaluated by counting proposals (candidate programs).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We demonstrate this metric hides the true cost of search, and redo the comparison using tokens. By replaying 600 logged runs across 5 tasks and 3 methods, we show that proposal costs vary wildly from 16k to 39k tokens.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In equal-proposal comparisons, this silently grants some methods up to 1.9x the compute of others, and gives evolution roughly 6x the budget of independent sampling. When we match token budgets, giving sampling six times more attempts, and remove scorer exploits, the evolutionary advantage largely vanishes.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Reporting tokens, not proposals and not model calls, fixes this and costs nothing, as the logs already hold them.

title: Where Should Physics Enter a Molecular Crystal Generator?
authors: Haocheng Tang, Junmei Wang et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Generative models make molecular crystal structure prediction fast, but their samples still exhibit geometric and packing violations.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Physics can be introduced during training, post-training, or inference, yet these choices are rarely compared with the generator and physical signal held fixed. We introduce CrystAF, an all-atom crystal flow-map generation model, and use it with the UMA interatomic potential to systematically study where physics should enter.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Post-training learns physical preferences directly into CrystAF, improving molecular validity and crystal packing while leaving sampling unchanged: physics is paid for once during training rather than repeatedly at deployment. In contrast, UMA relaxation is effective at repairing local clashes but makes generation 6--26times slower, while learning from relaxed targets provides little benefit.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, our results suggest a simple principle: learn reusable physical alignment into the generator, and reserve inference-time physics for residual constraints that are better corrected than learned.

authors: Haruki Nakayama, Satoyuki Tsukano et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Quantum Multi-Programming (QMP) enables the simultaneous execution of quantum circuits from multiple users on a single quantum chip in cloud quantum computing services.

title: Two dissociable axes of brain hierarchical dynamics track universal and population-specific effects of mindfulness
authors: Victor Oswald, David Zarka et al. (14 researchers)

slides.hook: How mental training reshapes the temporal architecture of large-scale brain dynamics and how these mechanisms differ between healthy and clinically vulnerable populations remains poorly understood.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Time-averaged neural measures collapse the multi-scale nature of brain activity, obscuring the dynamic processes through which behavioural interventions reorganise hierarchical brain function. Here, applying a sliding-window Temporal Irreversibility Index to source-reconstructed EEG across three complementary cohorts (n = 141), we decompose hierarchical brain trajectories into three orthogonal temporal descriptors and uncover two dissociable, mechanistically interpretable axes of intervention-induced plasticity.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Cumulative meditation practice drives a universal, pan-cerebral reduction in the exploratory breadth of hierarchical dynamics, tracking dose-dependently with lifetime hours of practice. Temporal persistence is bidirectionally tuned by 8-week mindfulness-based interventions in a population-specific way: reduced in healthy meditators but increased in trauma-exposed individuals, revealing that comparable MBI protocols engage qualitatively distinct network mechanisms depending on baseline clinical status.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for how behavioural training reorganises non-equilibrium brain dynamics, with direct implications for tailoring mindfulness-based interventions to individual clinical profiles.

title: Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness
authors: Asal Mehrabi, Mohammad Aliannejadi et al. (3 researchers)

comments.author: Dr. David Sterling (Caltech)

slides.hook: LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation is increasingly applied to multilingual tasks, yet prompting strategies such as Chain-of-Thought and Role Conditioning are recommended based solely on English benchmarks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Whether their effectiveness transfers across judge models and languages remains unknown: prompt-sensitivity studies are largely English-centric, while existing multilingual judge studies fix the prompt template. In this work, we address this gap by measuring this interaction through a benchmark of 9 prompting strategies, 4 open-weight judges, 27 languages, and 4 tasks across 13 datasets, yielding over 1M pointwise scores on gold-reference outputs, validated against human judgments.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We find that prompting strategies are not transferable: the choice of the judge model dominates the choice of prompting strategy, strategy effects reverse direction across judges, and stability degrades in low-resource languages, where these effects are concealed by aggregate reporting. These findings show that prompting effects in multilingual evaluation are conditioned on the judge, task, and language.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Consequently, prompting strategies should be validated for the intended evaluation setting, and cross-study comparisons should account for both judge and prompt configuration.

title: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding
authors: Taimeng Fu, Yi Du et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps have emerged as a key spatial memory representation for long-horizon robot autonomy, enabling robots to reason about objects, their spatial relationships, and past observations across time.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, existing object-centric semantic maps are primarily designed for static environments and rely on an append-only point integration strategy, where newly observed points are accumulated but previously integrated points are rarely reevaluated. Consequently, perception errors accumulate over time, and outdated points persist after objects move or disappear.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Although recent dynamic mapping methods update object-level representations in changing scenes, they do not explicitly revise noisy or obsolete points within each object. We propose an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Experiments demonstrate improved mapping accuracy over the previous method by 3.46% on Replica and 2.55% on ScanNet, show robustness in dynamic environments and under perception noise, and provide an effective spatial memory for object navigation and embodied question-answering with success rates of 82.4% and 76.7%.

title: What Shapes Brain Alignment of Large Language Models during Dialogue? Insights from Language Production and Comprehension
authors: Yuko Nakagi, Yuya Chiba et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Brain alignment of large language models (LLMs) offers a way to investigate representational similarities between LLMs and the human brain during language processing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While previous studies have mainly focused on passive language comprehension, little is known about such alignment during dialogue, in which speakers engage in both language production and comprehension. In this study, using fMRI data collected during dialogue, we examine brain alignment during language production and comprehension across LLM layers and brain regions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We assess its association with the intrinsic dimension (ID) of LLM representations and the contributions of several interpretable linguistic and communicative features. Our results reveal distinct patterns of brain alignment between production and comprehension, as well as strong associations with ID in brain regions associated with each processing mode.

authors: Yuji Zhao & Boris Gutman

slides.hook: As two most prevalent neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) shared commonalities both in symptomology and pathophysiology.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, to what extent and in what way these two distinct disorders overlap remain underexplored. In this study, we propose an explicit, interpretable and spatially adaptive transfer learning framework to elucidate the morphometric biomarkers linked to AD and PD.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We applied such high-dimensional machine learning model to two most popular open-source neuroimaging datasets, i.e., Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) and Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI). title: First Mathematical Runtime Analyses of Evolutionary Multitask Multi-Objective Optimization
authors: Danyang Zhang & Weijie Zheng

slides.hook: To facilitate the solving of complex problems, evolutionary multitask optimization is regarded as a promising technique due to its capacity for cross-task knowledge transfer.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In contrast to empirical evidences, no mathematical runtime support exists for this technique within the domain of multi-objective optimization. In this work, we aim to fill this important gap.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We analyze how the representative multiobjective multifactorial evolutionary algorithm (MO-MFEA) covers the Pareto fronts of two bi-objective problems simultaneously. For the two-task problem of maximizing the classic bi-objective OMM and the multimodal OJZJ benchmarks, the MO-MFEA requires only an expected runtime of O(n^2 log n)---the same as optimizing the simple OMM alone---yet achieves a speedup by a factor of Θ(n^{k-1}/log n) compared to optimizing OJZJ alone (with gap size k).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Similarly, for the task pair comprising the classic LOTZ and the multimodal DLTB benchmarks, a speedup of Θ(n) is attained over optimizing DLTB alone, while the runtime matches that of optimizing LOTZ alone.

title: Tracking the Emergence and Persistence of Abnormal Grain Growth in an Aluminum Alloy using Diffraction-Contrast Tomography
authors: Helmuth-André Schulz-Harder, Karolína Gutbrod et al. (15 researchers)

slides.hook: Abnormal grain growth is inherently three-dimensional, making 3D tracking of grain evolution essential for understanding its underlying mechanisms.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This study combines synchrotron-based diffraction-contrast tomography and phase-contrast tomography to characterize the three-dimensional grain structure and quantify the size and spatial distribution of second-phase particles in the aluminum alloy AA5252. Using an interrupted annealing protocol, we tracked the persistent growth of abnormal grains and the emergence of abnormal growth in a grain initially belonging to the matrix.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Although second-phase particles effectively suppressed grain growth in the matrix, variations in local particle density showed no apparent correlation with either the emergence or subsequent rapid growth of abnormal grains. Instead, crystallographic misorientation and, more notably, neighboring grain size were identified as stronger predictors of abnormal growth rate.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings suggest that the same microstructural characteristics facilitate both the emergence and persistence of abnormal grain growth, although the mechanism triggering the transition to rapid growth remains unresolved.

title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
authors: Masoud Mardani, Shivani Sharma et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

slides.hook: Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. title: Large-deviations theory for growing chemical reaction networks
authors: Praful Gagrani, Ignacio Madrid et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Growing biochemical systems are intrinsically noisy, with one important source of stochasticity arising from the discrete reaction events of the underlying biochemical network.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because growing systems do not generally admit stationary abundance distributions, it is unclear how to separate this intrinsic chemical noise from other sources of variability in population and single-cell data. Here we develop a large-deviation theory for exponentially growing stochastic chemical reaction networks by decomposing abundance into volume and composition.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In these coordinates, balanced growth corresponds to a stable composition together with exponentially increasing volume. We show that composition fluctuations satisfy a large-deviation principle with speed equal to the volume of the growing system, and the corresponding quasipotential is selected by a solution of the contact Hamilton--Jacobi equation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The framework therefore provides a stochastic null model for single-cell heterogeneity generated by the intrinsic stochasticity of the underlying chemical reaction network.

slides.hook: Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) of mixed oxide precursors offers an alternative route to produce sustainable alloys, bypassing the sequential extraction, refining, and remelting steps that dominate the carbon footprint of conventional metallurgy and individual metal production.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the thermodynamic limits and most effective H_2/H_2O ratio needed for full metallization of multicomponent oxides are not yet established. slides.content: By linking residual-oxide stability to the H_2/H_2O ratio, the framework identifies the thermodynamic limits and provides guidelines for designing sustainable multicomponent alloys directly from mixed oxide precursors.

slides.hook: Genome foundation models are growing into sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) networks whose expert weights no longer fit on the machines that hold the sequences, yet sending a private genome to rented accelerators exposes it: we show that a single server hosting one expert recovers the input nucleotides with 99.8% top-1 accuracy.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present CipherGenome, a protocol that keeps the embedding, attention and router of a 15.1B-parameter MoE genome model on a trusted thin client and outsources every expert projection, 95.8% of the parameters, to untrusted and possibly colluding GPU servers under module-LWE encryption. The design exploits three structural facts: expert layers are linear between two SwiGLU gates, expert weights are public, and GPU integer tensor cores can evaluate a ciphertext-weight product exactly modulo 2^{48} in a single GEMM.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The client evaluates the nonlinearity exactly and re-encrypts with fresh secrets, so no polynomial approximation or bootstrapping is ever needed. On 72 windows from 12 bacterial genomes, encryption adds 2.54 times 10^{-4} nats per token of KL divergence (95% CI upper bound 3.95 times 10^{-4}), below a pre-registered non-inferiority margin and indistinguishable from bf16 inference, while the same inversion attack falls to chance level.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Per expert and token, the server-side cost is more than six orders of magnitude below a CKKS baseline.

title: Bayesian adaptive design for neural recruitment curves

slides.hook: Nonlinear response models remain ubiquitous across disciplines with recruitment curves describing muscle response to neural stimulation.

slides.content: Conventional acquisition methods typically rely on static uniform sampling, requiring many stimuli, while adaptive threshold-hunting designs such as ML-PEST forfeit accurate characterization of the overall curve. title: Multiscale Quantum-Classical Simulation of Protein Autoproteolysis in a Million-Atom Membrane Environment
authors: Alexander Orlov, Alexis Ralli et al. (14 researchers)

slides.hook: Predicting chemical reactions in biomolecules is challenging because reactive centers are embedded within complex environments that strongly influence their energetics and mechanisms.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we present a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales. We apply this approach to ADGRG1 autoproteolysis, a maturation reaction in an adhesion G protein-coupled receptor that has not previously been studied using correlated electronic-structure methods.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our simulations treat a biologically realistic system containing more than one million atoms, including the full-length uncleaved receptor embedded in an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane, while incorporating a 54-qubit IQM quantum processor and up to 1,200 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. These results demonstrate how quantum computers can serve as accelerators within scalable scientific workflows, extending correlated electronic-structure methods to biologically relevant systems.

title: Sound-Horizon-Agnostic Forecast for Constraints on H_0 and Σm_ν from BAO, CMB Lensing, Supernovae and LSST-like Galaxy Lensing
authors: Seyed Hamidreza Mirpoorian, Helena García Escudero et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: We present a sound-horizon-agnostic forecast for constraints on the Hubble constant H_0 and the sum of the neutrino masses Σm_ν from a combination of LSST-like galaxy weak lensing, Simons-Observatory-like CMB lensing, the completed DESI BAO program, and expanded supernova samples.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Treating the sound horizon at baryon drag r_d as a free parameter, the method provides a consistency test of ΛCDM without relying on the standard early-Universe calibration of r_d. The analysis incorporates realistic galaxy weak-lensing systematics, explicitly marginalizing over photometric-redshift calibration, multiplicative shear biases, intrinsic alignments, and baryonic feedback, and extends the CMB-lensing analysis to L_{max}=5000.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: For fixed Σm_ν, we forecast uncertainties of σ(H_0)simeq 1.5 km/s/Mpc with our least informative prior set, σ(H_0)simeq 1.3 km/s/Mpc with more restrictive priors, and σ(H_0)simeq 0.7 km/s/Mpc with an additional informative prior on the amplitude of primordial fluctuations A_s. Allowing Σm_ν to vary weakens the H_0 constraints, while still yielding a forecast 95% CL upper limit of about 0.4 eV on Σm_ν.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The method recovers unbiased constraints on H_0 for the former but not the latter, highlighting its dependence on assumptions about early-Universe physics.

title: Simulating Alzheimer's amyloid-like pathology on a fly central nervous system connectome
authors: Taeho Jo

slides.hook: In Alzheimer's disease, the amount of pathology in the brain is an imperfect predictor of how much function is lost.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Pathology leads to that loss through neural circuits, but these cannot be observed neuron by neuron in patients. This study therefore simulated the central nervous system of the adult male Drosophila melanogaster: 166,700 integrate-and-fire neurons wired by the MaleCNS connectome.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The simulator reproduced a published fly brain model (rate correlation 0.9997). Three kinds of damage reported in amyloid-β flies, a lowered spike threshold, synapse loss and neuron loss, were imposed with assumed magnitudes, and circuit responses were measured in 1,424 simulated flies.

slides.content: Whole-brain activity revealed damage at milder severity than the learning index, because it changed much relative to its variation between trials.

title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
authors: Joseph Lee, Yanjing Li et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.

slides.hook: Content warning: this paper quotes slurs and hateful statements from published test suites; the racial slur among them is masked.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Automated systems decide at scale which messages are harmful, and they decide unevenly. Classifiers label African American English as offensive up to twice as often as other English, the accounts of prominent drag queens can score as more toxic than those of white nationalists, and safety behaviour that holds in English collapses in low-resource languages.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We argue that over-flagging and under-protection share one cause: deciding harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than from what a message does. We organise the evidence into seven failure modes and argue, as testable hypotheses, that harmful behaviours (a request for secrecy, a demand for payment, an attempt to isolate someone) travel across languages better than the words that express them.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Applied to five open systems in eleven languages, from a keyword lexicon to two current multilingual guard models, the protocol finds that none reaches native-speaker accuracy at separating harmful function from harmless form (51 of 55 system-language pairs fall short); that greater capability raises discrimination in nine languages while leaving Arabic and romanised Hindi near chance, so the gap between the best- and worst-served languages grows with capability; that one system both over-flags and under-protects the same language most; and that a language a system reads worst can look the most fairly treated when only false positives are reported.

title: Turning Quantum Compiler Configuration Selection Upside Down: A Top-Down Paradigm
authors: Ming Zhong, Xiangyu Ren et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Selecting an effective quantum compiler configuration requires coordinated decisions over both hardware targets and compiler settings, with the ultimate goal of improving circuit execution fidelity.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing SOTA approaches typically decompose this problem into two sequential stages: a device is chosen first, after which compiler options are tuned on that device through RL-based search. This bottom-up strategy can be fundamentally limited by its initial device decision, since a poorly matched backend may constrain the best fidelity achievable regardless of how effectively later compiler options are optimized.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In contrast to classical compiler tuning, where the search space is often prohibitively large, the configuration space of quantum compilers remains manageable enough to support exhaustive search. Consequently, rather than repeatedly searching from candidate configurations, one can derive reusable configuration knowledge from offline oracle results and apply it directly to new circuits.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Across our evaluation, the distilled rules consistently strengthen LLM-based selection, while QuTOP provides the strongest overall balance between solution quality and selection latency among the baselines.

title: De novo design of monoclonal and bispecific antibodies with OFAntibody
authors: Valhalla Team

slides.hook: Recent advances in generative protein design have enabled de novo antibody generation with explicit target and epitope conditioning.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, most existing approaches remain formulated around a single antigen-antibody interface, whereas bispecific antibody design requires modeling multi-component complexes in which multiple target-recognition interfaces must coexist and interact within a shared antibody structure. Here we present OFAntibody, an all-atom generative framework for de novo design of monoclonal and bispecific antibodies.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: OFAntibody expands CDR-epitope interaction learning with large-scale distilled antigen-antibody complexes, and introduces multi-component structural supervision and arm-aware multi-hotspot routing to learn compatible multi-interface geometries and couple each antibody paratope to its designated epitope. OFAntibody supports epitope-conditioned generation across monoclonal antibodies and diverse bispecific formats, including tandem VHH, diabody and CODV.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results extend de novo antibody design from binary antigen-antibody complexes to programmable multi-component complexes, providing a foundation for designing single molecules that combine recognition of distinct targets and their associated biological functions.

title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
authors: David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Mohammad Ali Armin et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: This chapter explores how robotic systems and ambient intelligence can enhance care for older adults in residential aged care (RAC) homes and private homes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although these settings differ, we frame both as extreme and challenging environments for human-robot interaction (HRI), characterised by cluttered and dynamic layouts, diverse resident needs, and limited on-site technical support. We review embodied and non-embodied systems that assist with daily living, safety monitoring, and social engagement, highlighting hybrid deployments where robots complement fixed and wearable sensors.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To ensure these technologies are usable and effective, design considerations consider the cognitive, physical, and social needs of older adults. Interaction design prioritises accessibility for older adults with low digital literacy, using robust but simple voice interfaces, small sets of non-verbal cues, accessible screen-based companions, and safe object handovers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We close by outlining open research challenges and future directions for scalable, regulation-ready deployments that support aging with dignity, safety, and independence.

title: Can AI Co-Design Structures? An AI Agent for Early-Stage Structural Design
authors: Ricardo Maia Avelino, Mennatallah El-Assady et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Recent advances in large language models and agentic workflows offer a new paradigm to early-stage structural design translating design intent into structural models.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although text-to-3D approaches have demonstrated that natural language can be used to produce visual, mesh-based geometric models, structural design requires domain-specific geometric arrangements and semantically rich data types. title: Gravitational Wave Diffractive Images Reveal the Structure of Astrophysical Objects
authors: Han Gil Choi, Sunghoon Jung et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Scattering patterns encode the structure of extended objects, as demonstrated by charged particle scattering on atomic nuclei.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Gravitational wave (GW) diffraction offers an analogous probe of otherwise invisible mass distributions. At linear order in the lens potential we derive expressions relating the central diffractive image contribution to a gravitationally lensed GW waveform to the Fourier transform of the projected lens density.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: For finite mass lenses this contribution takes the form of a point mass Born amplitude multiplied by a normalized mass form factor, analogous to that in nuclear scattering. As the frequency of GWs from a merging compact binary source evolves the signal samples this form factor across spatial scales, imprinting lens structure through interference with the primary image.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results provide a framework for characterizing extended dark matter and compact object astrophysical environments.

title: Searching for Axion Dark Matter via Superconductor-Spin Hybrid Magnetometers
authors: Runqi Kang, Jian Zhang et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Axions are a compelling dark matter candidate suggested by theories beyond the Standard Model.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The predicted axion-electron coupling and the resulting pseudomagnetic field allow for laboratory axion searches. Here we report an experimental axion search via a superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A state-of-the-art broadband magnetometer with a sensitivity of sub-100 aT/Hz^{1/2} at tens of kHz has been realized by coupling a ferrite spin sensor to a readout system based on a superconducting quantum interference device. The most stringent terrestrial constraints on the axion-electron coupling have been established in the frequency range 5sim60 kHz.

slides.content: This work demonstrates the potential of superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometers in high-precision magnetic field sensing and the study of fundamental physics.

title: MORAD: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Objective Rewards for RNA Inverse Design
authors: Jixin Tang, Ji Guo et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We introduce MORAD, an online reinforcement learning framework for backbone-conditioned RNA diffusion models that trains a single shared policy across diverse target backbones.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Structure-conditioned RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences compatible with a target three-dimensional backbone, yet existing reinforcement learning approaches either optimize a separate policy for each target backbone or rely on offline preference optimization, leaving online post-training of a reusable backbone-conditioned model largely unexplored. MORAD combines backbone-conditioned group sampling, group-relative reward normalization, and a forward-process diffusion objective.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. To aggregate these heterogeneous objectives despite differences in scale and optimization direction, MORAD maps each measurement to a bounded desirability score and combines them with a weighted geometric mean.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On the test set, MORAD outperforms RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, and RDesign across tertiary structural accuracy, secondary-structure pairing, and thermodynamic quality, establishing a new state of the art in structure-conditioned RNA inverse design.

authors: Lily Jade Joyce, Michelle M. Kelley et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

title: FLaG: Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling for Token Aggregation
authors: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Token aggregation converts token-level representations into fixed-dimensional sample representations, but most pooling methods operate only in the original token space.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling (FLaG), a plug-in aggregation module that re-expresses encoder outputs in the Fourier domain before final pooling. FLaG represents the nonredundant rFFT spectrum through concatenated real and imaginary components, summarizes spectral tokens with learnable latent queries, derives a sample-conditioned channel gate, and reconstructs modulated token representations for downstream aggregation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We evaluate the same architecture across ESM2-based antimicrobial peptide (AMP) activity prediction, ResNet18 image classification on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and three RoBERTa-based language tasks. FLaG achieves the best macro-averaged Spearman correlation coefficient, RMSE, and Recall@50 across four AMP backbone-species settings and the highest top-1 accuracy on CIFAR 10.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Supplementary materials, source code, and data are available at https://www.healthinformaticslab.org/supp/ and https://github.com/Kewei2023/AMPCliff/tree/FLaG.

title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
authors: Shujie Cheng, Lucas C. Céleri et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Background: Gamma entrainment using sensory stimulation (GENUS) is under study as a treatment for neurological disease, but cortical engagement is variable.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) modulates cortical state and sound-evoked beta-gamma activity, suggesting that it may strengthen responses to rhythmic sensory input. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Methods: Electrocorticography (ECoG) was recorded from core and belt auditory cortex, insular auditory field (IAF), and anterior insular cortex (AIC) in seven isoflurane-anesthetized rats before and 90 min after initiation of 30-Hz cervical VNS. Responses to 500-ms click trains at 20 and 40 Hz were quantified using inter-trial phase clustering (ITPC), event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP), and debiased weighted phase-lag index (WPLI).

slides.content: VNS may therefore enhance auditory cortical target engagement during GENUS, although effects on disease pathology or clinical outcomes remain untested.

title: Reaction-induced Localized Annealing for On-chip Materials Discovery
authors: Nensi Toncich, Nerea Abando et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: On-chip thermal processing is a key technology for materials discovery across all disciplines of the natural sciences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we present a microfabricated heat-delivery platform that enables reaction-induced localized on-chip annealing up to 1400°C. A buried reactive multilayer combined with a nanometric diffusion barrier provide ultra-fast heating and quenching rates on the order of 10^6°C s^{-1} as illustrated by the generation of ultra-high aspect ratio microstructures during rapid-solidification and the stabilization of dopant-free tetragonal zirconia at room temperature.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Rapid kinetics also enable the observation of transient states of capillary-driven hole collapse in melts. Our work expands localized high-temperature processing routes and offers a material-independent approach for rapid screening of multidimensional nanomaterials on and off-equilibrium.

title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
authors: Kaisei Ohata, Jun-Yu Dong et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. title: Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families
authors: Hantao Lou, Jianqing Zheng et al. (24 researchers)

slides.hook: Discovering broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) from human natural immune repertoires remains a fundamental challenge in immunology, hindered by: the extreme rarity of bnAb, incomplete understanding of their cellular origins across pathogens, and the inability of existing computational tools to generalize across emerging viral threats.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present ImmuneAgent, a closed-loop AI system that integrates multimodal reasoning with continual meta-learning and wet-lab feedback to overcome these barriers. Applied to screen the natural BCR repertoires from vaccinated or infected cohorts, the system achieves a ~55% neutralization antibody discovery rate (60 of 110 cloned candidates) and a ~11% bnAb yield (12 of 110), substantially outperforming a state-of-the-art sequence-based neutralization predictor or cofolding models evaluated at the same cloning budget.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Five ImmuneAgent-discovered antibodies conferred 100% in vivo protection against lethal influenza challenge, comparable to the clinical-stage therapeutic MEDI8852. The system recovered the cellular and structural determinants of bnAb activity and identified FCRL5+CD27+ atypical memory B cells as a conserved bnAb reservoir and hydrophobic interface enrichment as a cross-viral structural signature, which generalized to unseen antigens, discovering human metapneumovirus (hMPV) cross-neutralizing and human papillomavirus (HPV)-neutralizing antibodies without antigen-specific sorting.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results validate that ImmuneAgent is a generalizable framework for rapid therapeutic antibody discovery against emerging viral threats.

slides.content: The reservoir settings are found by a search on each task, and driving the reservoir with the input and collecting its states for every candidate setting dominates the cost of the search. title: Discrete time liquids
authors: Zuo Wang, Paul M. Schindler et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

title: Probabilistic Energy Modeling Unifies Versatile Swarm Control
authors: Xiang Zhou, Xiangyu Zhu et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Robotic swarms must coordinate across diverse missions, yet existing controllers often require redesign, retuning, or retraining when objectives change.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we show that probabilistic energy modeling provides a unifying representation for versatile swarm control, in which diverse missions emerge from compositions of shared interaction principles rather than task-specific control formulations. By exploiting the correspondence between Gibbs random field energy minimization and structured reward maximization, we encode fundamental swarm behaviors as reusable energy terms within a unified probabilistic objective.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Decentralized policies trained within this representation are composed into a single controller through lightweight policy gating, without retraining. An interpretable action-attention mechanism captures non-uniform local interactions, while dimensionless normalization supports transfer across swarm scales and platforms.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish probabilistic energy modeling as a scalable and transferable framework for decentralized swarm control.

title: Multi-Scale Temporal Flows for Peptide Trajectory Generation
authors: Xichen Sun, Wentao Wei et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Peptides occupy a particularly challenging regime of biomolecular dynamics.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Short peptides lack a stable folded core and populate broad conformational ensembles, while cyclization adds ring closure, non-local residue coupling, and stereochemical diversity. Deep generative models have made remarkable progress in emulating molecular-dynamics trajectories directly, yet each is trained on windows cut at a fixed interval and therefore observes the process at a fixed temporal resolution.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: More fundamentally, none takes that interval as an input, so the physical time a window spans is never represented, leaving the sparse frames on which a peptide crosses between metastable states difficult to learn. Here, we introduce PepTIDE, a multi-scale temporal framework for peptide trajectory generation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Read in temporal order, its trajectories recover these sparse transition frames and reproduce inter-state fluxes more faithfully, confirming that modeling multiple temporal scales is what makes these rare events accessible.

slides.hook: We explore the space-time cost of encoding of a bosonic mode into a set of qubits via various encodings, and their resilience to noise.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In particular, we compare the performance of the unary Fock state encoding, an unexplored encoding of Fock states into Dicke states (``Dicke'' encoding), and the binary quadrature encoding. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using classical simulations, we assess the accuracy and optimized space-time costs in terms of number of qubits, circuit depth and CNOT count of a quantum simulation of the time dynamics using these encodings. Although our study is far from comprehensive, we find that the binary quadrature encoding is overall most favorable in terms of being very space-efficient and relatively time-efficient due to the use of the quantum Fourier transform.

title: PopPert: Population-level Joint-Distribution Modeling for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
authors: Handong Wang, Jiaxin Qi et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Predicting transcriptional responses to specific perturbations is critical for understanding cellular regulatory mechanisms and accelerating drug discovery.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Single-cell RNA sequencing destroys each measured cell, yielding only unpaired populations of control and perturbed cells. However, existing methods typically model perturbation prediction at the single-cell level and assume cell-to-cell correspondence, which conflicts with the unpaired nature of the observed data.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address this challenge, we propose PopPert, a framework that explicitly parameterizes population-level joint gene expression distributions for collective transcriptional state modeling. Given a control population distribution and a perturbation condition, PopPert predicts perturbation-induced changes in distribution parameters, eliminating the need for cell-level correspondence and reducing sensitivity to single-cell noise.

title: Democratizing Clinical Tumor Whole Genome Sequencing: 18-hour End-to-end Analysis via Trillion-parameter Large Language Models Locally Deployed on Consumer-grade Hardware
authors: Rui Xiao & Yili Xu

slides.hook: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) is essential for precision oncology, yet its clinical adoption remains limited by prohibitive computational costs and multi-day turnaround times.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This work presents a fully localized low-resource framework enabling stable deployment of a trillion-parameter biomedical LLM on a single consumer-grade RTX 4060 laptop with 32GB system memory and 8GB VRAM, as well as on routine clinical workstations in general hospitals, completing the entire tumor-paired WGS workflow from raw FASTQ input to clinical-grade full-variation-spectrum report output. Under standard 30X depth configurations, our implementation finishes a single tumor-paired WGS analysis within 18 hours, achieving 99.62% F1 score for somatic variant detection with over 99.9% concordance to the industrial-standard A100 cluster pipeline, fully meeting clinical oncology accuracy requirements.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Quantitative profiling shows adaptive heterogeneous memory scheduling accounts for 71% of total execution time, while model optimization introduces less than 9% of total detection error. This work is the first engineering implementation of trillion-parameter biomedical LLM-driven clinical-grade genomic analysis on consumer-grade hardware, breaking the industry paradigm that trillion-scale genomic LLMs require hundred-thousand-dollar GPU clusters and multi-day turnaround, establishing a low-resource pathway for global primary medical institutions to adopt whole-genome precision oncology at zero additional cost.

authors: Sara Karimi & Soroush Shakeri

slides.hook: We develop a relativistic dynamical model for the thermal evolution of expanding kilonova ejecta, in which the effective temperature is determined by the ejecta mass, opacity, velocity, and radioactive heating rate.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The resulting thermal evolution follows a broken power law as the ejecta transition from the optically thick to the optically thin regime. We incorporate this thermal history into a relativistic spectral calculation that accounts for the equal-arrival-time surface geometry and Doppler boosting, enabling us to model the observed kilonova spectrum and constrain the underlying ejecta properties.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We investigate the effects of the model parameters and relativistic corrections on the observed temperature and spectral shape, and find that light-travel-time delays and Doppler shifts can produce significant spectral distortions at high ejecta velocities. We apply the model to the early-time X-shooter spectrum of the kilonova AT2017gfo and infer the ejecta mass, opacity, and velocity through Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting with a Student's t likelihood.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results highlight the importance of incorporating relativistic and equal-arrival-time effects when interpreting early-time kilonova spectra, especially for rapidly expanding ejecta.

title: Continuous Variational Synthesis
authors: Alan N. Amin, Mattia G. Gollub et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Biological machine learning was long bottlenecked by the ability to synthesize designed DNA.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Variational synthesis models control chemical reactions to physically manufacture quadrillions of designed sequences in DNA. However, training these generative models is challenging: constraints on chemical synthesis can force many parameters into a discrete space, limiting the ability to pre-train and fine-tune.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this article we train ``free'' variational synthesis models using stochastic gradient descent in continuous space, and then discretize with post-training quantization to impose hardware and wetware constraints. This enables variational synthesis models to satisfy stringent reward criteria, while still synthesizing diverse designs, achieving a strictly dominating quality-diversity Pareto frontier.

title: Demonstration-Based Robotic Feeding Using Dynamic Movement Primitives
authors: Kenzhi Iskandar Wong, Kitti Thamrongaphichartkul et al. (13 researchers)

slides.hook: This paper presents a demonstration-based robotic feeding framework that integrates human demonstration, Dynamic Movement Primitive-based motion planning, vision-based scene perception, and robot control.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: A human operator first demonstrates the scooping and feeding motions while the position and Euler-angle orientation of the spoon are recorded using a motion-capture system. slides.content: Before task execution, an RGB-D camera estimates the participant's mouth position, while two AprilTags are used for robot-frame registration and tray localization. The detected tray pose is used to position the scooping motion, whereas the detected mouth position defines the positional goal of the feeding motion.

slides.content: A real-world experiment demonstrates the feasibility of the integrated pipeline and shows that the learned spoon motions can be reproduced within the detected experimental scene.

title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation
authors: Sang-Hun Han, Changyeon Won et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Stable grasping under task-specific disturbances is important for robotic manipulation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, most dexterous grasp synthesis methods are developed for highly actuated hands in free space, and low-DoF hands may not be able to realize the contact topologies required by these grasps. Meanwhile, support surfaces can provide useful contact forces, but are often treated only as geometric constraints.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present a support-aware grasp synthesis framework for object immobilization with low-DoF coupled hands. Given irregular object geometry, our method represents both hand and object local surface regions as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings between them.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Real-world experiments further demonstrate physically executable grasps which enable object immobilization in cooking scenario.

title: Gate Initialisation versus Recurrent Dropout and Zoneout in Learning Long Dependencies: A Controlled Study of LSTM and GRU Networks on Synthetic Tasks
authors: Oleksandr Kholodniak & Oleksandr Prokhorov

slides.hook: Dropout and zoneout are routinely added to long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, but, to our knowledge, their placements have not been crossed with gate initialisation in a factorial design, and it is not known whether early gradient propagation tells which runs will learn long dependencies.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We trained one-layer LSTMs and GRUs on the adding problem and on delayed recall in a factorial grid of 720 runs, crossing conventional and chrono gate initialisation with up to six recurrent regulariser placements at one rate each, with pre-specified follow-ups, and recorded how sensitive the final hidden state was to the input at every lag. Because both tasks supply fresh or exhaustive training data, the study measures the regularisers' effects on optimisation and does not assess generalisation from a finite training set.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: At lengths chosen to make conventional initialisation difficult, all 360 chrono-initialised runs reached the validation criterion within 5000 updates, as did 119 of 120 unregularised runs with a horizon about four times too short or too long, whereas conventionally initialised networks learned slowly or did not reach the criterion within the budget at the longer lengths. Under conventional initialisation, dropout generally delayed learning and zoneout helped only in some conditions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The results support chrono initialisation, even with a rough horizon, on such tasks.

slides.hook: Proteins can possess numerous mutations relative to their wild-type amino acid sequences with minimal impact to their structure and function.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, in other cases, even a single amino acid mutation relative to the wild-type sequence can lead to a large change in structure or even a disease phenotype. title: Nanoscale chemical engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers through in situ electron beam irradiation in a TEM
authors: Ayoub Benmoumen, Marie-Laure David et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Defect engineering in low-dimensional materials is a powerful approach to tailor their structure and chemistry at the atomic scale, with high relevance for tuning physical properties.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we apply this strategy to MXenes, one of the largest families of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and demonstrate the use of a highly focused scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) beam for the structural and chemical nanoengineering of titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) multilayers. By adjusting the beam energy, electron dose, and scanning parameters, Ti3C2Tx multilayers were irradiated at 80 and 300 keV and characterized in situ using annular dark-field imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The irradiation induces gradual structural and chemical modifications, largely driven by the selective sputtering of atomic species and MXene layers. We identify irradiation conditions that selectively remove Cl or F surface terminations while largely preserving the Ti3C2 framework, whereas other conditions promote preferential carbon removal, in agreement with theoretical predictions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that electron irradiation can be used to locally tailor MXene composition and create nanoscale architectures beyond those accessible through conventional chemical synthesis.

slides.hook: We consider a minimal pressure-based model of heterogeneous cell populations consisting of proliferative and non-proliferative cells with different mobilities.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The model is formulated as a system of reaction--cross--diffusion equations describing the spatio-temporal dynamics of the cell densities. title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
authors: Wei-Wei Yang, Yang Shen et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca_2CuO_2Cl_2, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
authors: Haowei Shi, Kartikeya Arora et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: We propose distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing architecture that simultaneously exploits spatial- and spectral-domain entanglement to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our scheme consists of a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers interrogating spatially separated samples, each driven by a classical frequency comb at the bright port. A single two-mode squeezed frequency comb is distributed through a passive beam-splitter array into K entangled combs, establishing multipartite correlations across sensors while preserving intrinsic spectral entanglement.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The protocol is compatible with both heterodyne detection and division detection, and enables parallel estimation of weighted-average absorption features over multiple frequency components. Compared with spatially separable quantum strategies requiring K independently engineered nonclassical comb sources, our approach achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single quantum resource distributed across the network.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish a scalable route toward broadband distributed quantum spectroscopy with simultaneous spatial and spectral advantage.

title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zeropy Surio, Tobias Engel et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Counterfactual branching estimates this credit by re-running the episode after an alternative decision, but the branch draws its sampling noise independently of the factual episode, so the outcome difference mixes the effect of the decision with the luck of everything that follows. We observe that in agentic search the retriever, the corpus, and the grader are deterministic, so an episode is a deterministic function of the policy's decisions and its sampling noise.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Twin worlds are therefore realizable: the same noise, a different decision. We introduce TWICE (TWIn-world Credit Estimation), which keys the Gumbel noise of every token by turn and line, rolls out counterfactual twins that inherit the factual episode's downstream noise, and turns their paired outcome differences into turn-level advantages for policy-gradient updates on actor-sampled trajectories; only the actor is deployed.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On seven question-answering benchmarks, TWICE improves the average exact match of GRPO by 5.3 and 4.5 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, outperforms tree-search and counterfactual-branching baselines, and uses 68% fewer auxiliary tokens than VinePPO.

title: Enhancer-promoter proximity predicts transcriptional competence but not transcriptional output in the Drosophila brain
authors: Olivier Messina, Loucif Remini et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: How 3D genome architecture contributes to transcriptional specificity across neuronal cell types remains unclear.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we used multiplexed chromatin tracing to map chromatin architecture and cell identity at single-cell resolution in the adult Drosophila brain. We found that enhancer-promoter (E-P) proximity was increased in transcriptionally active compared with inactive neurons.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: RaSFNet: Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation
authors: Chuang Chen

slides.hook: LiDAR point cloud semantic segmentation is a fundamental component of 3D perception for autonomous driving and robotics.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Projection-based methods map 3D point clouds into 2D representations for feature extraction using 2D networks. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Moreover, proximity in the projected representation does not necessarily imply proximity in 3D space, and interactions between point and projected features may mix features from different ranges, reducing semantic discriminability. title: If the brain were so simple: Information-based drivers of intelligence and their interaction through an n-body-inspired framework
authors: Brett J. Kagan, Johnson Zhou et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Theories of how the brain processes information and returns intelligent outputs are numerous and often difficult to conclusively test.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we consider an approach grounded in informatics and algorithmic thermodynamics for how neural systems respond to different patterns of information in different ways, with a focus on the relationship between the information entropy of a signal and a new proposed quantity we term information enthalpy, which represents the internal resource of structured information within a system available to be used for predictions and other forms of work. To evaluate the capacity of the external signals to increase information enthalpy in the system, we introduce the information enthalpy potential (IEP) as a defined metric.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation
authors: Mahdi Sabbaghi, George Pappas et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Online Policy Distillation (OPD) often outperforms offline methods such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) by training on trajectories sampled directly from the student.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, standard OPD trains the student to follow the teacher at every state of the trajectory, assuming that teacher guidance is always beneficial. We instead distinguish between what the teacher prefers and what actually helps the current student succeed.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation (AOPD), which weights teacher actions by their counterfactual advantage under the student. Teacher actions that improve the student's expected outcome are reinforced, while those that do not are downweighted.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

title: Resource Analysis of Quantum Optimization Algorithms via Variational Methods
authors: Vitor Dallabona, Lucas Friedrich et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are promising approaches for solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the role played by quantum resources such as entanglement and coherence during the optimization process remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the evolution of these resources in two VQAs--the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON)--applied to the Minimum Vertex Cover problem.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We employ a variational resource-quantification framework based on the Bures metric and Uhlmann's theorem, in which an auxiliary quantum circuit is optimized to identify the closest resource-free states. This approach allows us to quantify Bures entanglement and Bures coherence of the algorithmic states without requiring full quantum state tomography.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results reveal distinct quantum-resource trajectories associated with the two optimization strategies and illustrate how entanglement and coherence evolve as variational quantum states approach solutions of a classical combinatorial optimization problem.

slides.hook: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions.

slides.content: Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI_2 is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed.

title: Storage-Centric System Designs for Enabling Fast, Efficient, and Low-Cost Genomic and Metagenomic Analyses
authors: Nika Mansouri Ghiasi

slides.hook: Genomic and metagenomic analyses play critical roles in many fields, such as precision medicine, urgent clinical settings, discovering early warnings of communicable diseases, ensuring food safety through pathogen monitoring, agriculture, and scientific discovery.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Due to the challenges of analyzing and storing massive volumes of genomic and metagenomic sequence data, significant efforts have been made to accelerate (meta)genomic analyses and store sequence data compressed. Despite the benefits of these techniques, we identify two major outstanding problems in accessing stored sequence data and supplying it to the analysis units: (i) the data movement bottleneck due to moving large amounts of low-reuse data from storage and the unnecessary burden on the rest of the system, and (ii) the data preparation bottleneck, where compressed sequence data needs to be first decompressed and formatted before analysis.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this dissertation, we present customized storage-centric systems, which efficiently (i) analyze (meta)genomic data inside the storage system, and (ii) enable highly-compressed storage and high-performance access of large-scale sequence data, thereby alleviating the overheads of data movement, computation, and data preparation. We demonstrate that the proposed systems significantly improve system performance, energy efficiency, and system cost-efficiency of (meta)genomic analysis.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We hope that the storage-centric systems proposed in this dissertation facilitate the broader adoption of (meta)genomic analyses and inspire future research to fundamentally improve the performance, energy efficiency, and cost-effectiveness of other data-intensive application domains related to health and life sciences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We test whether a shared decoder, trained on measurements from diverse proteins, can interpret these constraints in an unseen target, enabling cross-protein transfer for initial experimental round prescreening. We present StabilityArc , which maps frozen ESMC-600M residue representations through a shared RoPE transformer to an Lx20 matrix of substitution effects; a symmetric, contact-aware residual aids in predicting epistasis in simultaneous substitutions.

title: Robust paths to primordial B modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
authors: Arianna Rizzieri, Giorgia Zagatti et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: A detection of primordial B modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We examine how much polarised extragalactic point sources may contaminate the cosmological signal in ground-based CMB experiments, propagating their impact through component separation to the final parameter constraints. We discuss masking and modelling strategies to ensure that the resulting constraints remain both accurate and precise under this source of contamination.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We produce synthetic data containing polarised emission from extragalactic radio sources (ERSs) and dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) following state-of-the-art models for both samples. We find that, while the DSFG contribution is likely too small to cause any significant bias to the cosmological or foreground parameters, the ERS contribution instead, if left unmasked, leads to a bias in the parameters describing the Galactic synchrotron and lensing B-mode components.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: For experiments targeting noise levels of order σ_Psimeq 1,μK,{rm arcmin}, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above sim0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.

slides.hook: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. We evaluate LACToS across three diverse applications spanning medical imaging, human faces, and X-ray security screening.
