title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform d-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites.

Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.

slides.hook: Searches for periodic supermassive black hole binaries in quasar light curves rely on recovery fractions, the share of injected signals detected, which forecasts use as detection efficiencies.

At fixed absolute magnitude M_i=-23, sinusoid recovery falls toward high mass, and with DR7 magnitudes it climbs above about 10^8,M_odot, so the magnitude assignment sets the sign of the trend.

title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
authors: Chulwoo Ahn & Vladimir Manucharyan

slides.hook: We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internal idler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale.

slides.content: Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.

slides.hook: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K_3Ln(PO_4)_2 (Ln = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic P2_1/m structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Magnetization and specific heat measurements confirm the absence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 0.1 K in both compounds.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Direct quasi-ADR measurements demonstrate strongly contrasting refrigeration behaviors: K_3Yb(PO_4)_2 reaches a minimum temperature of 29.8 mK from an initial state of 2 K and 6 T, whereas K_3Gd(PO_4)_2 exhibits extended hold times below 150 mK associated with its larger magnetic entropy reservoir. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a J_{mathrm{eff}} = 1/2 ground-state doublet in K_3Yb(PO_4)_2, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results identify K_3Ln(PO_4)_2 as a chemically robust platform for rare-earth-tunable solid-state ADR.

authors: Anna Hart, Mohammed El-Kebir et al. (4 researchers)

title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
authors: Seung-Hyun Shin, Cheong-Eung Ahn et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

authors: Keita Nagasawa, Ryutaro Okuma et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. title: MD-LLM-2: A Transferable Language Model of Molecular Dynamics with Physical Conditioning and Explicit Path Probabilities
authors: Mhd Hussein Murtada, Z. Faidon Brotzakis et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations model the motion of proteins between conformational states, but crossing free energy barriers and sampling multiple thermodynamic conditions remain computationally costly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We recently introduced MD-LLM-1, which showed that language models can generate conformational trajectories at lower cost, but required a separate model for each protein and did not explicitly model thermodynamics or kinetics. Here we introduce MD-LLM-2, a transferable language model that generates trajectories conditioned on sequence, temperature and molecular history.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Because each step defines a normalized distribution over structural tokens, the model assigns an explicit likelihood to every generated or simulated trajectory. Trained across mdCATH domains, MD-LLM-2 reproduces the median radius of gyration of MD within 1 Angstrom in 10 of 12 unseen domains, predicts reduced Trp-cage compaction at higher temperature, and generates L99A T4 lysozyme trajectories that reach published transition-region backbone structures.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results extend MD-LLM from protein-specific trajectory generation to transferable, physically conditioned modelling with explicit path likelihoods, and show that the framework can predict equilibrium populations for force-field parameters not seen during training, with an initial indication that first-passage kinetics can also be captured.

slides.hook: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. title: Training-Data Extraction from Genomic Language Models
authors: Tianhao Mao, Zihao Wang et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Genomic language models generate long nucleotide continuations from short prefixes, exposing a direct route for studying training-sequence extraction through the generation interface.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present an output-only black-box attack on Evo 2 that selects convergent groups of repeated generations without gradients, token likelihoods, or training-corpus access during candidate selection. Recovered content is then scored by an evaluator combining aligned length, nucleotide identity, match multiplicity, and sequence complexity.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across 304 runs on Evo 2 7B with bacteriophage and plasmid prefixes, the attack yields 888 candidate clusters, of which 85 match training segments of at least 500 bp, giving a cluster-level attack success rate of 9.57%. Final filtering retains 22 uniquely matched extraction events at the 500-bp threshold and 15 at 1,000 bp, covering 14 and 7 distinct training-sequence regions, respectively.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The results establish convergence among repeated nucleotide generations as a practical output-only signal for recovering long training-sequence segments and characterize how recovery depends on prefix length, cluster size, perplexity, early stopping, and sequence domains.

title: CANN: Commutative Algebra Neural Networks for Virus Classification
authors: Mushal Zia, Faisal Suwayyid et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: The extensive diversity of viral genomes challenges alignment-free representations to capture both nucleotide composition and the higher-order organization of recurring sequence patterns.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Conventional k-mer representations quantify pattern abundance but do not explicitly encode how these patterns are organized across scales. Here, we introduce CANN, an alignment-free framework that combines persistent commutative-algebraic descriptors with neural representation learning for viral family classification.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

slides.hook: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties.

slides.content: Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.

title: Explainability from Training with Applications to TCR-Epitope Prediction
authors: Jiarui Li, Zixiang Yin et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Deep learning models have achieved strong performance in artificial intelligence for science, yet their black-box nature limits our understanding of how they learn scientific tasks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing methods for interpretability provide limited insight into how models organize evidence and evolve during learning. We introduce explainability from training (EFT), a model-agnostic paradigm that traces model interpretation during training to explain why models rely on specific features and how they organize these features as predictive evidence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We apply EFT to four state-of-the-art T cell receptor (TCR)-epitope prediction models, TCR-SRIM, TULIP, MixTCRpred, and NetTCR-2.2, spanning post-hoc and interpret-by-design approaches as well as transformers and CNNs. To investigate how structural information affects model explanations, we introduce a benchmark, TCR-XAI2, containing 388 unique experimentally resolved TCR-epitope structures, complemented by structures predicted using AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, TCRModel2, tFold-TCR, and OpenFold3.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Using EFT with TCR-XAI2, we demonstrate that (1) CNN and transformer models exhibit distinct learning trajectories; (2) TCR α and β evidence can conflict during learning, limiting the benefits of jointly modeling both chains, while MHC information mitigates this; and (3) real versus predicted structural data for TCR-epitope prediction exhibits distinct TCR and peptide feature preferences as well as differing trajectories of model certainty.

slides.hook: Reaching a degenerate ground-state manifold and sampling it uniformly are distinct properties of a quantum annealer.

slides.content: We quantify this distinction using an Ising ring with additional couplings between maximally separated sites. For antiferromagnetic benchmark couplings and N geq 5, we derive the exact ground-state energy, degeneracy, and defect structure for each congruence class of N modulo four.

slides.content: This classification separates ground-state hit probability from conditional sampling bias. We embed instances with up to 162 logical spins on a D-Wave Advantage processor using length-two chains and compare its output with simulated annealing on the embedded and logical problems.

title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
authors: Sunjun Hwang, Lee Wei Wesley Wong et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored.

slides.content: Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. slides.hook: Adult attachment is commonly represented by attachment anxiety and avoidance, but these person-level dimensions do not by themselves specify how momentary relational conditions are perceived, compared with desired conditions, translated into action, and updated after interpersonal feedback.

title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
authors: Stephen Chung & Wenyu Du

slides.hook: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

slides.hook: KV cache compression for multimodal LLMs usually selects the visual tokens to keep once, at prefill, and reuses that selection for the whole generation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

slides.hook: Taxonomic classifiers based on exact matches differ in which matches they use and in how each match splits its credit among the taxa containing it: Kraken~2 gives a k-mer's credit to the lowest common ancestor of those taxa, SPUMONI~2 labels each position of the read, Tagger gives each maximal exact match (MEM) one label, and Cliffy splits a match's credit evenly over a roughly logarithmic sample of the taxa.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compare these schemes on the same long MEMs, mainly on short 16S rRNA reads classified to genera with SILVA, where credit proportional to the number of occurrences of the MEM in each taxon is the most accurate, by 1.0 to 6.8 percentage points. We compute long MEMs with Boyer--Moore--Li on a run-length compressed suffix array, and count their occurrences in each taxon with a complete, run-length compressed tag array, in time proportional to the number of tag runs in the MEM's BWT interval, without locating any occurrence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We bound the number of tag runs in terms of the BWT runs and of how often suffixes with long common prefixes have different tags, and show that tags constant on d blocks of the text have a macro scheme with at most r + 2d phrases. On SILVA our index takes 1.44,GB and classifies a read in 66,μs with one thread at 93.8% accuracy, about what Cliffy reports for its 9,GB index; over minimizer digests it takes 0.49,GB and reaches 92.5%, against 84.2% for Cliffy's digested index on the same reads.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On nanopore reads from whole genomes, where almost every long MEM occurs in one species, we instead use each read's longest MEMs, found in one pass of a variant of Boyer--Moore--Li with a k-mer filter, which assigns 99.6% of the reads to their species with no length threshold.

title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). The shape of cluster haloes revealed by intracluster light
authors: Euclid Collaboration, T. Kolcu et al. (330 researchers)

slides.hook: Intracluster light (ICL) offers a luminous route for measuring the shapes and orientations of cluster haloes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at 0.1 leq z leq 0.8 selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. We measured the ICL properties across five bands (I_mathrm{E}, Y_mathrm{E}, J_mathrm{E}, H_mathrm{E} and the coadded YJH_mathrm{E}), and find that the shape parameters are consistent across the filters, with the H_mathrm{E} band probing the profiles to the largest cluster-centric distances (0.1R_{200mathrm{c}}sim100 kpc).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The ICL ellipticity (e=1-b/a) distribution peaks at 0.5, consistent with halo ellipticities inferred from strong and weak lensing studies, suggesting that the ICL traces the large-scale structure of the clusters. Cluster cores, dominated by brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) light, are round (esim0.2), while the ICL becomes progressively more elongated at large radii, reaching an ellipticity of sim0.5 by 0.1R_{200mathrm{c}}.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate the capability of Euclid to characterise the ICL morphology with high statistical precision, allowing new constraints on cluster halo structure and its evolution with redshift.

title: HyperTaxa: Multiscale Genome Representations for Generalized Microbial Taxonomic Inference
authors: Akash Rao, Sushim Gupta et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Reliable microbial taxonomic inference is challenged by the rapid growth of newly sequenced organisms and incomplete reference coverage.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While alignment- and database-driven tools remain essential for reference-backed identification, they are not designed for learned inference over species absent from genome-level training. We introduce HyperTaxa, a taxonomy-aligned representation learning framework for open-set microbial taxonomic inference.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: HyperTaxa encodes whole genomes as multiscale hyperspectral k-mer transition fields and aligns these representations to a taxonomy-derived semantic space using a two-stage Node2Vec-to-MDS procedure that combines local graph structure with global hierarchical distance preservation. The resulting space supports zero-shot inference over species excluded from genome-level training but represented in the taxonomy, generalized zero-shot inference over seen and unseen species, and cascaded genus-to-species prediction.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results position HyperTaxa as a complementary taxonomy-aware representation and candidate-generation framework for microbial identification under incomplete reference coverage and open-set uncertainty.

title: Cosmic Ray Observations using Coincident Scintillator and Radio Signals with the Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON)
authors: Zachary Martin, Jackson Hinkel et al. (21 researchers)

slides.hook: At energies above 100 PeV, coherent radio frequency (RF) emission across the 10 -- 1000 MHz band from cosmic particle-induced atmospheric showers becomes increasingly dominant, making radio detection a powerful probe at ultrahigh energies.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON) considers mountaintop phased radio arrays to monitor large areas at the horizon for upward-going geomagnetic emission in the 30 -- 80 MHz band produced as a consequence of Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. As part of ongoing efforts to measure the sensitivity of BEACON to such signals, the BEACON prototype identifies cosmic rays through the same emission mechanism.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Prior to 2023, BEACON operated a four-antenna prototype, which successfully demonstrated identification of coherent and impulsive sources using a beamforming RF trigger. In 2023, we upgraded the instrument to six newly designed antennas and added an independent scintillator array to cross-validate radio-detectable cosmic rays.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The reconstructed signal polarization angles are consistent with pure geomagnetic emission compared to various background classes.

slides.hook: The interpretability of complex neural networks remains a critical challenge, especially for models already deployed in high-stakes domains.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To address this, we adapted the Feature Selection Layer (FSL) to optimize feature weights post-training, a variant we term post-hoc FSL. Our approach reframes the FSL as a lightweight, trainable module that integrates with already frozen pre-trained models on tabular datasets to highlight the features the original model considers most important.

title: Evolutionary Architecture Search for Chlorophyll-a Prediction in Lakes using Sentinel-2
authors: Kursat Komurcu & Linas Petkevicius

slides.hook: Small tabular datasets with expert-designed spectral features are the norm in operational Earth observation, and the networks applied to them are typically hand-designed.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We revisit one such published model -- a Sentinel-2 algal bloom classifier -- and ask what architecture search adds, holding the task, the features and the lake-level train/test split of the original study fixed. Searching an extended multilayer-perceptron space with regularized evolution, and selecting on inner-cross-validation AUC only, we find networks that improve held-out AUC from 0.790 to 0.820 and accuracy from 0.733 to 0.748 while using 409 trainable parameters, 26 times fewer than the strongest hand-designed reference.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The search converges on a consistent recipe -- a single narrow layer, RMS normalisation, tanh activation, step-decayed RMSprop and weight averaging -- that a practitioner would be unlikely to reach by default. At 1.6,kB the resulting model is small enough to serve as an onboard screening trigger, which is the setting that motivates the work.

slides.content: Code: https://github.com/VU-AIML/automl4eo-bloom-nas.

slides.content: The relativistic jet associated with the z=6.1 AGN PSO J030947.49+271757.31 is the highest-redshift large-scale jet currently resolved in X-rays, providing a unique opportunity to study these structures. slides.content: The increased exposure allowed us to resolve the extended X-ray emission into two distinct, slightly resolved components and perform spatially resolved spectral analyses. title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization
authors: Ming Chen, Rong-Xi Tan et al. (11 researchers)

slides.hook: Black-box optimization (BBO) arises in many scientific and engineering problems where objective evaluations are expensive and limited.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Recent large language model (LLM) agents offer a new way to approach BBO by combining task semantics, computation, optimization tools, and feedback-driven decision making, showing great potential due to the integration with mathematically rigorous tools. However, existing agentic BBO studies use different task domains and system configurations, making their results difficult to compare and the effects of individual design choices hard to isolate.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We therefore introduce AgenticBBO-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for agentic BBO spanning synthetic functions, hyperparameter optimization, database tuning, chip design, and molecular design under a unified finite-budget evaluation protocol. In our experiments, agentic BBO achieves higher family-averaged scores than direct LLM-based methods in all five domains and outperforms the best numerical optimizers in four.

title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
authors: Kerem Yurtseven, Shantanu R. Jha et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.

title: ConQEC: Concolic Testing for Quantum Error-Correcting Code Implementations
authors: Zihao Li, Ji Guan et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) implementations are hybrid software-control systems: measured syndromes drive decoder dispatch, recovery actions, and logical checks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing QECC verification techniques can prove formal obligations, and general quantum testing can expose final failures, but developers still lack a scalable testing workflow that generates concrete faults and explains where a QECC repair path first diverges. This paper presents ConQEC, to our knowledge the first concolic testing framework for QECC implementations.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By combining concrete (Pauli) fault replay with symbolic repair-path constraints, ConQEC generates tests that expose not only final logical failures but also fault--syndrome--decoder--recovery (FSDR) diagnostics: the injected fault, observed syndrome, decoder decision, recovery action, oracle result, and earliest divergent stage. Its symbolic encoding of Pauli faults, syndrome predicates, decoder and recovery relations, and oracle checks enables this diagnostic workflow to scale beyond exponentially increasing amplitude-level quantum-state reasoning.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: ConQEC detects the seeded bug in every experimental case and reports a replay-valid, fault-localizing FSDR witness for each.

title: Cooling more while dissipating less: anomalous tradeoffs from thermodynamic geometry
authors: Andrea Canzio, Vasco Cavina et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: We show that, starting from the same state, optimal driving can sometimes reach a colder (or hotter) target in the same amount of time while dissipating less energy, or equivalently dissipate the same amount of energy in a shorter time.

slides.hook: We consider differentially private (DP) optimization in the federated setting, where a DP estimate of the feature covariance matrix serves as a Hessian approximation for generalized linear models.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing central DP methods for covariance estimation have communication cost that grows quadratically in the data dimension, while existing baselines with linear communication cost are only locally private and degrade as the number of clients increases. slides.hook: We calculate the relativistic axion energy density produced by the decay of a curvature-displaced Peccei--Quinn condensate in a quartic KSVZ model.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We follow the radial PQ field (the saxion) as it relaxes from its inflationary minimum and determine the surviving condensate abundance from the adiabatic action of its oscillations. We then evolve the condensate through its decay into axions and visible particles to calculate the resulting dark-radiation contribution, expressed as ΔN_{rm eff}.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: With one heavy coloured KSVZ fermion and no additional portal interactions included, the axion channel dominates the two tree-level decay modes. Two reference histories yield ΔN_{rm eff}simeq0.033 and 0.12, with maximum saxion energy fractions below 1% and 4%, respectively.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

slides.hook: How learning progresses over time and varies across individuals is a longstanding question in cognitive and behavioral science.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, a major challenge is identifying observable behavioral measures that faithfully capture learning progression. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

We introduce a self-supervised representation learning framework built on a simple hypothesis: behavioral characteristics associated with identity and learning remain relatively stable over nearby time intervals. Using temporal proximity as supervision, our framework learns compact representations directly from movement trajectories without manually defining behavioral states or kinematic features.

slides.hook: The core-collapse of massive stars ({geq}10 rm M_odot) usually takes the form of a supernova, but in some cases may lead to a direct collapse, leading to a failed core-collapse supernova (FccSN).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Wide-field time-domain surveys, such as the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), are a useful tool to find such ``disappearing" stars. We use a piecewise linear function model to search the entire ZTF optical photometric catalog for FccSNe, yielding 125 ``faders" that dip significantly with a flat top and bottom flux.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Although no candidates were definitively found, some of the sources exhibit promising behavior that may indicate a direct collapse event. Assuming a null result from the search, we calculate at 99% credibility that the maximum statistical rate of FccSNe in the Milky Way is 147 per century.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: However, we predict that similar monitoring using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's Wide Field Instrument (WFI) could enable population-level studies of nearby FccSNe.

slides.hook: Online motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) typically decode continuous EEG using fixed-length sliding windows that may be misaligned with neural events.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing window optimization methods often evaluate windows independently, overlooking temporal dependencies and potentially producing fragmented or physiologically implausible selections. We propose Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning (TSE-RL), a framework that incorporates prior knowledge of MI event structure into a constrained Markov decision process for adaptive window optimization.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: First, TSE-RL assigns each window an explicit semantic role through Discard, Onset, Sustain, or Offset actions, extending binary retain/discard decisions to event-level alignment. Second, a finite-state machine masks invalid actions to enforce the temporal order of MI phases and promote physiologically plausible window sequences.

title: Evolve on the Host, Predict on the Edge: Deploying Online Neuroevolutionary Architecture Search for Cross-sectional Stock Return Prediction
authors: Jonathan Chang & Zimeng Lyu

slides.hook: Accurate forecasting models are usually large, expensive to update online, and fixed in architecture once trained.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We apply ONE-NAS, an online neuroevolutionary architecture search that evolves a population of small recurrent networks as each window of data arrives, to daily cross-sectional stock return prediction, and pilot it on a host and endpoint pipeline: the host runs the search and ships each generation's champion genomes over TCP/IP to a Raspberry Pi 4B, which predicts online. title: A Reality Check of Inference-Time Context Augmentation Methods
authors: Haeun Yu, Geert Heyman et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) often fail to utilise the context given in the input, resulting in hallucinations or a fallback to parametric knowledge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Context augmentation methods aim to improve model performance by modifying the input, from inserting filler tokens that add computational time to adding relevant content such as elaboration of a context during inference. However, these methods have been evaluated in isolation and only by their performance gains, leaving it unclear how they compare and whether they reliably improve performance.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this paper, we present an evaluation framework spanning five methods that differ in how informative the inserted content is and apply them at the sentence level across seven models spanning multiple sizes on three datasets. We find that accuracy gains are not always genuine improvements but undirected perturbations: the methods correct some predictions while breaking others, particularly when the inserted text allows only for more computational time.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our findings highlight the need to evaluate the reliability of the accuracy gains before adopting them in practice.

title: From Qubit Tensorization to Gaussian Optimizers in Bosonic Systems
authors: Salman Beigi & Hami Mehrabi

slides.hook: We develop a method for deriving Gaussian optimality results for bosonic quantum systems from inequalities for qubit systems.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Inspired by Gross's derivation of the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality from an inequality on the two-point space, we use qubits as quantum two-point spaces and lift bosonic Weyl operators to pseudo-Weyl operators on large qubit systems. By controlling weighted norms and relative entropy in the fluctuation limit, we establish two transfer theorems that convert tensorized qubit inequalities into inequalities for bosonic Gaussian channels.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: As a first application, we prove that the sharp 2-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the bosonic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup tensorizes without loss in the constant. We also establish a sharp output entropy inequality for tensor powers of a class of qubit channels.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Applying our relative entropy transfer theorem, we obtain multimode constrained minimum output entropy bounds for Gaussian additive-noise channels and thermal attenuators in the heating range.

title: Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb_2
authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Nathan Giles-Donovan et al. (17 researchers)

slides.hook: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb_2.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~μm photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm^2 concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

title: STUART: Sequence Triage and qUAntification of Read Transcripts for Rapid Ionizing Radiation Exposure Assessment
authors: Tomasz Strzoda, Lourdes Cruz-Garcia et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Rapid medical triage following ionizing radiation exposure is critical for emergency management, yet traditional alignment-based bioinformatics are too computationally intensive for mass-casualty scenarios.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To address this, we developed STUART (Sequence Triage and qUAntification of Read Transcripts), a mapping-free machine learning framework optimized for mobile biological dosimetry. Inspired by Natural Language Processing (NLP), the system converts raw sequencing reads into k-mer-based numerical profiles, completely bypassing standard alignment.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: While the architecture is universally applicable to any transcriptomic biomarker, this study focused on radiation exposure using the FDXR gene model. Evaluating Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost, advanced signature selection strategies drastically reduced the initial 1024-dimensional feature space by over 98%.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By minimizing time-to-decision, this decentralized tool bridges the gap between advanced biomarkers and practical on-site biomonitoring, offering a scalable foundation for rapid epidemiological response and routine occupational radiation monitoring.

title: Confirming candidate self-lensing binary detections with radial velocity measurements
authors: Adam McMaster, Madeline-Mai Ward et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Compact objects in approximately edge-on binary orbits with stars are able to produce a self-lensing effect, amplifying light from their companion once per orbit.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To date, five white dwarf self-lensing systems are known, while none are known containing black holes or neutron stars. Discovery of such systems is a potential method of finding quiescent black holes and neutron stars, most of which will be pristine and unchanged from their formation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Photometric detections can suffer from degeneracies in the lens mass and orbital parameters when the amplification and crossing time are not well constrained, while photometric searches produce too many false positives to allow radial velocity investigation of every candidate. Therefore we investigate the minimal radial velocity (RV) observational requirements to characterise such systems by simulating detectable self-lensing light curves, using those light curves to generate targeted RV observations, and fitting RV jointly with photometry.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results suggest that multi-stage RV follow-up, starting with a small number of observations of many candidates, can efficiently classify self-lensing candidates and identify high-priority systems for further investigation.

title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
authors: Luciano Ambrosini

slides.hook: Architectural and structural design optimization in parametric software affords about a thousand evaluations of an expensive model for problems with tens of variables, a regime for which most metaheuristics were not designed.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: On the side of artificial intelligence, two hybrid metaheuristics are proposed: a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors, and a particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement. A budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution is also proposed.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Under a hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted, the CMA-ES hybrid ranks first on seven shifted and rotated functions at 10 and 30 variables and beats CMA-ES on six of seven functions at 30 variables. Ablations attribute this gain to the injection and show that a local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Solvers should therefore be selected by problem structure and stopping time, not by a single ranking.

title: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
authors: Aude Corbeel & Sebastian De Haro

slides.hook: We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We identify the assumptions underlying this modelling and highlight two key features, fast scrambling dynamics and entanglement as a resource, that underpin the information release in the model. We argue that this reasoning exemplifies a broader change in how information is used in black hole physics, in which quantum information theory now provides a useful operational modelling framework.

slides.hook: Diffusion language models generate multiple token positions in parallel, but few-step decoding makes parallel commitment difficult: tokens that appear reliable individually may be jointly inconsistent, while premature commitments can prevent later context-dependent refinement.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this paper, we introduce SetCommit, a training-free method for coordinated parallel token commitment. Instead of selecting tokens independently by confidence, SetCommit selects a commitment set that balances token reliability against local joint commitment risk, preserving conditioning opportunities for subsequent denoising steps.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: It further performs budget-neutral local exchanges, replacing vulnerable earlier commitments when newly revealed context supports more reliable alternatives. SetCommit requires no retraining or architectural modification and is compatible with existing diffusion decoding strategies.

title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3

slides.hook: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society.

slides.content: For LLMs, reinforcement learning is the first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore, it is the stage where convergent instrumental behavior, on IC grounds, likely to appear. title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
authors: Takeru Ito, Shogo Yoshida et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: Engineering Low-Latency, High-Throughput Quantum Decoders on NVIDIA GPUs
authors: Stefano Markidis, Luca Pennati et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We design and optimize a quantum error correction (QEC) decoder for NVIDIA GPUs, combining Relay belief propagation, a state-of-the-art message-passing algorithm, with order-zero ordered statistics post-processing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our implementation uses CUDA Graphs to control GPU execution, stops updates for converged samples, and collects unresolved samples in queues for post-processing. We optimize sparse traversal through coalesced message accesses, prefetching, and register reuse, and accelerate binary post-processing with warp-level collectives.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In addition, mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic and INT8 quantization reduce message storage and traffic while retaining accuracy using accumulators at higher precision. We evaluate surface, hypergraph product, and bivariate bicycle code workloads on NVIDIA A100 and GH200 data-center GPUs and a commodity RTX 5080.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The combination of performance optimization, mixed precision, INT8 quantization, and concurrent decoder instances opens a path toward QEC decoder clusters built from commodity GPUs.

title: MQAScore: Fine-Grained Text-Music Alignment Evaluation via Large Audio Language Model
authors: Wei-Jaw Lee, Chun-Ping Wang et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Text-to-music alignment is commonly evaluated by the global similarity between text and audio embeddings, which collapses all described attributes into a single score and obscures which ones are missing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We instead introduce MQAScore, which verifies each atomic musical concept along five clip-level dimensions (genre, instrument, mood/theme, vocal, and usage) by the probability that a large audio language model (LALM) answers affirmatively to a binary question. To assess evaluator reliability, we construct verification labels from presence/absence annotations and LLM-guided concept substitutions, and propose the Sensitivity-Invariance Ratio, which measures how selectively an evaluator responds to meaning-changing substitutions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To assess evaluator reliability, we construct verification labels from presence/absence annotations and LLM-guided concept substitutions, and propose the Sensitivity-Invariance Ratio, which measures how selectively an evaluator responds to meaning-changing substitutions. Experiments show that concept-level scoring improves both question-answering and similarity-based evaluators, and MQAScore can be a more reliable and interpretable fine-grained complement to global similarity for evaluating text-to-music alignment.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Experiments show that concept-level scoring improves both question-answering and similarity-based evaluators, and MQAScore can be a more reliable and interpretable fine-grained complement to global similarity for evaluating text-to-music alignment.

title: Differentiable powder X-ray diffraction enables analysis of evolving structures
authors: Xiangyu Yin, Nina Andrejevic et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Operando and in-situ experiments extend powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to materials that evolve during experiments, producing series of hundreds or thousands of patterns.

slides.content: Such series are commonly refined one pattern at a time, so weak signals give noisy structural trajectories. Parametric refinement instead fits a shared model to all patterns, but with most existing programs, changing the model or fitting it efficiently remains challenging.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we introduce diffPXRD, a differentiable PXRD engine in PyTorch. diffPXRD calculates derivatives by automatic differentiation, so a shared model can be changed without new derivative code.

slides.hook: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Additionally, the edge regions act as electronically active sites that may significantly enhance chemical reactivity relative to the central regions.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results provide important insights into tailoring the physical properties of goldene through lateral confinement, highlighting its potential for applications in nanoscale field-effect transistors, spintronic devices, and catalysis.

title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
authors: Hagen Holthusen, Matthias Knipper et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Finite element model updating is among the most general approaches to discover constitutive models from structural experiments: since the displacement field is computed rather than measured, it accommodates arbitrary geometries, boundary conditions, and sparse or noisy data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, every loss evaluation requires a nonlinear finite element solve per load step, and training neural materials requires many such evaluations. Intrusive model order reduction lowers this cost while retaining boundary conditions and variational structure.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: How can a reduced model remain accurate while the network weights change at every training step? We combine proper orthogonal decomposition and energy-conserving sampling and weighting with adjoint sensitivities of the reduced model, and adapt both the trial space and the sampled elements along the optimization path. The constitutive law is a polyconvex neural network: a logarithmic normalization term, together with a zero-anchored input convex architecture and a growth term, renders the energy polyconvex, coercive, and non-negative by construction, independent of the trained weights.

title: Fragment Path Complex Networks for Viral Genome Classification
authors: Alice Wachira, Xiang Liu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Accurate classification of viral families is essential to understanding genomic diversity, but rapid evolution and heterogeneous genome structure complicate reliable assignment.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Newly discovered viruses, particularly those from underrepresented ecosystems, expand the known diversity of viral genomes. This growing diversity poses challenges for classification methods that rely on similarity to existing references.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present Fragment Path Complex Networks (FPCN), a framework that represents viral genomes as sequences of ordered fragments at various scales. FPCN captures contextual sequence information within each fragment and uses path complexes to model complex relationships between neighboring fragments.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results position FPCN as an effective tool for classifying viral genomes within known families across benchmark datasets and newly released genomes.

title: Structure is not mechanism: high-gain gated-FFN rows across text and genomic foundation models
authors: Alexandros Tzanakakis, Aris Karatzikos et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: A small number of unusually high-gain parameters can exert disproportionate effects in transformer language models, but whether analogous structures recur in genomic foundation models and whether structural geometry determines functional importance remains unknown.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We analyzed high-gain rows in gated feed-forward networks across text and genomic foundation models, including a frozen 22-model causal census. Computing an associated bilinear weight operator exactly, without a diagonal approximation, we tested whether structural extremeness is a transferable mechanism.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Activation-derived candidates were functionally enriched relative to random and top-norm same-layer controls, yet neither spectral concentration nor operator magnitude predicted causal effect size, and these associations vanished within the endpoint-homogeneous text-decoder subset. A within-layer sweep of 36 rows in one genomic and one text decoder resolved this into two regimes: below the detector's acceptance threshold the ratio carried no positive information about causal damage, whereas above it the ratio ordered rows strongly but did not grade severity as a dose-response.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Enrichment is general, but the mechanism is model-specific.

title: MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models
authors: Khaled Waleed Dawoud, Muhammad Zaigham Zaheer et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong potential for video anomaly detection, but dense frame-level inference makes them impractical for real-time deployment.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing acceleration commonly relies on uniform sampling, which ignores content dynamics and can either waste computation on static segments or miss localized anomalies. We propose MoG-VLM a motion-adaptive anomaly detection framework that leverages motion purely as a lightweight control signal to decide when VLM inference is necessary.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To this end, we introduce Temporal Gradient Magnitude (TGM) which performs content-aware sampling to concentrate computation on informative regions while avoiding redundant processing. We further introduce a hierarchical dual-stream design in which dense multi-frame VLM reasoning is activated only around frames with elevated anomaly likelihood, via anchor-triggered context-window expansion with early termination.

title: CrisiLangs: A Multilingual Resource for Crisis Warning Generation
authors: Giacomo Gonella, Stefano Menini et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Communicating with the public during an emergency entails issuing warning messages promptly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In Europe, it often requires producing them in more than one language. Recent work has shown that language models can be trained to generate warning messages as a crisis unfolds, but the available data covers only English.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To fill this gap, we present CrisiLangs, a multilingual extension of CrisiText (an English dataset of crisis events paired with warning messages written according to expert communication guidelines) to Italian, Bulgarian, German, and Greek. Expert native speakers translated the warning messages of 1,000 events drawn from 411 scenarios, for a total of 5,000 event-message pairs across five languages.

title: Continuous Measurement of Quantum Axion Dark Matter
authors: Yunjia Bao, Dhong Yeon Cheong et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: We provide a fully quantum-mechanical description of the continuous measurement of wavelike dark matter.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Our focus is cavity haloscopes, although our results inform a broad range of axion searches. We extend the input-output formalism by treating the axion as a quantum field, finding how its quantum state is imprinted onto higher-order moments of observables of the outgoing transmission-line modes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We further develop a novel measurement-record formalism, which computes the joint probability distribution of all measurement outcomes and is well suited to studying the axion in the time domain. With it, we compute the exact axion-induced number distribution for the first time, demonstrating that it is not Poisson.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Finally, we show that intrinsically quantum effects, such as those from Fock or squeezed axion states, are far too weak to detect.

slides.hook: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the 2times10^{-5} level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from 1/f flux noise.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

slides.hook: We propose a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol based on fractional-revival dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a ring, combined with a controlled interaction quench.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using the Truncated Wigner Approximation, we show that nonlinear evolution to the quarter revival generates modest spin squeezing of -2.03pm0.28;dB, which subsequently degrades under further nonlinear evolution. title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
authors: Kleanthis Avramidis, Ivan Tashev et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Recent electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models increasingly emphasize model scale, potentially limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices and in everyday environments.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We argue that transferable EEG features can instead be learned with a compact architecture and introduce BrainCodes, a lightweight foundation model pretrained through self-supervised learning on more than 800 hours of recordings from over 1,000 participants. slides.content: The pretraining objective explicitly encourages representations that capture spatial connectivity through channel positional encoding, and sensitivity to narrowband neural oscillations through an auxiliary training objective. Our model matches or surpasses the state of the art across diverse neurophysiological monitoring tasks, including sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation.

title: Sequence-Informed Geometric Evaluation of RNA 3D Structures
authors: Andrea Zerio, Yighua Yao et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Computational RNA structure pipelines generate many candidate conformations for the same sequence.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Reliable evaluation therefore requires more than recognising plausible geometry, it requires determining whether that geometry is compatible with the sequence. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

slides.content: These findings provide initial evidence that pretrained sequence representations supply ranking information that complements geometric reasoning.

authors: Daniil M. Khodachenko, Andrei V. Ruban et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: The atomic ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys strongly influences their magnetic properties and mechanical behavior.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While general features of long-range atomic ordering are known from the experimentally established phase diagram in this composition range, detailed atomic configurations and driving forces behind them remain speculative. Here, we address this gap by using effective cluster interactions (ECI) obtained from density functional theory (DFT) calculations and subsequent statistical thermodynamics modeling to unravel the interplay between magnetism, composition, and temperature in body-centered cubic (bcc) Fe-Si alloys up to 20 at% Si.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our analysis reveals that the ordering behavior is governed by a strong coupling between magnetic order, lattice expansion, and Si concentration, with specific ECI shells switching sign or magnitude as the magnetic state changes, which is reflected in the phase equilibria and ordering behavior of Fe-Si alloys. In particular, we demonstrate that D0_3 ordering is, in fact, primary in the totally ordered ferromagnetic state, while the B2 type of ordering is promoted in the paramagnetic state at elevated temperatures.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By explicitly linking the magnetic state with the effective interactions and macroscopic phase behavior, this work establishes a predictive framework for an ab initio-based description of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys and highlights the decisive role of magnetism in ordering phenomena in this system.

title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs
authors: Prajvi Saxena, Sabine Janzen et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: As large language models are deployed in high-stakes roles such as therapy, education, and personal assistance, their social cognition must be assessed reliably.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Current Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks report aggregate scores that conflate two distinct competencies: explicit ToM (recognizing what someone believes) and applied ToM (using that belief to predict behavior). Building on this distinction, we investigate the gap and its recoverability using four structurally diverse benchmarks.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Aggregate reporting obscures uneven competence: on SimpleToM, Llama-3.1-8B scores 51.5 percent overall while recognizing mental states at 99.4 percent and predicting behavior at only 28.9 percent. To assess recovery, we compare structured prompting, matched in-context learning, and our proposed Belief-State Test-Time Training (BSTTT), which adapts lightweight parameters on answered support questions through action reconstruction.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We recommend decomposed reporting of explicit and applied accuracy alongside intervention comparisons that establish which failures are recoverable and under what conditions.

title: Fast Template Matching for Quantum Circuits Using Hypergraph
authors: Xin Hong, Jintao Yu et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Quantum circuit optimization is a key step toward the efficient execution of quantum algorithms.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Template matching has emerged as one of the dominant approaches for simplifying quantum circuits, yet it confronts the intrinsic challenge of accommodating gate commutativity. The state-of-the-art template-matching algorithm relies on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: While this DAG-based technique handles gate commutativity satisfactorily, it fails to preserve the local connectivity inherent to quantum circuits, thereby leading to relatively high matching complexity. In this paper, we introduce a hypergraph representation (HG), a commutativity-aware representation that collapses commuting gates into a single super-node while retaining all local connectivity.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The acceleration increases with circuit size, confirming that preserving locality and connectivity is the key to scalable quantum circuit optimisation.

title: What I Disbelieve: Quantifying Belief With Negative Ranking Functions
authors: Hanbin Go & Britt Anderson

slides.hook: A challenge in exploring the psychology of human uncertainty is its measurement and quantification.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Prior work has focused almost exclusively on probability, while the formal theories developed in philosophy are rarely tested. We tested Wolfgang Spohn's ranking theory, a normative account in which belief is graded by ordinal ranks of disbelief that combine by minimization rather than addition, as a descriptive model of human belief.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across six experiments, participants assigned ranks of disbelief to propositions involving personal experience, chance devices, sequential learning, and an Ellsberg urn. Ranks were reliable and, through the theory's two-sided rank function, distinguished belief, disbelief, and suspension of judgment.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: As a clear account of human belief dynamics with metrics that can be reliably measured, Ranking Theory provides a valuable framework for investigating and contrasting probabilistic and non-probabilistic accounts of human belief.

slides.hook: Search is a central component of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems and has been deeply investigated for classical ASR modeling based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, in work on current sequence-to-sequence ASR architectures it is often simplified to a small fixed-size beam search without external Language Model (LM). slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that these end-to-end (E2E) models work with a small search space most of the time but exhibit large temporary peaks in hypothesis count during periods of uncertainty. slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results highlight the limitations of search with low fixed-size beam pruning and provide practical guidelines for efficient search in E2E ASR.

slides.hook: The growing demand for high-capacity, fast-charging, and durable rechargeable batteries has intensified the search for advanced electrode materials, with two-dimensional materials offering large surface-to-mass ratios and short ion-diffusion pathways.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, pristine and Co-doped Janus HfSSe monolayers were investigated as anode materials for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries using first-principles density functional theory. authors: Zhongkai Shangguan, Yanbin Kang et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: General-purpose embeddings trained on profile similarity often misrank candidates in professional networks, where relevance is inherently complementary rather than symmetric.

title: Language Models Share a Readout Bottleneck in Working Memory
authors: Dongyu Gong

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) reproduce a human working-memory signature on the N-back task: performance declines as memory load N increases, and errors concentrate on lures, items that repeat the current stimulus at a neighboring but incorrect serial position.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We ask whether this shared behavioral signature reflects a shared mechanism. The literature offers two candidate accounts.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On a precision account, softmax attention cannot concentrate its weight on the item N positions back, so adjacent items are retrieved instead. On an interference account, attention selects the correct item, but the content of competing items corrupts the decision.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The working-memory limit of LLMs therefore lies in reading items out under interference rather than in locating them, consistent with interference accounts of human working memory.

slides.hook: Bright standard sirens from the Einstein Telescope (ET) provide an independent probe of cosmic expansion.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this article, we test whether future ET observations can constrain a dynamical dark-energy scenario inspired by DESI DR2. Using the best-fitting 29-bin dark-energy equation of state as the fiducial cosmology, we generate mock catalogs of 100, 500, 1000, and 3000 binary-neutron-star standard sirens with known host redshifts, and reconstruct the equation of state using both GW-only data and combined analyses with DESI DR2 BAO, BBN, and a compressed CMB constraint.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The effective numbers of constrained modes are N_{mathrm{eff}}sim 4-5 (GW-only) and 5-6 (combined), with information concentrated in a few correlated modes. The GW3000 catalog yields a departure from ΛCDM exceeding 5σ, and combined analyses reach similar significance for O(10^3) events.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results indicate that a few thousand ET bright standard sirens could provide a sensitive test of departures from ΛCDM.

title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
authors: Dingxuan Zhang, Yanhui Jiang et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution. In coding agents, however, execution poses an additional runtime control problem: the same task may be solved through primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework that treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures. The system combines a feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state recovery executor.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.

title: Cosmological Gravitational Wave Collider Physics
authors: Sukannya Bhattacharya, Matteo Fasiello et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Primordial tensor non-Gaussianity can probe massive particles present during inflation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We investigate this possibility in an effective field theory where the massless graviton mixes with the helicity-two mode of an additional massive spin-two field σ_{ij} with cubic self-interactions. For constant sound speed, we compute the leading tensor power-spectrum correction and the tree-level bispectrum, finding novel analytical expressions for these quantities.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the m_σ>3H/2 regime, we find a nonanalytic squeezed contribution that exhibits logarithmic oscillations with characteristic dependence (k_L/k_S)^{3/2pm iμ}, where μ=sqrt{m_σ^2/H^2-9/4}. The oscillation frequency is set by the mass m_σ, while the polarisation contractions determine the relative amplitudes of the different graviton helicity configurations.

slides.content: Finally, we explore how a slowly varying sound speed modifies the squeezed signal.~These results connect the two-point, three-point, and quadrupolar tensor signatures of massive spin-two fields in the cosmological gravitational wave collider.
