title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
authors: Zhaoyi Zhou, Akshayaa Magesh et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: As LLM agents operate over corpora of more than ten thousand tools, selecting the right tool for a complex multi-step user instruction becomes a central bottleneck.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Tool descriptions cannot all fit in context, and relevance-based retrievers only rank tools without knowing which are actually needed. Recent work instead leverages proprietary commercial LLMs like Claude or ChatGPT to drive a retriever, decomposing the instruction and selecting over retrieved candidates.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that a small, open model can be trained via reinforcement learning to perform the same functionality. On ToolBench, a Qwen3-8B model post-trained with our recipe outperforms Llama-4-Maverick (402B).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: In addition, the trained model transfers directly to different retrievers and generalizes to new tool corpora in different domains.

title: CoDecoder: Make Quantum Decoders Up to 100x Faster and Even More Accurate
authors: Yicheng Guang, Yuliang Xiong et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Fault-tolerant quantum computers need fast and accurate error decoding.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present CoDecoder, a small neural frontend that composes with an existing decoder to improve accuracy and reduce mean decoding time. It predicts each shot's logical outcome, retains confident predictions and routes the remaining shots to the unchanged fallback.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A logical-operator-aware output head scores shifted logical operators, combining equivalent logical lines on surface codes and deciding logical qubits jointly on bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes. Fused GPU inference and efficient routing reduce the overhead paid on every shot.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On retained shots, the frontend corrects more fallback errors than it introduces, even when it is less accurate overall.

title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
authors: Thanh Q. Tran, John Russell Himawan et al. (7 researchers)

comments.author: Hélène Dubois (Institut Pasteur)

slides.hook: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. However, existing approaches do not jointly offer fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address this gap, we introduce DIAL (Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels) to achieve all three properties. For fine-grained control, we perform classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a frozen LLM to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at different levels.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: When trained on SteerIF, DIAL provides fine-grained control over personas and, when combined with prompting, improves verifiable instruction following.

title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ali Najar, Hosein Hasani et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: It decomposes the fast adaptation phase into two temporal scales: a causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compact episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without attending over the full interaction history. Moreover, equipping agents with neural memory provides sufficient expressive capacity and test-time training capability, enabling effective adaptation to unseen held-out tasks and task families at meta-test time.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show that METTA provides an efficient path toward more adaptive and scalable long-context meta-RL.

title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
authors: Xie-Hang Yu & Pavel Kos

slides.hook: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

slides.content: Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. title: Humanoid Mobility via Attention-based Contacts
authors: Junzhe He, Kehan Wen et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Humanoid mobility over complex terrain requires accurate foot placement and coordinated whole-body motion capable of robust adaptation.

slides.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies trained without motion references generalize well across terrains, yet eliciting effective whole-body coordination through reward design and exploration alone remains challenging. slides.hook: Tetrahymena calcium-binding protein (Tcb2) forms Ca^{2+}-responsive networks that exhibit contractile behavior, yet how Ca^{2+} concentration controls their local mechanical response remains poorly understood.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

We find that increasing Ca^{2+} from 1 to 100~mM enhances the effective stiffness by nearly two orders of magnitude, from sim1times10^{-3} to sim7times10^{-2}~pN/nm, corresponding to a transition from a viscosity-dominated to a more elastic and mechanically robust network.

slides.content: These results establish Tcb2 networks as a minimal, tunable system for probing chemomechanical coupling and viscoelasticity in Ca^{2+}-regulated protein networks.

title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. II. The Multi-component Age-Metallicity Structure of the High-α Disk
authors: Tiancheng Sun, Maosheng Xiang et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Whether the high-α disk experienced a continuous or episodic star-formation history remains an open question.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we investigate the age--metallicity distribution of the high-α disk using approximately 145,000 Gaia DR3 subgiants with [mathrm{Fe/H}]>-1, 6.5~kpc lesssim Rlesssim9.5~kpc, and |Z|lesssim1.5~kpc. We adopt a forward-modelling framework that accounts for individual age and metallicity uncertainties and corrects for sample selection effects.

These features suggest an episodic history of star formation and chemical enrichment in the high-α disk, qualitatively consistent with cosmological simulations in which recurrent gas accretion drives variations in the star formation rate.

slides.content: Together, these results favour a picture in which the high-α disk was built through recurrent episodes of enhanced star formation rather than a single temporally smooth phase, even for the regime of {rm [Fe/H]}>-1.

authors: Shin Yamaguchi, Masaya Taniguchi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Language models (LMs) often exhibit successful cross-lingual transfer through continued (pre)training, still their underlying process remains unclear.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: One possibility is that LMs can leverage the evidence toward language-universal principles, namely, hierarchical structure, from a source language (L1) to a new language (L2), while many other non-linguistic explanations, e.g., improved initialization of position embeddings, can be potentially possible. In this study, to quantify the cross-linguistic transferability of linguistic evidence in cross-lingual LM training, we introduce a new experimental design, namely, a cross-lingual poverty-of-stimulus (CPOS) setting that ablates how LMs' hierarchical generalization in L2 can be led by structural evidence provided in L1.

slides.content: We contrast counterfactual L1 and L2 learning scenarios where the L2 corpus is ambiguous between linear and hierarchical grammar rules, while the amount of positive evidence for the hierarchical rule is controlled on the L1 side. Our experimental results show that LMs can partially, yet not perfectly, transfer L1 structural evidence to L2, yielding only a small but detectable hierarchical bias, while the strength of transfer depends on language pairs.

slides.hook: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation.

title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
authors: Blessing Isoyiza Adeika & Onyema Osuagwu

slides.hook: Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We recommend that speech-decoding studies report band-limited and artifact-channel accuracy, the direction of accuracy across frequency, and a measured detection floor.

title: CliffRank: A Dual-Branch Framework for Activity-Cliff Ranking Prediction
authors: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Activity-cliff ranking remains difficult because local structural changes can cause large activity differences, while high-quality data that resolve the underlying mechanisms remain limited.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To use available activity labels more effectively, we combine absolute-activity regression with ranking-consistency learning. CliffRank trains two parallel predictors with mean squared error, a thresholded listwise loss, and Pairwise Preference Consistency (PPC), which aligns relative ordering in the preference-probability space.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On three antimicrobial peptide datasets, CliffRank with ESM2-t12 achieved the highest mean Spearman correlation of 0.5393 and mean Recall@50 of 21.4, although the leading method varied across individual datasets. On three small-molecule datasets, CliffRank with PNA, where PPC was activated after 120 epochs, achieved the highest mean Spearman correlation of 0.6890, while its mean Recall@50 of 30.4 matched that of ACANet-PNA.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Future work should evaluate more targets and antimicrobial peptide systems, develop adaptive PPC schedules, and incorporate protein or membrane context when available.

title: Rest-frame Ultraviolet Variability of Quasars in the Cosmic Himalayas Overdensity
authors: Jiaqi Lin, Zhenya Zheng et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Some high-redshift overdensities show an enhanced incidence of AGNs, suggesting that large-scale environment may influence supermassive black hole fuelling and triggering.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Whether environment also affects AGN variability remains unclear.Using the Cosmic Himalayas (CH), an extreme concentration of 11 type 1 quasars at z=2.16-2.20, we investigate possible offsets in rest-frame ultraviolet variability relative to quasars with comparable redshifts, black hole masses, and Eddington ratios.We construct a parent sample of 1,138 Stripe 82 quasars at 2.11<=z<=2.25 and combine photometry from the SDSS, the PS1, and the ZTF to build observer-frame g- and r-band light curves spanning up to 27~yr. slides.content: In this paper, we give the local distinguishability of five quadripartite OPSs, where any two of these five states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. title: Chunk Recomputation under Real Document Revisions: Measuring Update Cost and Retrieval Quality of Fixed, Recursive, and Content-Defined Chunking
authors: Yuning Bian, Lele Xu et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Chunking strategies for retrieval-augmented generation are almost always evaluated on a static snapshot, yet the documents underlying a knowledge base continue to change.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because chunks are embedded independently, a boundary that moves after an edit forces unchanged text to be re-embedded. We measure this update cost on 120 pairs of adjacent Chinese and English Wikipedia revisions for three stateless chunkers (non-overlapping fixed-size, recursive paragraph-first, and content-defined chunking) under a strict byte-identical reuse rule and a frozen dense encoder.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On the 116-article common-success pool, with frozen, length-calibrated parameters, fixed-size chunking recomputes 57-68% of its full new-version embedding-input workload, recursive chunking 38-56%, and content-defined chunking 43-54% (it failed on 4 of 62 Chinese articles), while at these parameters mean evidence recall under a fixed 2048-token retrieval budget differs by less than two percentage points within either language. A cost-only parameter grid shows that the ranking of the two content-aware chunkers changes with chunk-length settings, whereas non-overlapping fixed-size chunking has the highest recomputation cost in every length-matched condition.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Update cost is therefore a substantial, parameter-sensitive dimension that static retrieval evaluations do not expose and that should be reported alongside retrieval quality.

title: Readout Dependent Parameter Identifiability of Quantum Kernels
authors: Hyong Keun Park, Jahoon Jeong et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: A circuit parameter can change measured features without changing their projected Gaussian kernel.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

title: Perpendicular Magnetization from Crystallite Boundaries in Polycrystalline Antiferromagnetic γ-FeMn
authors: Rachel E. Maizel, Sachli Abdizadeh et al. (23 researchers)

slides.hook: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn_3Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic γ-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, γ-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: When the crystallite size D falls below approx 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density propto 1/D. This magnetization is accompanied by a room-temperature anomalous Hall conductivity exceeding 10 S/cm, comparable to that of single-crystalline Mn_3Sn.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our findings in manufacturing-friendly polycrystalline γ-FeMn redefine crystal defects as enablers, rather than impediments, for scalable antiferromagnetic memory.

title: Formation and Detectability of PSR J0653+0443-like Extremely Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars in the Milky Way
authors: Zhiwei Chen, Jihui Zhang et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Recently, the Five-hundred-meter-Aperture-Spherical-radio-Telescope (FAST) Galactic Plane Pulsar Snapshot (GPPS) survey discovers an extraordinary binary neutron star (BNS) system, PSR J0653+0443, possessing the highest known orbital eccentricity (eapprox0.992) among Galactic BNSs (Yang et al., 2026), which provides a unique probe into the formation and evolution of BNSs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this Letter, we perform compact binary population synthesis calculations with self-consistent neutron star spin evolution to model extremely eccentric BNS population detectable by the FAST GPPS survey, explicitly incorporating observational selection effects. We find that BNSs with e>0.99 constitute only sim0.6% of the detectable population, with an expected detection number of λ_{mathrm{GPPS}}approx0.31 over the full planned footprint.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Thus, although rare, systems as eccentric as PSR J0653+0443 are compatible with standard binary evolution. We further demonstrate that extremely eccentric BNSs arise preferentially from core-collapse supernovae, whereas imposing Plesssim0.1 s select older, more frequently recycled systems, which naturally reproduce the observed properties of PSR J0653+0443.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By contrast, future facilities are expected to enlarge the detectable highly eccentric BNS population, with SKA potentially detecting PSR J0653+0443-like systems and sub-mHz gravitational-wave detectors probing a larger population with e>0.9, enabling much more in-depth population-level constraints.

title: γhosts from the past: reheating neutron stars with supernova-sourced ALPs
authors: Debajit Bose, Sougata Ganguly et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can be copiously produced in the hot and dense environment of a core-collapse supernova.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: If their mass is within an order of magnitude of the supernova temperature, a non-negligible fraction of them will remain gravitationally bound to the neutron star remnant. This basin of ALPs can then decay to photons over the lifetime of the neutron star, thereby reheating it.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using the measured luminosities of several neutron stars, we close multiple windows in ALP parameter space while also satisfying the SN 1987A cooling constraint on the ALP-nucleon coupling. In particular, using the 35000 K upper limit on the temperature of the coldest neutron star observed, PSR J2144-3933, we derive the strongest upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling for 1-400 MeV ALP masses.

slides.content: Observations of a 2000 , {rm K}-hot neutron star in infrared observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope could reach ALP-photon couplings three orders lower and ALP masses one order lower than our current limits.

slides.hook: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact ((6,2,3)) codes, SSLP yields 66 candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly 15 are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders 2, 3, and 5.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This code also attains the minimum length n=6 among exact ((n, 2, ge 3)) codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.

title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use
authors: Yijiang River Dong, Zexue He et al. (12 researchers)

slides.hook: Memory enables language model assistants to maintain continuity across sessions and generate personalized responses, but knowing more about a user does not necessarily produce responses they prefer.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing evaluations assess memory capabilities without directly establishing whether memory use benefits the user. To study this gap, we collect approximately 1,000 pairwise judgments from 87 participants using their own ChatGPT queries and personal memories.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We find that memory-conditioned responses are not consistently preferred over responses generated without memory and in some cases, users strongly prefer the latter. Automatic evaluators also show limited agreement with users and favor memory-conditioned responses substantially more often than users do.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our findings motivate evaluation and optimization objectives that align memory use with the preferences of the people whose information is being used.

title: Peer-Relative Trust-Guided Update Screening for Robust Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning under Label-Flipping Attacks
authors: Ajay Kumar Shrestha & Sandhya Joshi

slides.hook: Trust and reputation mechanisms can reduce the influence of malicious clients in federated learning (FL), but strict update filtering is difficult under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data because honest local updates may temporarily reduce performance on a shared validation proxy.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Building on our earlier trust-based semi-decentralized FL (SDFL) framework, this paper operationalizes the trust signals and introduces peer-relative update screening that combines a robust validation-utility score with direction- and norm-based update quality. The method is evaluated with 50 MNIST clients, 20% persistent label-flip attackers, Dirichlet heterogeneity levels of 0.5 and 0.1, 100 communication rounds, and five paired random seeds.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Under moderate heterogeneity, the proposed method reaches 98.37% final accuracy while rejecting 95.82% of malicious updates and retaining 90.30% of benign updates; the final benign and malicious trust distributions are completely separated (KS=1.00). Under severe heterogeneity, it reaches 95.25% accuracy, rejects 88.55% of malicious updates, and retains 76.90% of benign updates (KS=0.96).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The study provides an empirically validated off-chain governance core that can feed blockchain-based audit and incentive layers in SDFL.

slides.hook: Geometric phase gates with addressed laser radiation are widely used in trapped-ion quantum computers to drive high-fidelity entangling gates on an arbitrary qubit pair of a larger ion chain.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such programmable connectivity exploits the collective phonons to mediate the desired interaction, while simultaneously achieving robustness to their thermal fluctuations by a careful calibration of the gate time with respect to the laser and vibrational-mode frequencies. Crosstalk errors can arise when the spectator qubits, which should ideally remain idle during the gate, are partially driven by the laser fields.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The minimal crosstalk, which is set by the laser beam size on the spectator ions, can be achieved when the addressing beams propagate perpendicular to the ion chain. However, this results in exciting the radial phonons, and can complicate achieving high-fidelities as the ion chain grows due to the so-called spectral mode crowding.

title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models
authors: Athira Gopal, Patil Prathamesh Pravin et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Multilingual language models can give different identity judgments when the same people's names are written in different scripts.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study this effect using 601 audited identity pairs with attested Devanagari and Latin forms, holding the question and relation fixed. Qwen2.5-7B's same-person accuracy falls from 35.1% in Latin to 8.5% in Devanagari under Marathi prompts, while different-person accuracy remains above 98%.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Evaluation across five models reveals distinct response biases, and reduced tokenization fragmentation does not reliably close the gap. Replicating the design on 374 audited Malayalam pairs built from the same entities reproduces the effect in a second script and language family: same-person accuracy falls to 5.3%, about half the matched Devanagari rate, while the margin still ranks matching above non-matching names at 0.925 AUROC.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results distinguish script-dependent discrimination from criterion placement and identify a causal site for improving identity judgments.

title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
authors: C. Grünsteidl, C. Kerschbaummayr et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

title: Progress Probes P^2: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Atiksh Bhardwaj, Edward W. Duan et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA π_{0.5} and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.

slides.hook: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment (S^2), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We find that S^2 correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. S^2 can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: With S^2, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference
authors: St John Grimbly, Nicolas Kuske et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: An embodied agent must prioritise among competing bodily needs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In active inference, it can respond to an urgent need by increasing the precision of information about that need or by increasing its preference for outcomes that relieve it. We compare these two interventions, separately and together, in a foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, and ask how each changes survival, perception and the body model the agent learns.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Precision sharpens interoceptive posteriors and improves survival. Preference reweighting keeps bodily states further from their lethal boundaries and changes the states from which the agent learns, so its learned model covers fewer need levels, with lower quality across all levels but slightly higher quality on the levels it visits.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Survival alone therefore gives an incomplete account of how a model prioritises needs and learns about its body.

title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
authors: Hanbo Xie, Yue Zhao et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.

title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
authors: Aman Behera, Namit Solanki et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Long-context models often use answer-bearing evidence less effectively when it appears away from a prompt boundary.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compare this position bias across Transformer, state-space, and hybrid Mamba architectures by moving one gold document through a fixed set of nine distractors. The evaluated Transformers show a beginning advantage that the evaluated state-space models lack, while both families favor evidence near the end.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A matched pure-versus-hybrid Mamba comparison points in the same direction but remains statistically uncertain. The family difference appears among models that can answer the task.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These exploratory results show that effective context use depends on the evaluated architecture family, capability, task, and prompt, without isolating the sequence mixer as the sole cause.

title: Multigroup Radiation Diffusion with Compton Scattering on a Moving Mesh: Implementation in RICH and Application to Tidal Disruption Events
authors: Itamar Giron, Menahem Krief et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Compton scattering exchanges energy between radiation and hot gas and changes the spectrum in high-energy astrophysical systems such as tidal disruption events (TDEs).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because it couples all photon energies and can act faster than the hydrodynamic time step, many radiation-hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations omit its spectral redistribution or treat its energy exchange in the gray approximation. We extend the multigroup flux-limited diffusion module of the moving-mesh RHD code RICH to include Compton scattering with the exact thermal Compton kernel.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In our semi-implicit scheme for the thermal radiative transfer equation, the temperature dependence of the kernel enters a generalized Fleck factor, and the group Compton operator conserves photon number and satisfies detailed balance. In equilibration tests, the scheme agrees with independent solutions, relaxes without absorption and emission to a Bose-Einstein spectrum, and remains stable for time steps that do not resolve the Compton equilibration timescale.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Outside the X-ray thermalization radii, its instantaneous X-ray production rate during the flash is comparable to or larger than the escaping X-ray luminosity, so it may contribute substantially to the X-ray emission from TDEs.

title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification
authors: Yawen Ouyang, Xinbo Zhang et al. (18 researchers)

slides.hook: Protein modification requires navigating an immense sequence space, yet wet-lab validation remains low-throughput and costly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Although computational paradigms including protein language models (PLMs), large language models (LLMs), and LLM-based agents have shown promise in protein modification, their relative efficacy across realistic experimental decision-making settings remains unclear. To bridge this gap, we introduce PFArena, a benchmark comprising four controlled task interfaces that cover single-mutant generation and multi-mutant ranking.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By providing varying levels of mutation fitness data, PFArena reflects four representative research scenarios characterized by differing degrees of prior experimental context. We assess six PLMs, six LLMs, and five LLM-based agents using complementary metrics to measure both peak and overall protein modification performance.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We release our code and benchmark suite to facilitate reproducible research in model-assisted protein modification.

title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
authors: Oem Trivedi, Robert J. Scherrer et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.

title: High-throughput Down-selection of Fusion Candidate Materials
authors: Elena Botica-Artalejo, Josh Randolph et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Developing radiation-resistant fusion reactor materials is constrained by the slow pace of conventional irradiation qualification methodologies, which usually require extensive one-at-a-time irradiation campaigns and post-irradiation characterization.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: At the current pace of development, we may not discover the materials necessary to deploy fusion power plants at desired rates. In this work, we present a high-throughput (HT) experimental framework for the accelerated down-selection of fusion-relevant, Cu-Cr-Ta RF antenna materials by integrating combinatorial synthesis, in situ ion irradiation, and multi-property screening within a unified workflow.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: A 2D compositional Cu-Cr-Ta gradient wafer was fabricated by physical vapor deposition and characterized using in situ ion irradiation transient grating spectroscopy I3TGS. Radiation-induced surface acoustic wave frequency fluctuations were used as a rapid proxy for primary defect accumulation, while thermal diffusivity measurements were obtained simultaneously during irradiation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This integrated methodology enabled an acceleration with respect to conventional irradiation approaches by more than 100 times, from months to hours to analyze 78 new materials.

title: FRB 20210601A: Extreme Temporal Clustering in a Repeating Fast Radio Burst Source as Evidence for a Hidden Class of Episodic Repeaters

slides.hook: Population studies of fast radio burst (FRB) repetition typically model sources using a single distribution of steady, time-averaged burst rates, yet individual sources show significant departures from this assumption.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present FRB 20210601A, a source discovered by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment FRB project (CHIME/FRB) that represents the most extreme such departure yet identified. The source produced at least nine bursts within a single 106.5 s interval -- the highest instantaneous burst rate yet reported from a repeating FRB source at gtrsim 2 Jy ms fluences -- yet remained otherwise undetected despite sim 320 hr of exposure spanning 7 yr.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The active interval occurred while the source was in a side-lobe of the CHIME/FRB digitized beams, implying an instantaneous burst rate gtrsim2.3times higher (gtrsim 21 bursts) at main-lobe sensitivity. The source's intense, brief burst storm flanked by apparent quiescence despite substantial exposure is unique among the CHIME/FRB repeater sample, although its burst morphology, excess dispersion measure (rm{DM_{excess}} sim 360 pc cm^{-3}), Faraday rotation measure (|rm{RM_{excess}}| sim 150-170 rad m^{-2}), and temporal scattering (τlesssim 0.37 ms at 600 MHz) are otherwise typical.

title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
authors: Akash Gupta, Austin Guo et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The critical temperature increases with pressure, from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa, and we find no phase separation at 3000 and 4000 K up to 100 GPa. The slope of the critical curve decreases substantially between 0.3 and 30 GPa, and the curve nearly flattens above about 30 GPa and 2000 K, where molecules begin to give way to atomic species.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together with previous studies, our results suggest that silicates, water and ammonia separate from hydrogen in sequence as planets cool, with implications for their compositional, thermal and structural evolution.

title: Predictive Multiplicity in Cell-Fate Assignment: Label-Free Rashomon Sets and the Limits of Per-Cell Certification
authors: Arjun Bhupatiraju & Abhiram Bhupatiraju

slides.hook: Single-cell trajectory inference maps transcriptomic measurements onto developmental continua, yet configurations that fit the data equally well can assign conflicting cell fates.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: FateMultiplicity is a label-free framework that constructs a statistically admissible model set, or Rashomon set, without lineage labels, by evaluating model discrepancy on cross-fitted held-out genes under non-inferiority testing calibrated against random-seed variation. Multiplicity is large and depends more on the diversity of the model space than its size: twelve configurations of a second algorithm expose 20.0% of cells where twenty-four of the first expose 3.8%.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Whether the per-cell certified fate margin FM yields more reliable assignments than the fitted model already provides is then tested, and it does not. On simulation ground truth, on the same cells, FM discriminates misassignment at AUC 0.682, against 0.965 for the baseline configuration's own decision margin (p = 0.003) and 0.854 for a seed-dispersion baseline.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Two constructions survive: a margin-erosion ratio separates real from spurious branch points in simulation (AUC 0.890, untested on real data), and against clonally observed fate, uncertified cells disagree with their clone's outcome 16.4 percentage points more often than certified cells (p < 0.001).

title: Attention over noisy examples: generalization and memorization in the exponential Hopfield network
authors: Francesco Alemanno

slides.hook: In Hebbian learning from examples, a Hopfield network retrieves archetypes seen only through noisy examples.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study it in the exponential Hopfield model: one softmax attention step with the unlabelled examples as keys. A signal-to-noise analysis gives the overlap with an unseen archetype in closed form: a majority-rule law in which an attention entropy replaces the dataset entropy.

slides.content: At high temperature the archetype is lost in the crosstalk; at low temperature the softmax freezes on the closest training example, as in a random energy model, and the layer memorizes. slides.content: On structured datasets, such as MNIST and fashion-MNIST, the best accuracy lies beyond the freezing.

title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO_3: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy

slides.hook: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions.

slides.content: At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. slides.hook: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity χ_0, the Electrostatic Rigidity mathcal{R}---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus mathcal{A}. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d^{5} configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital.

slides.hook: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper-type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting-edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier-density-dependent optical responses.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA)_2PbI_4 under infrared excitation, resonant with the two-photon energy of its excitonic transition. title: Constant-Depth Quantum Barrier Option Pricing via a Static Bivariate Oracle Framework
authors: Ji-Hui Mo & Yuan-Hong Tao

slides.hook: Quantum amplitude estimation offers a theoretical quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo methods for financial derivative pricing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, extending gate-based algorithms to path-dependent barrier options has historically been hampered by sequential path discretization, where tracking price paths across d monitoring dates incurs a linear escalation in qubit footprint and gate depth (mathcal{O}(d)), posing severe coherence challenges for near-term quantum processors. In this work, we present a constant-depth quantum pricing framework that fundamentally eliminates the temporal dependency of barrier monitoring.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Leveraging the Brownian reflection principle and Girsanov theorem, we project the continuous supremum dynamics onto a static bivariate joint distribution of the terminal price S_T and running supremum M_T. This allows decoupling dynamic boundary checks into a static bivariate oracle comprising two parallel comparators and a dual-controlled rotation gate.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Finally, the framework seamlessly extends to nonlinear exotic payoffs lacking analytical solutions, establishing a noise-resilient pathway toward practical quantum advantage in computational finance.

title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Rustam Arabov, Konstantin Sozykin et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

slides.hook: We present an error-controlled framework for the quantum simulation of non-Markovian open-system dynamics in Gaussian environments.

slides.content: For a system coupled linearly to a Gaussian environment with zero mean, the bath's influence on the reduced dynamics is completely determined by its two-time correlation kernel. This allows us to replace the microscopic environment with an equivalent bath that has the same kernel.

slides.content: Here, we investigate an anisotropic Dicke QB with Kerr nonlinearity, focusing on the role of PTs in the charging process of the QB system. title: Multi-orbit S-star probes of Lorentz violation at the Galactic Center
authors: Jia-Yuan Fang, Jian-Ming Yan et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We investigate the potential of Galactic-center S-star observations to probe Lorentz violation in the minimal pure-gravity Standard-Model Extension (SME), focusing on parameter degeneracies associated with anisotropic orbital signatures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We construct simulated astrometric and spectroscopic observations of S2 and S55 using fiducial orbital and Galactic-center parameters based on the multi-star solution from the GRAVITY Collaboration and evolve the stellar trajectories using the leading Lorentz-violating two-body dynamics supplemented by the Schwarzschild first-post-Newtonian (1PN) correction. Separate Fisher-matrix analyses of S2 and S55 each resolve seven of the eight independent SME directions, while their joint analysis resolves all eight directions by combining complementary projections from the differently oriented orbits.

title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
authors: Gabriele Dominici, Teague McMillan et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.

title: Riding the Fixed-Point Curve: Image Classification in the Continuous Thought Machine
authors: Thomas Hannagan

slides.hook: The Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) is a recurrent network that attends to inputs and makes predictions based on the synchronization between its neurons.

authors: Zhen Cao, F. Aharonian et al. (341 researchers)

slides.hook: Ultra-relativistic magnetic monopoles traversing the atmosphere are expected to initiate extensive air showers characterized by a muon deficit and a compact lateral profile.

slides.content: Using 1438.81 live days of data from the LHAASO-KM2A array, we present a search for these cosmic particles within the Lorentz factor range of 10^5 to 10^7. slides.hook: Computer-model calibration is usually undertaken in service of prediction, yet neither Bayesian Kennedy-O'Hagan (KOH) calibration nor amortized simulation-based inference is built to control the predictive error of the calibrated simulator.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: When parameters are weakly identified or the data-model discrepancy is misspecified, the simulator-output bands induced by a nominal posterior level can be far from nominal. We propose a two-layer framework that targets predictive miscoverage directly.

slides.hook: Nonparametric estimation of joint probability distributions is a core problem in statistics, which is notoriously challenging with high-dimensional data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Such challenges also arise with conditional distribution estimation and have led to flexible algorithms that aim to tackle the ''curse of dimensionality'' by exploiting predictive structures of lower dimension than the ambient space. In this paper, we study the use of such conditional distribution estimators to estimate joint distributions by factorizing the latter in an ''autoregressive'' way.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that for loss functions satisfying a subadditivity property, bounds on the convergence rate of an autoregressive estimator can be derived from bounds on the convergence rate of the conditional distribution estimators. These bounds relate the difficulty of estimating the joint distribution to that of estimating the most challenging factor in the autoregressive factorization.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results support nonparametric autoregressive estimation as a practical approach to flexible joint distribution estimation.

title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
authors: K. Fabitha, T. Runggaldier et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Concatenation of quantum repeater nodes has been proposed as a means to distribute entanglement efficiently across future long-distance networks.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we demonstrate a trapped-ion repeater node that establishes photonic entanglement over a 17 km fiber traversing a city, moving beyond laboratory-only prototypes. The node comprises two atomic ions coupled to an optical cavity.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: First, a detailed characterization is performed of the long fiber channel and of ion-photon entanglement distributed across it. Next, a repeater-node protocol is implemented, achieving entanglement between a local photon and a remote photon with a Bell-state fidelity of 81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}%.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results demonstrate that trapped-ion repeater-node technology can operate over existing city-scale fiber infrastructure and represent a step toward distributed quantum repeater networks.

slides.hook: Spaceflight-associated motion sickness, including space motion sickness (SMS) and terrestrial readaptation motion sickness (TRMS), has presented as the most operationally limiting effect on the human in the days following a gravity transition.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Published data suggest that astronaut head movements provoke symptoms, but those studies rarely controlled for them. Most previous studies use postflight retrospective reporting and have not quantified temporal dynamics or persistence of symptoms; no study has published motion sickness in a cohort of commercial flyers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Here, we comprehensively evaluate SMS and TRMS within commercial flyers (N=8; 4F, 4M) for the first time, across two commercial missions of short duration (Polaris Dawn and Fram2). Utilizing a standard reporting methodology, we find an 87.5% incidence of SMS, which persisted for at least three days on orbit in 25% of crewmembers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings establish a systematic baseline for spaceflight-associated motion sickness, informing its operational impact and salience as human spaceflight missions expand in accessibility and scope.

title: Approaching Backpropagation Accuracy with Weight Perturbation on MNIST
authors: Patrick Inoue

slides.hook: Weight perturbation (WP) estimates learning directions from random parameter perturbations and a scalar change in loss, without backpropagating derivatives.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We examine how batch size, training duration, and estimator stabilization affect its attainable accuracy in fully connected MNIST networks. In the shallow configuration, large-batch training reaches approximately 97% test accuracy, compared with an early backpropagation (BP) reference near 97.5--98%.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The same comparison exposes a substantial efficiency gap: under a ten-epoch budget, shallow WP reaches 90.2%, whereas the reported BP reference reaches 97.4%. Epoch-indexed curves show diminishing returns from increasing batch size beyond 4,000.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, the results identify near-BP accuracy as a configuration- and budget-dependent possibility, rather than evidence of equal efficiency or an unconditional accuracy guarantee across depth.

title: Consistent Distributed Invariant EKF SLAM with Point and Object Features
authors: Mengya Xu, Xianjia Yu et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Multi-robot SLAM allows robots to improve their estimates by exchanging map information, but repeated exchanges create unknown correlations between local estimators.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Covariance intersection (CI) can fuse estimates without tracking these correlations. In right-invariant extended Kalman filter (RI-EKF) SLAM, however, point features obtain their invariant errors through the robot rotation, so a neighbor's map estimate is expressed in its own error coordinates and is correlated with its pose, and cannot be fused by CI directly.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: This paper presents Joint-CI, a unified fusion method for distributed RI-EKF SLAM with point, object, and mixed point--object maps. Using a neighboring robot's local posterior and an inter-robot observation, a joint estimate of the receiving robot's pose and the common features is constructed in the receiving robot's error coordinates, retaining the robot--feature and feature--feature correlations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Monte Carlo simulations and a real-world dataset-derived experiment show that Joint-CI improves estimation accuracy while maintaining consistent, mildly conservative uncertainty.

title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). The metallicity of the intracluster light
authors: Euclid Collaboration, J. B. Golden-Marx et al. (323 researchers)

slides.hook: Colour provides key information to constrain the stellar population of the intracluster light (ICL), the diffuse light within galaxy clusters.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We derive radial colour profiles (Y_mathrm{E}-H_mathrm{E}, J_mathrm{E}-H_mathrm{E}, I_mathrm{E}-H_mathrm{E}) of the brightest central galaxy (BCG) and ICL for 168 galaxy clusters from the Dark Energy Survey redMaPPer catalogue within the redshift range 0.1 < z < 0.75 and halo mass M_{rm 200m} > 10^{14.05}M_odot/h, within the Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). By stacking the light profiles measured using elliptical annuli on the BCG and ICL images, we reliably measure the ICL colour out to approximately 300 kpc, over which we find a colour gradient, with the ICL becoming bluer than the BCG out to approximately 150 kpc.

title: Optical microelectrode arrays for differential readout of electrical and mechanical signals in cardiac cells
authors: Alessandro Leronni & Rosalia Moreddu

slides.hook: Simultaneous assessment of electrical excitation and mechanical contraction is essential for understanding cardiac cell function, yet these two processes are commonly measured with separate techniques or invasively.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, changes in cellular electrical activity modulate local charge redistribution in optical microelectrodes and are converted into fluorescence signals, while cell contraction induces membrane displacement that contributes an additional mechanical component to the optical readout. authors: Jacob de Nobel, Diederick Vermetten et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Since their introduction, modern evolution strategies, such as the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES), have become established as powerful methods for continuous black-box optimization.

title: Coarse-Graining Agent-Based Models of Bacterial Infections
authors: Wesley J. M. Ridgway & Raymond J. Spiteri

comments.author: Dr. Clara Wu (MIT CSAIL)
comments.text: What are the thermodynamic boundaries of this configuration?

slides.hook: Agent-based models (ABMs) provide a natural framework for representing cell-level rules and spatial heterogeneity in bacterial infections, but their computational cost limits their use for macroscopic tissue-scale simulations and broad parameter exploration.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We derive a deterministic coarse-grained description for a class of bacterial-infection ABMs in which immune cells and extracellular bacteria diffuse, immune cells ingest nearby bacteria, and intracellular bacterial loads evolve through prescribed birth and clearance processes. The first coarse-grained model is a semidiscrete reaction--diffusion system that retains a discrete internal state for each immune-cell bacterial load while representing cell and bacterial populations by continuum concentration fields.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The key technical step is the derivation of state-dependent effective ingestion rates from the microscopic ABM parameters: these rates are obtained by solving an auxiliary diffusion problem around a single bacterium and computing the flux of immune cells into the interaction region. We then take a continuum limit in the internal state variable, yielding a state-structured reaction--diffusion system in which intracellular dynamics appear as advection and diffusion in state space.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The resulting framework preserves the rule-based structure of the ABM while producing PDE models that are substantially more tractable for large-scale simulation and parameter studies.

title: CircuitATLAS: Agentic reasoning over a systems neuroscience knowledge graph for target discovery in circuitopathies
authors: Gabriel Ocana-Santero & Marko Tvrdic

slides.hook: Drug discovery for neurological disease has traditionally centered on the molecules altered by disease.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: But the molecules that cause pathology are not necessarily the best points from which to reverse it. Here, we ask which otherwise unaltered molecular control points can be engaged to restore pathological neural circuits toward functional states.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present CircuitATLAS, a provenance-grounded systems-neuroscience knowledge graph and agentic framework for target discovery in circuitopathies. It structures literature-derived relationships across diseases, phenotypes, electrophysiology, circuits, brain regions, cell types and molecular effectors, while deliberately excluding direct disease-gene and disease-protein edges to reduce shortcut reasoning.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: CircuitATLAS thus provides a framework for discovering therapeutics based not only on what is molecularly disrupted in disease, but on what can be controlled to restore circuit function.

title: Phase shifts and fluctuations from motional, relativistic, and dark-matter effects in ion-trap clocks
authors: Alexander Bott, Fabio Di Pumpo et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Ions possess both center-of-mass motion and internal states, rendering trapped-ion optical clocks susceptible to perturbations of both degrees of freedom, which results in systematic shifts and fluctuations with motional and relativistic origins.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We develop a quantum theory that connects these effects to filter functions determined by the employed pulse sequences and show how the interrogation can be tailored to suppress or enhance specific perturbations. Our treatment includes laser frequency noise and motional effects such as recoil and Doppler shifts, micromotion and excess micromotion, as well as state-dependent trap imperfections and accelerations, e.g., caused by Stark shifts.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We further account for relativistic effects including time dilation and the mass defect, and show how the same framework can be applied to hypothetical dark-matter signals. By considering ensemble-averaged phases and their variances, we characterize both systematic shifts and fluctuations, while asynchronous operation relative to the Paul-trap drive allows motional fluctuations to average down between runs.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results provide a unified framework for characterizing and controlling the systematic and statistical contributions that determine the trueness and precision of trapped-ion optical clocks.

title: Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery
authors: Zachary Cutts, John Coller et al. (12 researchers)

slides.hook: Despite breakthroughs in AI-driven molecular generation, existing discovery pipelines operate largely in silico, with wet-lab feedback reserved for validation rather than iterative improvement.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Whether large language model (LLM)-based reasoning agents can accelerate de novo discovery by iterating with lab data remains unproven. Here we use protein-binding aptamer design as a sandbox (1-2 week cycles, 1-3 per candidate) to demonstrate a wet lab in a closed loop with AI systems.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We tasked agentic pipelines with developing aptamer binders against α-thrombin and myoglobin across three design-test-improve cycles (sim1,000 candidates per round; sim4,400 constructs). Statistically significant, bead-corrected on-target hit rates among new candidates rose across rounds from 0.0% in Round 1 to 26.0% in Round 2 and 42.1% in Round 3 on α-thrombin (37.1% excluding literature motif descendants), and from 10.2% in Round 1 to 3.7% in Round 2 and 33.5% in Round 3 on myoglobin.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We demonstrate that empirical lab data is more valuable than existing computational proxies, showing how iterative experimental feedback enables AI agents to diagnose assay artifacts and refine molecular designs across rounds.

title: Collective Benefits and Efficiency in Coupled Echo State Networks
authors: Polyphony Bruna, Rick Dale et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Simple aggregation of independent responses ("wisdom of crowds") generally improves collective performance through statistical facilitation, but interaction among members can sometimes hinder group outcomes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, under certain circumstances, coordination studies show that interacting groups can outperform their individual members and nominal groups, and interaction can also be more efficient than independence. We present a reservoir computing model to investigate how interaction can enhance joint performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

slides.content: Echo state networks were trained independently to identify Japanese speakers from vowel recordings and tested jointly with and without coupled feedback. Model pairs reproduced the dyadic advantage reported by Bahrami et al.

title: Crucial role of magnetic dipole and anomalous field dependence in mathrm{NiPS_3}
authors: Do Hoon Kiem, Muhammad Nauman et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: mathrm{NiPS_3} has attracted considerable attention, yet the origin of its intriguing magnetic behaviors remains elusive due to limited insight into its low-energy anisotropy.

slides.hook: Optimal approximate state conversion is a fundamental task in quantum resource theories, yet existing solutions are largely tailored to specific distinguishability measures and resource theories.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We show that every optimal approximate-conversion problem in the three paradigmatic majorization-based quantum resource theories of non-uniformity, bipartite pure-state entanglement, and pure-state coherence reduces exactly to one of only four elementary taut-string constructions. This holds for problems generated by Schur-convex spectral distances and by a broad family of quantum divergences satisfying a natural reduction property with respect to the corresponding equivalence group.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The resulting framework encompasses a broad class of physically relevant distinguishability measures, including the trace distance, all unitarily invariant norms, quantum relative entropy, maximal quantum f-divergences, and the α-z Rényi relative entropies. The increment vector of the corresponding taut string completely determines both the optimal approximation error and a canonical optimal state.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results establish a common geometric framework for approximate quantum resource conversion, revealing that a broad class of seemingly different optimization problems is governed by the same taut-string geometric principle.

title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
authors: Zhou Zhang, Hanqun Cao et al. (8 researchers)

slides.hook: Designing RNA molecules that bind to target protein structures requires generating both an RNA conformation and its bound complex geometry, without assuming a predefined binding site.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing approaches generally model these coupled processes within a unified representation, entangling RNA conformation generation with protein-relative placement. In this work, we introduce RiboBridge, a structure-first framework that separates RNA conformational generation from protein--RNA assembly through cross-frame interaction geometry.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: RiboBridge first proposes multiple candidate RNA-binding interfaces on the protein surface, generates canonical RNA conformations within a pretrained RNA structural latent space (RiboSphere), and then predicts protein--RNA interaction constraints to bridge the independently defined RNA and protein coordinate frames. The resulting interaction geometry is converted into a geometrically consistent protein-relative pose through rigid placement.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Component ablations and stage-wise diagnostics further characterize the contributions of RNA conformational generation, interaction prediction, and rigid placement, identifying the main sources of complex-recovery error.

title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
authors: Matthew A. Delmont, Yu Wu et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.
