authors: Eduardo D. Sontag

slides.hook: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

title: Predicting Music Valence and Arousal via Textual and Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Language Models
authors: Chi-En Dai, Chih-Pin Tan et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: While arousal can be reliably predicted from musical audio, emotional valence remains difficult to model due to its subjective and context-dependent nature.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this work, we investigate the potential of in-context learning (ICL) with large language models to advance continuous valence and arousal prediction. Rather than predicting emotion scores directly, our framework leverages contextual demonstrations from an auxiliary dataset to refine the initial predictions produced by a small, task-specific base model.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We systematically evaluate a text-based ICL variant using lyrics and generated audio captions, alongside a multimodal variant that incorporates raw audio signals. Using the entire MER60 dataset strictly as a held-out test set, our experiments demonstrate substantial performance gains, particularly for valence.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings suggest that training-free ICL offers an effective inference-time strategy for current language models to predict continuous music emotion.

slides.hook: Strongly connected components (SCCs) characterize modular structure in directed networks but are fragile to single node failures.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study strongly biconnected components (SBCs), which are the set of nodes in which every node pair remains mutually reachable after the removal of any single node, as a more robust notion of connectivity. Using a generating function formalism, we derive the size of the giant SBC and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removal.

slides.content: We show that the giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly due to stricter connectivity requirements. We also applied our theoretical framework to real-world biological networks including gene regulatory networks and neural connectome.

title: SaltyMeta: a curated benchmark and protein language model-informed web tool for salty peptide prediction
authors: Wanchao Chen, Wen Li et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Excess sodium intake remains a major public health challenge, while salty and saltiness-enhancing peptides offer a potential route to preserve sensory saltiness in reduced-sodium foods.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Machine-learning studies of salty peptides, however, are constrained by small datasets, heterogeneous evidence standards, uncertain negative labels, and sequence similarity leakage. title: TRACE: Traversability-aware Reactive Navigation via VLM-driven Adaptive Constraints Estimation
authors: Mario A. V. Saucedo, Midhun Edatharam Kunnath et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: This paper presents TRACE, a traversability-aware reactive navigation framework designed for the autonomous operation of ground robots in unstructured forest environments.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Unlike traditional approaches, TRACE leverages VLM-based confidence maps from positive and negative natural-language prompt sets and combines them through evidential fusion to produce a dense traversability map that prioritizes the terrain based on signs of previously traversed paths. Traversability-annotated points are then extracted and used to derive the left and right boundaries of the traversable path via percentile binning followed by spline or regularized polynomial fitting.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: These boundaries are then incorporated as soft barrier constraints within an NMPC formulation, enabling safe and adaptive path following in complex natural environments. Rigorous experimental trials carried out in real-life forest environments demonstrate TRACE ability for smooth navigation in cluttered, deformable, and visually ambiguous terrains.

title: Tracing model-generated DNA with position-independent watermarking
authors: Kimon Antonios Provatas1, Christos Galanopoulos et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Genomic language models can write synthetic DNA that carries no record of its origin.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: A generation-time watermark could provide a provenance signal, if a verifier can detect it using only the DNA sequence, a key, and published detector settings, without knowing where the generated region starts, which strand it lies on, or how it was divided into six-base tokens. We embed the SynthID tournament watermark in two genomic language models, Carbon and GENERator-v2.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The verifier searches both strands, every start position, and four window lengths, and corrects its decision for the whole search. In a detection cohort of 1,544 held-out prompts, it found all 3,088 marked sequences per model, unedited and after one substituted, inserted, or deleted base.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results show statistical detection, not biological function, secret-key security, or robustness to an editor who sees the detector.

slides.hook: Identifying the quantum signatures of classical chaos remains a central question in quantum physics, and quantum scrambling provides a new perspective on this correspondence.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study two distinct limits of the same model to examine how the correspondence between chaos and scrambling changes across different regimes. The thermodynamic-limit anisotropic Dicke model exhibits a close correspondence between chaos and scrambling, whereas this correspondence breaks down in the large-frequency-ratio limit of the anisotropic Rabi model (ARM).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The contrasting chaotic behavior in the two limits originates from the different numbers of classical degrees of freedom, whereas their similar scrambling behavior stems from eigenstate delocalization. This implies that, in the large-frequency-ratio limit, eigenstate delocalization alone is insufficient to qualify the ARM as a classically chaotic model.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This finding suggests that identifying chaos in quantum systems requires jointly considering the classical degrees of freedom and eigenstate delocalization.

title: A Unified Unsupervised Framework for Genome-Wide Association Studies in Heterogeneous Populations
authors: Xiong Shen, Zhenshuang Tang et al. (17 researchers)

slides.hook: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have greatly advanced the discovery of genetic variants underlying complex traits and diseases.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Yet in heterogeneous populations, existing GWAS strategies typically either pool all individuals under an assumption of population homogeneity or perform meta-analysis across predefined subgroups, both of which are limited when latent genetic heterogeneity attenuates subgroup-specific effects and masks true associations or subgroup labels are imprecise. Here we present UCALM, a unified unsupervised framework that infers genetically homogeneous subgroups directly from the data and integrates subgroup-specific GWAS with a novel layered meta-analysis method to capture both shared and subgroup-specific association signals.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Through extensive simulations and analyses of large-scale human and livestock cohorts, including the UK Biobank (n approx 487{,}000) and a heterogeneous pig cohort (n approx 85{,}000), we demonstrate that UCALM substantially alleviated the mean genomic inflation across 24 UK Biobank traits to 1.17 compared with 1.43 for GLM and 1.37 for LDAK-KVIK, and further revealed 74 loci in the pig cohort that were previously obscured by conventional approaches. Our results establish a robust and broadly applicable strategy for association mapping in structured populations and improve the resolution of genetic signals across diverse species.

title: CrystalAR: Autoregressive Modeling for Symmetric Crystal Generation
authors: Ziqiao Meng, Rongsheng Chen et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Deep generative modeling has achieved remarkable progress in crystal generation.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Given the rich symmetries inherent in crystalline structures, recent work has sought to explicitly incorporate space-group symmetry into generative models, enabling more effective exploration of novel symmetry templates. Yet introducing symmetry templates increases the combinatorial complexity of stoichiometric relationships between atomic species and crystallographic sites, while creating a fundamental tension between flexible exploration of discrete crystallographic templates and faithful realization of these templates as continuous three-dimensional structures.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To address these challenges, we propose CrystalAR, a unified autoregressive framework that models Wyckoff symmetry templates and complete crystal structures within a single generative sequence. Specifically, CrystalAR reformulates continuous coordinate generation as a symmetry-conditioned hierarchy of discrete spatial localization decisions, autoregressively refining the positions of all symmetry-inequivalent sites across resolution levels while jointly modeling their spatial configuration within each level.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results suggest that symmetry-template generation can be retained alongside broadly competitive de novo generation performance and competitive CSP without reliance on symmetry templates retrieved from prior data, providing a promising alternative paradigm for symmetry-preserving crystal generation.

title: Measuring the Reasoning-Action Coupling in Driving Vision-Language-Action Models through Counterfactuals
authors: Gabriel Manalu, Saad Wazir et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models bring an appealing form of explainability to a safety-critical domain, since a system that can state the reasons for its maneuvers offers the transparency that deployment and public trust in autonomous driving demand.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These models read the world into language before they act on it, describing the scene and reasoning over it in text that ranges from chain-of-thought to multi-stage question answering on the way to a trajectory. That framing quietly assumes two separable properties, namely that the trajectory follows the generated reasoning and that the generated reasoning tracks the causes that actually produce the trajectory.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: To thoroughly investigate these properties, we apply causal, counterfactual interventions to four driving VLAs across different benchmarks. First, we perturb the models' own reasoning and show that altering its meaning produces small trajectory changes relative to blanking the same models' camera inputs, a pattern that persists across benchmarks and model architectures.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Overall, our findings indicate that the reasoning these models present to account for their resulting driving behavior is weakly coupled to that behavior itself, pointing to limits on the explainability these systems are intended to provide.

title: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation
authors: Kodur Sai Vinay Sathvik, Kakoli Bora et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Theoretically, we show that no finite penalty guarantees compliance near a dietary-rule threshold, establish approximation guarantees for greedy allocation under utilitarian and smoothed Nash objectives in the stock-free model before filtering, and characterize the scale invariance of Nash welfare. We also use the minimax theorem to analyze rotating shared meals.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: In simulation, shared meals reduce pantry use by about one-third, and weekly rotation increases the worst-off member's utility by 38% over the best fixed meal.

title: A Catalog of Spectral Properties for DESI DR1 Quasars
authors: Qiaoya Wu & Yue Shen

slides.hook: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is carrying out a five-year spectroscopic survey designed to map the large-scale structure of the Universe and obtain spectra for millions of galaxies and quasars over a wide redshift range.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present a value-added catalog of spectral properties for 1,717,774 unique quasars (1,774,723 spectra) in the DESI Data Release 1. We perform a uniform spectral decomposition of the quasar continuum, host galaxy emission (at z<1), and FeII emission, and measure the line properties of major broad and narrow emission lines from Lyα to Hα covered by DESI spectra.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We also provide single-epoch black hole mass estimates (from Hβ, MgII, and CIV), bolometric luminosities, and Eddington ratios for these quasars. We provide systemic redshifts that account for the intrinsic velocity shifts of individual lines; they agree with the DESI pipeline redshifts to within 500~km s^{-1} for 88.6% of the sample, and are most useful at z>1 where the pipeline redshift is heavily constrained by blueshifted high-ionization lines.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

slides.hook: Protein mutation effect generation asks a model to describe the functional consequence of a point mutation in natural language.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing protein-to-text systems typically encode mutation information into undifferentiated representations, overlooking the organization of mutation-induced evidence across structural and biochemical factors. We propose RipplePLM, a mutation-aware generation framework centered on Direct-Distal Cross-Attention (DDCA).

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By constructing a residue-level Mutation Perturbation Field from pre-trained protein language models, DDCA leverages predicted contact maps to organize mutation representations into two pathways: the mutation site's immediate contact neighborhood and its multi-hop distal context. To complement this structural decomposition, we further introduce the Property Latent Chain (PLChain), which injects expert-guided supervision of biochemical property changes (e.g., thermostability and optimal pH) into the LLM hidden-state pathway through latent property tokens.

title: Boundary exceptional point driven chiral switch of topological edge states
authors: Bikashkali Midya & Barsa Rani Sahu

slides.hook: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: By tuning the boundary gain and loss parameters, we exploit the finite-size hybridization of two mid-gap topological edge states to analytically derive the exact coordinates of boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs), Γ_{rm EP}=pm i v^{N}/w^{N-1}, at which these states undergo coalescence. We demonstrate that dynamically encircling these boundary EPs facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Depending on the orientation of the encircling loop, this protocol allows a topological edge state localized at one boundary to be either transferred to the opposite edge with perfect fidelity or returned to its starting position through a double switching process. Importantly, since the non-Hermiticity remains strictly confined to the boundaries, this chiral transport occurs without affecting the energy spectrum of the bulk bands.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results establish a minimal framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch that is experimentally verifiable and capable of being controlled through boundary non-Hermitian driving.

title: LAST-V2X: Language-Driven Adaptive Scenario Synthesis and Testing for Communication-Induced Failures in V2X Safety Applications

slides.hook: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication enables connected vehicles to make safety-critical decisions, but delayed, missing, or incorrect information can compromise driving safety.

slides.content: Systematically testing such failures is challenging because traffic interactions, communication conditions, and application responses must be jointly configured to produce meaningful scenarios. authors: Ryan Smith, Sabrina Yue Wang et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched.

slides.content: We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size N, which goes from mathcal{O}({rm poly}(N)) to mathcal{O}(1) for reference states with non-vanishing energy density.

title: In Vivo Length Distributions as Mechanistic Fingerprints of Pathological Protein Aggregation
authors: Matthew W. Cotton, David Klenerman et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Modern imaging techniques can resolve individual pathological protein aggregates in postmortem human samples, providing detailed measurements of aggregate size distributions that are inaccessible with conventional bulk approaches.

title: Gate-Based Feature Importance in Simulation-Based Inference for EEG: A Cautionary Tale
authors: Shrivatsa Deshmukh, Sasha Brenner et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Simulation-based inference (SBI) provides a powerful way to fit mechanistic models to data, but offers little insight into which information in the data shapes the inferred parameter values.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: It could therefore benefit from robust and inexpensive interpretability methods. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
authors: Daniel Kaplan, Gabriel Kotliar et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. slides.content: Spectral analysis and multidimensional scaling reveal a geometry dominated by a small number of directions. slides.content: These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.

title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
authors: Ali Atiah Alzahrani

slides.hook: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards.

title: TexFlow: learning crystallographic texture on SO(3) manifold via normalizing flows
authors: Gowtham Nimmal Haribabu, Tarakram Ramgopal et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Crystallographic texture is an important microstructural feature that statistically describes the orientations of grains in polycrystalline materials.

slides.content: Conventional texture analysis relies on the orientation distribution functions and pole figures, which are essential for interpreting the texture of a given material specimen but do not, by themselves, provide a direct framework for predictive modeling of process-structure-property linkages. slides.hook: Topic models learn gene programs from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, and the same counts are then used to test which genes and donors are associated with those programs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

On a 104,400-cell lupus cohort with 300 permuted null genes per run, naive tests rejected 36% of null gene-topic pairs at a nominal 5% level, and the usual two-way split rejected 38%, because the encoder sees the tested gene's own held-out count.

A label-free interferon program shifts in held-out counts in the lupus cohort and in a pre-specified COVID-19 cohort, and donor-level topic usage predicts disease (AUROC 0.96) beyond cell-type proportions (0.86 and 0.58 in the two cohorts).

authors: Tanmoy Kanti Halder, Akash Ghosh et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in biological reasoning; however, genomic disease inference remains largely dependent on memorized gene-disease associations rather than understanding biological pathways.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This shortcut learning undermines robustness and generalization, and breaks down when molecular identifiers are unavailable. We present GenoMorph, a multimodal genomic reasoning framework that shifts disease prediction from associative gene-disease mapping toward pathway-grounded reasoning.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: GenoMorph couples a frozen DNA foundation model with question-conditioned cross-attention fusion, self-adaptive latent reasoning (LatentSp), a residual reasoning gate for iterative genomic evidence reinjection, and rejection sampling fine-tuning regularized by hierarchical optimal transport (OT). title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
authors: Junyu Lin, Bosong Qi et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.

slides.hook: Biological reaction networks often exhibit complex transient behavior that cannot be explained solely by the analysis of steady states or long-term persistence.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Existing structural approaches identify persistent system properties and have considered transitions between organizations, but do not provide a general criterion for admissible transitions between arbitrary species configurations. We introduce admissible transitions, a new structural concept that describes feasible changes between species subsets using only reaction network structure and feasible reaction fluxes, independently of kinetic parameters.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We prove that solutions of reaction-based ordinary differential equation systems induce canonical sequences of admissible transitions with a fundamental asymmetry: closure-building transitions are uniquely determined by network structure, whereas downward transitions are generally non-unique and depend on the realized trajectory. This establishes a structural layer linking network topology to transient system evolution.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: By extending structural reaction network analysis from persistent states to transient dynamics, the proposed theory provides a general, kinetics-independent framework for analyzing reachability, organization formation, and transient behavior in biological systems.

title: Early-stage local melting during solid-state sintering of a Cu-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf alloy: A combined thermodynamic and kinetic analysis
authors: Andrea Skolakova, Hana Lesakova et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Complex concentrated alloys (CCAs) combining elements from 3d transition and refractory groups, specifically Cu-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf-based shape memory systems, exhibit excellent functional properties but present significant manufacturing challenges via powder metallurgy.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this study, a non-equimolar Cu15Ni35Ti25Zr12.5Hf12.5 (at. %) alloy was successfully produced by induction melting, followed by atomization and subsequent consolidation via Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at temperatures ranging from 850 to 1100 C.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Although global equilibrium phase diagrams predict solid-state stability up to 1260 C, localized melting unexpectedly occurred during SPS at 1100 C. By combining retrospective Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulations with 2D local equilibrium heat maps, we demonstrate that this early-stage melting is not driven by macroscopic thermal gradients, but by microsegregation inherited from atomization.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This framework accounts for localized melting phenomena in rapidly solidified CCA powders containing low-melting constituents with strong negative mixing enthalpies.

title: Evaluating Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection for Identifying Unusual Galaxy Morphologies in CEERS and NGDEEP
authors: T. B. Surakan, J. S. Kartaltepe et al. (10 researchers)

slides.hook: Galaxy morphology out to zsim 6 provides insight into galaxy formation and evolution, but identifying rare or structurally complex systems is difficult due to observational limits and the scale of modern imaging surveys.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we apply AdaCLIP, a Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection (ZSAD) model built upon the Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) model and adapted using non-astronomical anomaly-detection datasets, to identify structurally unusual galaxies without galaxy-specific anomaly-detection training or morphological labels. We extract anomaly scores and 768-dimensional feature embeddings from 38,853 galaxies in the Cosmic Evolution Early Release Science (CEERS) and Next Generation Deep Extragalactic Exploratory Public (NGDEEP) surveys, and compare the resulting anomaly scores with parametric GALFIT and nonparametric statmorph measurements.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The feature embeddings reveal structure associated with galaxy morphology and observational properties, while anomaly scores show modest trends with structural measures, including asymmetry, concentration, M_{20}, and size, but weaker or less consistent trends with Sérsic index, axis ratio, smoothness, and Gini coefficient. These results highlight the potential of ZSAD as a scalable tool for identifying unusual galaxy morphologies in large astronomical imaging surveys, including those anticipated from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

title: How Well Do Decision Models Transfer to Vietnamese? An Empirical Study of Text Classification
authors: Phat Huu Ha, Nguyen Xuan Phuc et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Recent advances in specialized decision models have expanded the possibilities for zero-shot classification, yet their effectiveness on Vietnamese remains underexplored.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This study evaluates four specialized decision models across 13 classification settings spanning six task groups, examining zero-shot performance, sensitivity to label-description language, and robustness to Vietnamese linguistic variations. The evaluation considers English, Vietnamese, and bilingual label descriptions, alongside common linguistic perturbations involving teencode, typographical errors, and diacritic removal.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Under English label descriptions, JEV achieves the strongest overall performance, ranking first in 11 classification settings. The effects of label-description language vary across models and datasets, with bilingual descriptions providing no consistent improvement.

slides.content: These findings highlight the importance of label-description choices and Vietnamese orthographic variation when evaluating specialized decision models for zero-shot text classification.

title: QUIJOTE scientific results - XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
authors: F. Vansyngel, J. A. Rubino-Martin et al. (22 researchers)

slides.hook: We present an analysis of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power-spectrum level in the multipole range 30 < ell < 130, using the recent QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey (10-20GHz) in combination with Planck and WMAP data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The EE and BB power spectra are well described by a simple power-law model, with no evidence for the need of additional parameters. The best-fit slopes are α_{EE} = -3.24 pm 0.12 and α_{BB} = -3.81 pm 0.34 for |b|>20^circ, hinting toward a steepening of the BB spectrum relative to EE at the sim 1.6σ level.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The synchrotron frequency spectral indices are found to be β_s^{EE} = -3.26 pm 0.05 and β_s^{BB} = -3.25 pm 0.10 for the same cut, in agreement with earlier real-space analyses. We find no evidence for spatial variations of β_s across different Galactic latitude cuts, within current uncertainties.

slides.content: Using these results, we estimate the level of synchrotron contamination in future CMB B-mode measurements, finding an average power in the considered sky masks equivalent to r sim 0.003 at 90GHz and r sim 0.0002 at 150GHz for the relevant angular scales.

slides.content: Distance to optimality remains unobservable, while conclusions may depend on reward design, stochasticity, hyperparameters, environment selection, and simulator details. title: Pushing beyond the memory barrier in propagation algorithms with randomization
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Ricard Puig et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Performant classical tools for simulating quantum circuits are important for benchmarking and supporting upcoming quantum devices.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Pauli propagation offers promising capabilities, but deep circuits usually cause a rapid growth in the number of Pauli strings and can quickly exhaust the available memory. In this work, we introduce a randomized protocol that combines a specialized resampling schedule, merging, and a controlled amount of bias to keep the propagating Pauli sum within any prescribed memory budget.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Additional computational resources can then be spent on embarrassingly parallel repetitions that systematically improve the estimate. Building on the open-source library PauliPropagation.jl, we show that 1) increasing memory of each simulation reduces the error systematically more than outside averaging, 2) resampling just enough to apply the next gate delays variance accumulation and gives better error-per-time trade-offs than more aggressive resampling, and 3) a small, controlled bias is crucial in cutting down variance and pushing far beyond unbiased randomization.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The resulting framework can reproduce deterministic calculations while requiring several orders of magnitude less memory.

slides.hook: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential to automate heuristic design for NP-hard combinatorial optimization (CO) tasks without human intervention.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Recent methods predominantly rely on evolutionary computation (EC) frameworks, where heuristic diversification is mainly induced through EC-like operators or downstream selection, while the direction of heuristic transformation remains largely unharnessed. In this paper, we propose a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for automatic heuristic design that factorizes heuristic transformation through directional search primitives at the generation level.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Specifically, PRS operates on heuristic ideas through three complementary directions: expansion toward richer and more expressive designs, compression toward simpler and less specialized designs, and steering for fine-grained refinement, together enabling broader and more sustained exploration of diverse regions in the heuristic design space. PRS further organizes candidate exploration within a breadth-first search-based process with adaptive operator control, which ensures thorough candidate utilization and sustained exploration, and maintains strong search dynamics while preventing premature convergence.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Extensive empirical results across diverse CO tasks show that PRS consistently discovers high-quality heuristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of explicitly directional exploration design.

title: Learning infinite context windows in recurrent architectures via spatial neural computing
authors: Aleix Salvador-Pomarol, Arthur N. Montanari et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) offer linear-time scaling with sequence length while requiring only constant memory, yet they struggle to capture long-range dependencies due to vanishing gradients and limited receptive fields.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To address these limitations, we introduce a second-order recurrent model in which the standard neuron-to-neuron communication is replaced by a spatially evolving field governed by (discretized) partial differential equations. Drawing inspiration from the role of cortical waves in brain computation, this mechanism allows structured spatiotemporal patterns to serve as an implicit, high-capacity memory.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that the resulting model is equivalent to a structured infinite-order RNN in which the current state depends explicitly on its entire history of past states, yielding an effectively unbounded receptive field with a fixed number of parameters. We further derive constructive conditions to ensure marginal stability, constraining the gradient spectrum on the unit circle and thereby eliminating vanishing and exploding gradients.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Empirically, the proposed architecture outperforms other recurrent models on long-horizon benchmarks while using substantially fewer parameters, demonstrating that spatial dynamics can effectively bridge the gap between efficient inference and long-term memory.

title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
authors: Jiawen Liu, Chengli Wang et al. (11 researchers)

slides.hook: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.

slides.hook: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: ARGUS wraps 458 DNABERT-based TF binding models in a hypothesis-directed investigation loop where a planner selects evidence sources based on current uncertainty, a verifier deterministically interprets each observation, and intermediate results change the investigation path. title: CoWriter: Guiding Methodological and Synergetic Human-LLM Co-Authoring
authors: Shmuel Amar, Benjamin Lieber et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: While LLMs have transformed text generation, standard chat-and-canvas interfaces often reduce human authoring to quite passive supervision, causing review fatigue, over-reliance on AI, and the sidelining of the human role in long-form, source-grounded writing.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Prior systems typically address isolated writing phases, leaving comprehensive end-to-end human-LLM collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce CoWriter, a proactive agentic scheme that adapts expert human (co-)authoring methodologies from cognitive science to flexibly steer the entire writing workflow while actively encouraging the user to engage.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In an exploratory user study, compared to a standard LLM baseline, authors using CoWriter better expressed their perspectives and maintained a higher sense of document ownership, supported quantitatively by 2.2times more successful agent engagements. Furthermore, external reader judges rated the resulting texts higher in "human touch" qualities like storytelling and integrating unique personal experiences.

title: Observable-Level Framework for Finite-Key Security in Coherent-One-Way Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Aryan Kuntal, Utkarsh Giradkar et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Practical security analysis of Coherent-One-Way (COW) quantum key distribution requires optical-device modeling, finite experimental statistics, and security inference to be treated consistently without conflating assumptions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present a modular observable-level simulation framework organized through the pipeline θ_phys -> p -> O -> S_j(O), in which physical source, channel, receiver, and detector parameters determine detector-resolved event probabilities, a finite-block layer applies an effective dead-time treatment and generates aggregate detector counts, and interchangeable security evaluators act on the same observable record. The framework is verified against analytical optical, virtual-state, and finite-key relations and evaluated against reported experimental COW-QKD operating points.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The Kato finite-key calculation reproduces the refined experimentally reported secure-key rates most closely at intermediate distances, with deviations of -1.5% at 50 km and -10.3% at 75 km. Monitoring bright-port decoy counts agree within 0.9-2.4%, while remaining distance-dependent dark-port residual identifies the principal model-sensitive observable of the present physical description.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The framework therefore provides a common computational interface for experimental reproduction, controlled security-model comparison, model-based protocol optimization, and modular adversarial stress testing in COW-QKD.

title: How 'Foundational' Are Current Molecular Foundation Models?
authors: Francesca Grisoni

slides.hook: Large-scale models have permeated the molecular sciences, yet what makes a model 'foundational' in this domain remains poorly defined.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This paper proposes three testable criteria for assessing the foundational nature of molecular models: (i) generality across molecular entities, properties, and tasks; (ii) transferability to new applications with no or minimal task-specific retraining; and (iii) generalization beyond the training distribution. Applying these criteria to the state of the art reveals promising progress, particularly visible in biomolecular structure prediction and machine-learned interatomic potentials, although none of the approaches examined fully satisfies all three.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Success is concentrated in domains where target properties are consistently defined and training data are abundant, with low label noise relative to physically meaningful variation. More broadly, progress in the molecular sciences appears to depend less on model scale alone than on the quality and structure of available data, as well as the incorporation of prior knowledge into models, prediction tasks, or downstream applications.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work shifts the notion of a molecular foundation model from a descriptive label to a testable hypothesis, offering a framework for assessing current models and guiding future developments.

title: MerKurio: sequence extraction and annotation based on matching k-mers
authors: Lukas Schönmann, Heinz Himmelbauer et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: K-mers, short subsequences of length k, play an important role in computational analyses using biological sequence data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: A critical downstream processing step involves getting back to the source sequences of selected k-mers for further analysis or validation. Here, we present MerKurio, a high-performance command line tool written in Rust with two main functionalities: 1) extracting sequence records from FASTA/FASTQ files using k-mers and 2) annotating or filtering aligned sequences in SAM/BAM files with k-mer tags.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Humans address this challenge by using mental world models that "imagine" the shape and material properties from partial observations, which enables them to predict how actions affect future states. title: CancerZigZag: Iterative Seed-Anchored Diffusion for Generative Modeling of Single-Cell State Transitions
authors: Johannes Schlüter & Alexander Schönhuth

slides.hook: Single-cell cancer datasets are predominantly cross-sectional and rarely provide paired or longitudinal observations linking individual healthy-like cells to tumor-associated states.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce CancerZigZag, a seed-initialized diffusion-based framework for exploratory generation of tumor-associated single-cell candidate clouds from unpaired epithelial cell populations. For each cancer context, a diffusion model is trained exclusively on tumor-derived epithelial cells and applied through repeated partial latent-space perturbation and reverse diffusion to held-out healthy-like seeds, generating stochastic candidate clouds without paired measurements or classifier guidance.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We applied CancerZigZag to colorectal, breast, lung, and renal cell carcinoma contexts and explored parameter landscapes defined by perturbation depth and the number of ZigZag cycles. Across the reported operating configurations, candidate clouds contained outputs classified toward held-out tumor-derived reference populations for each evaluated seed.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Instead, it provides a reference-informed framework for exploring tumor-associated candidate distributions from unpaired healthy-like seeds and quantifying the context-dependent relationship between tumor-associated displacement and residual seed dependence.

title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films
authors: Yidi Liu, Yaoju Tarn et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO_4 (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. A direct correlation between the azimuthal-angle-dependent two-step transition and step-terrace orientation establishes this connection, further supported by atomic-scale visualization of structurally disrupted regions at step terraces.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Modeling the films as pristine (weak-link) regions with higher (lower) transition temperature reproduces essential features of the two-step transition using both a simple model and finite-element simulations. Transport measurements further reveal a strong dependence of transition characteristics - and even the occurrence of superconductivity itself - on average terrace width.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results identify step-induced weak links as the microscopic origin of two-step transitions in bilayer nickelate films, providing a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative transport, and a route to superconducting devices.

title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
authors: Md Khalid Syfullah & Alvi Ataur Khalil

slides.hook: As quantum computing moves from the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era toward early fault-tolerant quantum computing (EFTQC), quantum-enhanced AI is shifting from a conceptual idea to experimental research.

slides.content: Quantum components are expected to extend the capabilities of existing AI systems, yet it remains unclear how such components will help within large multimodal models. title: Early panchromatic spectra reveal helium in the thermonuclear supernova 2024kce
authors: Abigail Polin, Dillon Hasenour et al. (29 researchers)

slides.hook: Faint Type I supernovae blur the boundaries between spectroscopic classes, obscuring their progenitors and explosion mechanisms.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: One proposed origin is a double detonation, in which ignition of an accreted helium shell triggers the explosion of a carbon oxygen white dwarf. title: Bidirectional Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation of Quantum Circuits
authors: Luis Paulo Santos & Thomas Bashford-Rogers

slides.hook: We propose an approximate classical algorithm for estimating quantum circuits' transition amplitudes, langle Ψ_f | hat{U} | Ψ_0 rangle, based on Monte Carlo sums over bidirectionally sampled Feynman paths.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: The algorithm generates Feynman paths, i.e., sequences of intermediate computational basis states, by combining information from random walks initiated at both the input and output states, Ψ_0 and Ψ_f, respectively. title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
authors: Sachin Gupta

slides.hook: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

slides.hook: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed.

title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
authors: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We propose a new method for proving L^2 and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance.

slides.content: We first establish the L^2 logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. title: Correlation-Guided Flow Matching with Annealed Masking for Spatial Transcriptomics Generation
authors: Yupei Zhang, Hao Chen et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression profiling but remains expensive, motivating the prediction of ST from histology images.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Generative models have emerged as a mainstream paradigm for ST prediction due to their ability to model the conditional distribution of gene expression and capture its inherent stochasticity. However, these methods typically treat genes as independent prediction targets and overlook the intrinsic gene-gene interactions in biological systems, which limits their ability to preserve biologically meaningful co-expression patterns.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We argue that gene-gene interactions, which reflect shared pathways and regulatory mechanisms, are essential for generating numerically accurate and biologically coherent ST profiles. In this paper, we propose CorrFlow, a correlation-guided flow matching framework for histology-to-ST prediction that explicitly models gene-gene dependencies through two complementary mechanisms.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Extensive experiments across 12 datasets show that CorrFlow achieves the best average PCC and HPCC among evaluated methods, leading to more biologically coherent ST predictions.

title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
authors: Mohammad Talaei, Mohammad Goudarzi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Soil moisture and temperature govern plant-water availability and microbial activity, making them key indicators for evaluating land-restoration efforts on degraded landscapes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the physical and data-driven models normally used to forecast them both need information that a newly instrumented restoration site does not yet have: hydraulic parameters for the former and months of per-site training data for the latter. We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and enclosure temperature at seven lead times from 1 h to 168 h.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using gap-aware rolling-origin evaluation across sensors, we find that TimesFM beats the best rule-based statistical forecasting baselines (persistence, seasonal-naive, or 7-day climatology) by 21-76% at sub-daily lead times but loses by 6-79% beyond a day, a pattern explained by a diurnal-alignment mechanism that holds for both soil-moisture depths and temperature. A CatBoost baseline trained walk-forward on the same origins with full history and weather covariates never wins overall, and we show that its weakness is partly a cold-start effect specific to short deployments.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results highlight a practical trade-off between zero-shot forecasting capability, predictive performance, and computational efficiency.

title: Quantum Optimisation for Protein-Protein Interaction Network Alignment
authors: Merle Stahl, Robert J. Banks et al. (7 researchers)

slides.hook: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network alignment combines topological and sequence information to identify conserved modules across species, but global alignment remains challenging: heuristics sacrifice optimality, while exact methods lack scalability.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We model the alignment as a weighted maximum common induced subgraph problem and reformulate it through the modular product graph to a minimum-weight vertex cover on the complement, with node weights carrying sequence similarity. To solve this problem, we develop a hybrid framework combining kernelisation, branch-and-bound, and seven Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) formulations.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: These formulations differ in how the cover constraints are enforced, from penalty terms in the cost Hamiltonian to mixers confined to the feasible subspace. For single round QAOA, we derive closed-form expressions for the expected cost of four circulant mixer variants, enabling performance characterisation without circuit simulation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Together, these results highlight the potential of quantum optimisation for PPI network alignment and the resource trade-offs that will shape its scalability as quantum hardware matures.

slides.hook: Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.

title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
authors: Sridevi Kuriyattil, Johannes Kombe et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.

title: REMBGO for Evaluation-Limited Optimization: CEC2022 Benchmarking and EAF-STATCOM Generalization
authors: Vikram Chekuri, Narapareddy Ramarao et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Metaheuristic comparisons are often reported at evaluation budgets far larger than an expensive engineering simulation can afford.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This paper presents REMBGO, an evaluation-budget-aware refinement of EMBGO. Its contribution is not any single operator: it is the integration of population preservation, scale-normalized exploration and recovery mechanisms whose parent-relative benefit is concentrated under restricted function-evaluation budgets.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: REMBGO is evaluated on CEC2022 at a primary, application-aligned budget of 1040 function evaluations, with a surrounding budget ladder reported descriptively to characterise budget dependence rather than as a family of controlled hypotheses. A component-removal study finds no individual mechanism whose removal survives multiplicity correction, consistent with an integrated rather than a single-operator contribution.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: REMBGO is therefore presented as a resource-aware refinement whose benefit must be stated together with the evaluation budget, not as a universally superior optimizer.

title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
authors: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Unai Zulaika et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Accuracy on medical examinations is common evidence offered for the clinical use of language models, yet a health system that intends to run an open model on its own hardware needs to know considerably more: whether the model recognizes when it is likely to be wrong, whether medical fine-tuning improves this ability, whether its correct answers rest on sound clinical reasoning, or whether it actually uses the images it is given.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We examine these questions for four open models of 8 to 27 billion parameters on the Spanish MIR residency examination, scoring 1,552 questions from eight editions under the exam's own rules. Answering every question, the three larger models would rank among roughly the first 600 to 3,000 candidates, with 41 to 43 specialties still open to them.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Abstention, however, never pays, because even their least confident answers are right more often than the 25% break-even. Medical fine-tuning reduced overconfidence at the cost of accuracy, without improving how well confidence separates right from wrong answers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Moreover, 13-38% of correct answers rejected a distractor for a clinically unsound reason that confidence did not reflect, and removing or swapping the provided contextual images left accuracy unchanged.

slides.hook: A new adaptive restart rule for Genetic Algorithms (GAs) is considered.

title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Jinya Sakurai, Xun Xu et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Masked diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but their efficiency depends on which predictions are committed.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Learned unmasking policies improve the speed--accuracy trade-off, yet differ in supervision, inputs, and capacity, obscuring which choices matter. We view supervised policies as distilling a decoding procedure through a teacher and examine independently what the teacher labels as committable, on which states the policy imitates it, what the policy observes, and how much the number of function evaluations (NFE) must decrease to offset policy overhead.

title: A Semantic Model of Genetic Evidence: A Step Toward Bridging the Basic-Science-Clinic Gap
authors: Michael Bouzinier & Dmitry Etin

slides.hook: Scientific and clinical decision-making depends on evidence from the primary literature, but existing standards for representing that evidence (FHIR Evidence, ECO, SEPIO, and the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Standards) are oriented toward clinical-trial workflows, evidence codes, or single-variant assertions, and do not capture the fine-grained, domain-specific structure of claims in basic and pre-clinical research.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce a semantic model for scientific evidence with three core classes, specialize it for genetics, align it structurally to FHIR Evidence with a SEPIO-anchored credibility decomposition, and attach a compact dimensional vocabulary whose conditional-activation rules are validated by a SHACL schema for the implemented constraints. Using clinical variant interpretation as the driving use case, we evaluate the model through a human-AI annotation pilot over six genetics papers, yielding 28 evidence items and 95 source-anchored assertions, with a workflow that keeps curator-authored reference annotations distinct from AI-drafted annotations.

slides.content: Using clinical variant interpretation as the driving use case, we evaluate the model through a human-AI annotation pilot over six genetics papers, yielding 28 evidence items and 95 source-anchored assertions, with a workflow that keeps curator-authored reference annotations distinct from AI-drafted annotations. Treating the pilot as a feasibility study rather than a benchmark, we argue that the model is a useful increment toward trustworthy, AI-ready infrastructure for variant interpretation: a reference data model and validation schema for representing genetic evidence.

slides.hook: Tree-based speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by verifying multiple candidate branches in parallel.

slides.content: However, in practical serving scenarios, similar requests repeatedly induce overlapping candidate branches. slides.hook: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons.

title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
authors: Buse Giledereli, Basar Temiz et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generation offers a promising route for privacy-aware biomedical data sharing, but donor-linked datasets require careful balancing of biological utility and privacy risk.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this work, we benchmark synthetic generation methods for the CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge using the donor-split OneK1K dataset, comparing scGFT, scLDM, and Cell2Sentence across statistical fidelity, downstream biological preservation, and membership inference vulnerability. Because full-transcriptome generation is computationally demanding, we focus generative modeling on highly variable genes and evaluate alternative strategies for reconstructing non-HVG expression.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our results show that non-HVG handling is a central determinant of privacy: directly copying non-HVG values leads to severe leakage, whereas Poisson-based reconstruction substantially reduces membership inference risk. We further find that scGFT and scLDM better preserve biological structure than an independent Poisson baseline, while maintaining near-random privacy profiles under appropriate configurations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings highlight the importance of evaluating synthetic single-cell data beyond marginal similarity alone, emphasizing robustness, interpretability, and privacy-conscious design choices throughout preprocessing, generation, and post-processing.

title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
authors: Yancheng Zhu & Yifan Yuan

slides.hook: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures).

slides.content: Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.

title: Dealing with low-weight errors that lead BP OSD to fail
authors: Giacomo Fregona, Matthias C. Löbl et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Belief Propagation combined with Ordered Statistics Decoding (BP OSD) is an open-source decoding tool used widely within the community due to its versatility and ease of application to Quantum Low Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the degeneracy of quantum codes has been observed to degrade the performance of BP OSD, particularly leading to error floors for low physical error rates. Here, we investigate the low-weight error configurations responsible for such failures in Bivariate Bicycle codes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that, at code capacity, BP OSD fails on errors whose weight is significantly smaller than d/2, arising from global symmetries of the decoding graph that prevent the convergence of parallel BP. Furthermore, our analysis reveals new pitfalls that can arise when analysing the performance of BP OSD in the rare events regime, such as loss of ergodicity in splitting methods and numerical instabilities in the decoder.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We show how to mitigate these failure mechanisms by modifying the BP update rules and the decoder implementation, leading to substantial improvement in logical error rate.
